data.title: Finding Peter Putnam
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了1987年，一名名叫彼得·普特南（Peter Putnam）的男子在路易斯安那州霍玛被醉酒司机撞死。表面上他是个清洁工，但实际上他曾是与爱因斯坦、约翰·阿奇博尔德·惠勒（John Archibald Wheeler）等著名物理学家共事的物理学家，并留下了突破性的心灵理论。尽管他的思想深度受到高度评价，他却默默无闻。作者试图揭开普特南被遗忘的原因，最终在惠勒的笔记中发现普特南曾是其学生，且对“观察者在宇宙中的角色”有深刻见解。普特南的一生充满谜团，他不仅在哲学上有巨大潜力，还成功投资累积了巨额财富，但他的故事却鲜为人知。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Peter Putnam的学术贡献及其理论的理解与传播

不同观点：
• **支持Putnam理论并赞赏其深度**：
   - iandanforth认为Putnam的理论与强化学习（RL）应该基于体内平衡（homeostasis）的观点一致，并对Putnam的思维方式表示赞赏，认为他的思想具有前瞻性。
   - golly_ned和kruffalon对Putnam的个人魅力和理论表示兴趣，并希望能阅读更多关于他的传记或深入内容。

• **质疑Putnam的表达能力和理论影响**：
   - jinlisp认为Putnam如果真的是天才，应该能够更清晰地传达他的思想，并质疑Putnam的理论对后世的实际影响，指出Putnam可能只是触及到了某个领域而未深入。
   - demaga同样质疑Putnam的天才身份，认为他的作品难以理解，并以编程语言的难懂性作比喻，表示不会去阅读Putnam的作品。

• **对Putnam理论的进一步探讨和兴趣**：
   - nissomon对Putnam的研究是否被现代专家关注表示好奇，并希望了解更多关于Putnam研究的后续影响。
   - khakimov表示在阅读Putnam的作品后对其人其事有了更深的了解，并提供了相关链接供他人参考。

• **对文章写作风格和内容安排的评价**：
   - noplynon对文章的写作风格不满，认为文章进入主题太慢，表达了对文章结构的不满。
   - morninglight则对文章整体评价不高，认为Putnam的故事不如其他被遗忘的天才故事（如Vivian Maier）那样有吸引力。

补充讨论：
• Putnam的理论涉及自我重复（repetition）作为内在目标，并与细胞自动机、体内平衡、固定点理论和错误恢复等概念相关联。
• 讨论中有人提到Hilary Putnam，暗示对Putnam家族的学术背景有所混淆，并澄清了两者并无直接关系。
• 一些评论者如fumeux_fume和myst提供了扩展阅读的建议或链接，旨在帮助他人更好地理解Putnam的理论和背景。

争议焦点：
• Putnam的理论是否真正具有创新性和影响力，还是仅仅停留在概念层面而未被深入发展。
• Putnam的作品难以理解，是否影响其作为天才的评价及其学术贡献的传播。

he neighborhood was quiet. There was a chill in the air. The scent of Spanish moss hung from the cypress trees. Plumes of white smoke rose from the burning cane fields and stretched across the skies of Terrebonne Parish. The man swung a long leg over a bicycle frame and pedaled off down the street.

It was 1987 in Houma, Louisiana, and he was headed to the Department of Transportation, where he was working the night shift, sweeping floors and cleaning toilets. He was just picking up speed when a car came barreling toward him with a drunken swerve.
A screech shot down the corridor of East Main Street, echoed through the vacant lots, and rang out over the Bayou.
Then silence.

The 60-year-old man lying on the street, as far as anyone knew, was just a janitor hit by a drunk driver. There was no mention of it on the local news, no obituary in the morning paper. His name might have been Anonymous. But it wasn’t.
How could this genius just vanish into obscurity?
His name was Peter Putnam. He was a physicist who’d hung out with Albert Einstein, John Archibald Wheeler, and Niels Bohr, and two blocks from the crash, in his run-down apartment, where his partner, Claude, was startled by a screech, were thousands of typed pages containing a groundbreaking new theory of the mind.
“Only two or three times in my life have I met thinkers with insights so far reaching, a breadth of vision so great, and a mind so keen as Putnam’s,” Wheeler said in 1991. And Wheeler, who coined the terms “black hole” and “wormhole,” had worked alongside some of the greatest minds in science.
ADVERTISEMENT

Log in
or
Join now
.
Robert Works Fuller, a physicist and former president of Oberlin College, who worked closely with Putnam in the 1960s, told me in 2012, “Putnam really should be regarded as one of the great philosophers of the 20th century. Yet he’s completely unknown.”
That word—
unknown
—it came to haunt me as I spent the next 12 years trying to find out why.
The American Philosophical Society
Library in Philadelphia, with its marbled floors and chandeliered ceilings, is home to millions of rare books and manuscripts, including John Wheeler’s notebooks. I was there in 2012, fresh off writing a physics book that had left me with nagging questions about the strange relationship between observer and observed. Physics seemed to suggest that observers play some role in the nature of reality, yet who or what an observer is remained a stubborn mystery.
ADVERTISEMENT
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
Wheeler, who made key contributions to nuclear physics, general relativity, and quantum gravity, had thought more about the observer’s role in the universe than anyone—if there was a clue to that mystery anywhere, I was convinced it was somewhere in his papers. That’s when I turned over a mylar overhead, the kind people used to lay on projectors, with the titles of two talks, as if given back-to-back at the same unnamed event:
Wheeler: From Reality to Consciousness
Putnam: From Consciousness to Reality
Putnam, it seemed, had been one of Wheeler’s students, whose opinion Wheeler held in exceptionally high regard. That was odd, because Wheeler’s students were known for becoming physics superstars, earning fame, prestige, and Nobel Prizes: Richard Feynman, Hugh Everett, and Kip Thorne.

Join now
.
Back home, a Google search yielded images of a very muscly, very orange man wearing a very small speedo. This, it turned out, was the wrong Peter Putnam. Eventually, I stumbled on a 1991 article in the
Princeton Alumni Weekly
newsletter called “Brilliant Enigma.” “Except for the barest outline,” the article read, “Putnam’s life is ‘veiled,’ in the words of Putnam’s lifelong friend and mentor, John Archibald Wheeler.”
THE SCHOLAR:
Peter Putnam catches up with the news while studying at the University of Leiden in 1956. Putnam spent a semester in the Netherlands working as an assistant to physicist John Archibald Wheeler.
Credit: John Archibald Wheeler, courtesy of Alison Lahnston.
A quick search of old newspaper archives turned up an intriguing article from the
Associated Press
, published six years after Putnam’s death. “Peter Putnam lived in a remote bayou town in Louisiana, worked as a night watchman on a swing bridge [and] wrote philosophical essays,” the article said. “He also tripled the family fortune to about $40 million by investing successfully in risky stock ventures.”
The questions kept piling up.
Forty million dollars?

data.title: 2025 ARRL Field Day
data.author: rookderby
data.article_summary: ARRL Field Day是北美一年一度的最大业余无线电活动，于每年六月的第四个周末举行。2025年的活动时间为6月28-29日。超过31,000名无线电爱好者会在临时地点设立电台，展示无线电技术及其在公共服务和应急准备中的作用。活动目标是在多个频段上尽可能多地联络其他电台，并提高在非正常条件下的操作技能。Field Day面向ARRL/RAC覆盖区域的业余无线电爱好者，也欢迎公众参与和了解。参与者可通过Field Day Locator查找附近活动地点，并在社交媒体上使用#ARRLFD标签分享经验。尽管不是竞赛，完整结果将刊登在12月的《QST》杂志上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：业余无线电爱好者对ARRL Field Day活动的不同经历和观点

不同观点：
• [怀旧与个人经历] nlh分享了自己1990年首次获得业余无线电执照并参加Field Day的经历，强调了当时等待执照到来的紧张心情以及首次参与活动的难忘体验。他提到自己在活动中升级技能，并回忆了与俱乐部成员一起操作HF设备的细节。

• [竞赛精神与团队合作] drmpeg讲述了在1990年代初期与San Jose State无线电俱乐部的成员合作参加Field Day的经历。这些成员非常重视比赛，并邀请drmpeg及其朋友加入以提高比赛成绩。他们成功地在两年内进入了前10名，显示了团队对成绩的重视。

• [邀请与实时信息] rookderby简单提醒大家2025年ARRL Field Day的到来，鼓励人们参与活动。

• [竞赛偏好与操作建议] howard941表达了对Field Day的喜爱，尤其是对于喜欢深夜操作和户外架设电台的人。他还提到Field Day是他第二喜欢的竞赛，仅次于十一月CW Sweepstakes。

• [参与方式与资源分享] agent86提供了ESPN HAM Radio俱乐部的信息，并分享了他们通过YouTube直播Field Day活动的链接，鼓励感兴趣的人观看并与操作者互动。

• [设备与环境限制] b00ty4breakfast提到由于天气原因，无法架设天线参与活动，表现出对错过活动的无奈。

• [新手参与与建议] ericye16询问没有HF电台的情况下如何参与Field Day，特别是住在小公寓里的情况，显示出新手对参与活动的渴望和实际困难。

补充讨论：
• sciencesama分享了自己在Field Day中成功进行了两次联系的积极体验，强调了活动的趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 不同参与者对Field Day的重视程度不同，有些人将其视为社交和学习的机会，而另一些人则更注重竞赛成绩。
• 新手在参与Field Day时面临的实际困难，如设备和居住环境的限制，如何有效解决这些问题以促进更多人参与活动。

Field Day Rules
. Other Field Day resources are available below.
Follow ARRL Field Day preparations with the news and stories below (stories will be added as they are available, so check back).
New to Field Day? START HERE!
Field Day is ham radio's open house.
Every June, more than 31,000 hams throughout North America set up temporary transmitting stations in public places to demonstrate ham radio's science, skill and service to our communities and our nation. It combines public service, emergency preparedness, community outreach, and technical skills all in a single event. Field Day has been an annual event since 1933, and remains the most popular event in ham radio.
We welcome the public to come learn more about ham radio! Use our
Field Day Locator
to search for a Field Day site near you.
Field Day on Social Media!
Click
below to join the ARRL Field Day Facebook Group.
Share your plans, tips and tricks to a successful Field Day. When posting content from Field Day,
use hashtag #ARRLFD
on all social media to receive 100 bonus points!
https://www.facebook.com/groups/arrlfd/
Rules and Resources
Objective
To contact as many stations as possible on the 160-, 80-, 40-, 20-,15- and 10-Meter HF bands, as well as all bands 50 MHz and above, and to learn to operate in abnormal situations in less than optimal conditions.
Field Day is open to all amateurs in the areas covered by the ARRL/RAC Field Organizations and countries within IARU Region 2. DX stations residing in other regions may be contacted for credit, but are not eligible to submit entries.
Each claimed contact must include contemporaneous direct initiation by the operator on both sides of the contact. Initiation of a contact may be either locally or by remote.
Dates (Always the 4th Weekend in June)
Field Day is always the fourth full weekend of June, beginning at 1800 UTC Saturday and running through 2059 UTC Sunday.
Field Day 2025 is June 28 - 29.
Bands and modes
Bands: 160-, 80-, 40-, 20-,15- and 10-Meter HF bands, as well as all bands 50 MHz and above,
Any mode supporting the Field Day exchange is allowed.
Field Day Entry/Results Submission Deadline
Entries must be postmarked or submitted via web app at
field-day.arrl.org/fdentry.php
by Tuesday, July 29, 2025
.
Late entries cannot be accepted.
To see if your entry has been received see
field-day.arrl.org/fdentriesrcvd.php
. If your entry is missing any required document or bonus point proof, the status will be listed as "pending."  Participants may upload additional documentation to the entry for up to 30 days after the entry deadline.
-----------
To submit your Field Day results, see the Field Day Packet (complete) section 8 (REPORTING) for web app and mail options.
Terms Of Entry
- Entrants agree to be bound by the provisions and intent of ARRL contest rules.
- Entrants agree to be bound by the regulations of their national licensing authority.
- Entrants agree to be bound by the decisions of the ARRL Awards Committee.
- Entry contents used to determine final score and awards will be available to the public.
- All entries become the property of the ARRL.
Contact Information
For Field Day information contact ARRL:
fdinfo@arrl.org
or (860) 594-0232.
Awards
Field Day is not a contest:
-  no logs are required
- dupe sheets must be submitted
- no certificates are awarded
- full results appear in the December issue of
QST
magazine.

data.title: Community Is Motivation on Tap
data.author: lunw
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了社群对个人动机的重要性。作者通过对比自己在《星际争霸》和《Brawl Stars》中的经历，说明拥有一个共同目标的社群可以显著增强动机，而独自工作则容易失去动力。文章提出了两个关键机制：寻求认同（如责任伙伴和良性竞争）和“所见即所有”偏见（社群让目标信息持续可见）。作者建议主动加入或创建有助于实现个人目标的社群，并远离产生负面影响的社群，以保持积极的动力。

不同观点：

44373562.article_content:
Community is Motivation on Tap
A good community can have tremendous influence on one’s motivation. I never appreciated this fact enough so I wanted to write about it here.
Looking at successful athletes, founders, musicians, game speedrunners, or overachievers in any area, they seem to have unlimited motivation to do loads of tedious work or practice. One might say they are interested in the work itself, but how inherently interesting can beating super mario 1ms faster be? The work of a founder might look stimulating on the surface, but the amount of monotony that has to be tolerated to make ends meet is daunting. How do these people carry through with this while I still struggle to get my laundry done?
My Story
I believe most highly motivated people have a good community working towards the same goals. A community can multiply your motivation while people working alone run out of steam easily.
My experience with StarCraft resonates with this. I have a long held passion for this game, but the game (along with the entire RTS genre) is dwindling and few of my peers even know of it. I’ve made practice plans but never ended up putting in consistent effort. It’s hard to be entirely self-motivated, especially as life priorities shift every other week.
Is contrast, I poured hundreds of hours playing, studying meta, watching pro plays into Brawl Stars, a completely brainrotting game whose gameplay itself I didn’t even enjoy a single bit. Yet I was hard grinding the game, just because I happened to have a few friends sweating this game too.
I enjoyed StarCraft a lot more, yet I was far more motivated for BrawlStars. I wonder if this powerful source of motivation can be harnessed to achieve greater things.
The Mechanics of Motivating Communities
The ideas mentioned here may sound intuitive, but I think a clear understanding of the underlying mechanics of motivation helps me come up with reasonable action plans without conducting extensive tests.
Approval Seeking.
It’s in our genes to seek approval. Well-known terms like
accountability partner
or
productive competition
are in fact describing the mechanics of our approval seeking tendencies boosting productivity. With accountability partners, we’re motivated to stick to our promises so as not to let them down. With productive competition, everyone within the community is motivated to get better. A good community helps us turn our approval seeking tendency into motivation.
WYSIATI Bias.
What you see is all there is. Another name for this is
availability bias
: when making decisions, our minds primarily deal with readily available information and ignore information that we can’t easily retrieve. As we spend more time with a community centered around some topic, we are exposed to lots of information on it. This biases our day-to-day decision making towards that goal. For example, when I decide how to spend my afternoon, I’m biased towards hopping on BrawlStars since that’s at the top of my head. Tasks that I don’t think about often, like doing laundry, are harder to surface. A community is a great way to provide a constant stream of relevant information to make the goal fresh on your mind.
Apart from these two reasons, a productive community also helps make your work or practice more efficient (learning from experts, avoiding tunnel vision, etc.) which yields more progress, which is the true goal of acquiring higher motivation.
Actionable Advice
Be
proactive
in joining productive communities or make your own, on the topics you want to work on.
You don’t have to let your existing communities/circles dictate what you do.
Be part of multiple communities, each for a goal you want motivation for.
Also means you should leave counterproductive communities as they motivates you on “bad” things.

data.title: Tennis Scorigami
data.author: jlarks32
data.article_summary: 自1968年以来的57年间，尽管进行了大量网球比赛，但仍有一些比分组合从未出现过。这个项目旨在追踪和发现这些缺失的比分线。在所有可能的比分中，只有一部分曾在比赛中出现，其余的则尚未发生。项目提供互动方式，供用户探索哪些具体比分组合至今未在比赛中出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对网站功能、设计及内容的不同看法和体验

不同观点：
• [pimlottc] 认为自动轮播的框得分（box scores）更新让人困扰，特别是在移动端下滑后无法轻易停止或查看，尽管最终发现可以手动控制，但过程并不直观。

• [jlarks32] 则关注网站的`Explore`页面，认为其视觉效果有趣，但提到自己第一次访问该页面的跳出率较高，暗示内容或体验未达预期。

• [jedberg] 通过快速浏览发现，一些比分缺失是因为比赛结果在两局中出现极端不平衡的情况（如6-0和0-6），这种情况极为罕见，因此合乎逻辑。

• [npinsker] 对足球Scorigami（稀有比分组合）表示欣赏，认为其背后有故事性，并能从不同角度欣赏足球。不过，该用户对当前网站的具体数字不太感兴趣，但称赞网站设计美观。

• [ben0x539] 被网站logo的鼠标互动效果吸引，以至于尚未深入了解网站内容，显示出对设计细节的关注。

• [yzydserd] 总结了在女子3盘比赛和男子5盘比赛中的未出现比分组合，并指出巨大的用户界面（UI）增加了使用的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• 用户对自动轮播功能和比分显示的实用性存在争议，特别是移动端体验不佳。
• 网站的视觉设计和互动效果（如鼠标效果）得到了部分用户的赞赏，但内容和功能的使用体验存在分歧。
• 对Scorigami比分背后的故事性和趣味性有正面评价，但也有用户对具体比分数据缺乏兴趣。
• 讨论中还涉及到比赛结果的统计分析，特别是未出现比分组合的稀有性。

data.title: Improving River Simulation
data.author: Hooke
data.article_summary: 文章描述了在将旧区域绘图功能转换为新的全局上下文过程中，对河流流量追踪方法的改进。以前，程序仅存储每年一月和七月的河流流量，并通过插值估算其他月份的数据。然而，这种方法不够准确，因为河流流量不仅取决于本地气候，还受水源区域的气候影响。为解决此问题，作者更新了程序，使其为每个全球格点计算并存储全年十二个月的河流流量，并逐月将流量信息传递到下游格点。这使得河流流量的季节性变化能够更准确地呈现。文章通过几个例子展示了不同河流在各种气候条件下的流量变化，强调了改进后的系统能更真实地模拟河流在不同月份的动态变化。最终目标是让河流在区域地图上随月份动态显示大小变化，增强模拟的真实性。

44382419.article_content:
I'm continuing with the process of converting the old region-drawing functions into the new globular context, and refactoring and improving them where possible.
While doing this I decided that the old way of tracking river flow wasn't accurate enough. At the moment, UW stores the January and July temperature and rainfall for every point on the global map. When needed, it can calculate the temperature and rainfall for other months by extrapolating them from that stored information (along with other relevant information such as the planet's obliquity, eccentricity, and so on). So far I've been doing the same thing with river flow: for every global cell, the program stores how much water is flowing in January and in July. The problem is that it's not possible to extrapolate the information for the other months from this information. This is because river flow is determined by more than just information about that point on the map. The water comes from elsewhere, and quite different climactic conditions might prevail in those other places. So we can't say (for example) that because there's less rain in March than in October there should be less river flow, because perhaps that isn't true of the place where most of the water is coming from.
So I've updated the program to track and store river flow for all twelve months. When the rivers are calculated, it goes through every cell on the globe and calculates how much water will be flowing for every month, and then adds that, month by month, to every downstream cell from that point. This means that the variation in flow can be shown quite accurately.
Here, for example, is a world with a very long river that travels through mostly desert and tundra:
(I've removed the clouds so it's easier to see.)
The information in the graphs to the top right are for a point on this river roughly in the middle of the image, where it passes through a pretty cold desert. There's significant variation in temperature, and no precipitation at all, but the river has a roughly constant flow throughout the year because its sources, far to the north, are in places with fairly even rainfall throughout the year.
Now compare this image:
You can see another large river which joins the first one near its southernmost point, in a darker area that indicates extensive wetlands. This river has its sources further south in the tundra and arctic mountains to the bottom right of the image. The graphs here are for a point on this new river near where it joins the first one. The temperatures and rainfall are similar to the previous one, but here you can see extreme variation in river flow: none at all for much of the year, and then a deluge in the brief summer as the snow melts in the sources of the river far to the southeast.
And, finally, we have this image:
This shows information for a point on the river near its mouth. Here, there is a bit more rainfall (not much!), but you can see that the variation in flow of the river follows an opposite pattern. For most of the year the river is moderately sized. This is the same flow that we saw in the first image. Then in the summer the river floods extensively, thanks to the meltwater coming from the second river that joined this one.
Since UW now displays
variation in the seasons
, the plan is that the sizes of rivers at the regional level will be shown dynamically, so you can see them swell and shrink as you move from month to month. Now that the program is storing flow information for every month, rivers like the one above should show this kind of variation in a way that adds a bit of believability to the simulation.

Wayback 是一个实验性的 X 兼容层，旨在通过 Wayland 组件运行完整的 X 桌面环境。它作为一个基础合成器，提供足够的 Wayland 功能以支持一个完整的 Xwayland 服务器，目标是最终在 Alpine 系统中取代经典的 X.org 服务器，以减少对 X 应用程序的维护负担。当前 Wayback 处于实验阶段，存在许多错误和重大变化，鼓励开发者通过提交拉取请求来修复错误而不是仅报告错误。

**主要信息：**
- 项目名称：Wayback
- 功能：X 兼容层，运行 X 桌面环境
- 目标：取代 Alpine 中的 X.org 服务器
- 状态：实验阶段，存在错误
- 依赖：wayland、xkbcommon、wlroots 等
- 许可证：MIT
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Wayback项目及其与X.org、XWayland等的比较和应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• bandrami认为，Wayback项目本应更早推出，类似于Pipewire替代PulseAudio和JACK的方式，直接插入替代现有系统。
• resoluteteeth指出，Wayback可能更适合那些希望继续使用X11环境的人，而不是去维护或分叉Xorg服务器。
• ajb提出疑问，询问在Alpine这种通常用于服务器的操作系统上运行GUI应用程序的实际用例，并质疑是否有人将其用于诸如信息亭（kiosks）之类的场景。

补充讨论：
• thdhhghgbhy问了一个基础问题，即Wayback与XWayland之间的区别，nobody9999引用README文件解释Wayback是一个实验性的X兼容层，允许使用Wayland组件运行完整的X桌面环境，它本质上是一个提供足够Wayland功能以支持完整Xwayland服务器的复合器。
• 争议的焦点似乎在于Wayback项目的实际需求和应用场景，特别是在Alpine这种操作系统中运行GUI应用程序的合理性。

总结：讨论围绕Wayback项目的定位、替代传统X系统的合理性以及其与XWayland的区别展开，同时对Alpine操作系统中的GUI应用场景提出了疑问。

wayback
Wayback is an experimental X compatibility layer which allows for running
full X desktop environments using Wayland components.  It is essentially
a stub compositor which provides just enough Wayland capabilities to host
a rootful Xwayland server.
It is intended to eventually replace the classic X.org server in Alpine,
thus reducing maintenance burden of X applications in Alpine, but a lot
of work needs to be done first.
Wayback is an experimental state: expect breaking changes, and lots of
bugs.  Please submit pull requests fixing bugs instead of bug reports
if you are able.
Installation
Dependencies:
wayland (wayland-server, wayland-client, wayland-cursor, wayland-egl)
wayland-protocol >=1.14
xkbcommon
wlroots-0.19
Building:
meson setup _build
cd _build
meson compile
Installing:
meson install

data.title: Sequence and first differences together list all positive numbers exactly once
data.author: andersource
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了整数数列OEIS中的序列A005228及其相关性质。该序列与它的首次差值序列A030124共同包含所有正整数且每个正整数只出现一次。序列从1开始，后续项通过前一项加上一个尚未出现在序列中的最小正整数生成。文章还提供了生成该序列的Maple和Mathematica代码示例，并引用了相关文献和研究。该序列由Douglas Hofstadter引入，并在其著作《哥德尔、艾舍尔、巴赫》中讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于序列A035313及其相关数学概念的讨论

不同观点：
• OscarCunningham提出了一个数学问题，询问是否存在一种序列，使得该序列及其所有差值包含每个正整数一次，并提供了一个示例序列，最终指向OEIS链接A035313。
• 8organicbits赞赏OEIS作为一个优秀的参考工具，分享了自己在软件开发中利用OEIS找到闭式解的经验，从而提高了生产力。
• Kleiba提出一个编程练习，要求编写一个函数来判断一个整数是否属于该序列，且不允许预存序列并仅进行查找。
• Cluckindan引入了另一个序列A086714，并试图解释其与波形叠加和伪随机性之间的关系，但内容较为专业和抽象。

补充讨论：
• Vishnugupta表示对cluckindan的解释感到困惑，请求进一步的说明。
• Aardwolf对序列的命名提出疑问，认为可能应被称为"Hofstadter's sequence"，并提到序列A030124中对该序列的引用。
• HocusLocus用比喻"even and odd on steroids"来形容该序列的复杂性，但没有提供具体的技术细节。

争议焦点：
• Cluckindan的解释较为专业，涉及波形干扰和伪随机性，可能不易理解，导致vishnugupta请求澄清。
• Aardwolf对序列命名方式提出质疑，但未展开详细讨论。

data.title: Magnetic Tape Storage Technology: usage, history, and future outlook
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：磁带存储技术的现状、发展及其替代方案

不同观点：
• **dale_glass**：认为现代磁带驱动器通过拉伸磁带以校准轨道，这种技术对于应对温度和湿度等现实环境影响是必要的，特别是随着存储密度的增加。

• **qurashee**：提到微软的Project Silica项目，正在研究替代磁带存储的未来技术，暗示磁带存储可能逐渐被新技术取代。

• **marklar423**：分享了其公司几年前将大量数据从磁带迁移走的经验，指出磁带读取速度慢、无法随机访问是主要问题，尽管磁带本身可靠且耐用。

• **jgalt212**：认为拥有并运营一个磁带库是其业务成功的标志，显示了对磁带存储技术的积极看法，尤其是对于大规模数据存储。

• **johnklos**：反驳所谓“磁带已死”的观点，认为那些持此观点的人通常没有实际使用过磁带。他强调磁带在长期存档和可靠性方面的优势。

• **netbioserror**：提出是否可以重新考虑软盘作为长期存档介质的可能性，并对软盘的稳定性和物理设计提出了疑问，暗示软盘可能有改进空间。

补充讨论：
• **磁带技术的现实挑战**：marklar423指出磁带存储在实际应用中的局限性，如读取速度慢和无法随机访问，这些问题在数据量增长时尤为明显。

• **磁带与新技术的对比**：qurashee和johnklos的观点形成了对比，前者提到新技术（如Project Silica）可能替代磁带，而后者则坚信磁带在长期存档方面的优势。

• **软盘作为存档介质的可行性**：netbioserror提出了一个与主流存储介质不同的观点，即重新考虑软盘，虽然这在当前技术背景下显得不太实际，但引发了对存档介质多样性的思考。

争议焦点：磁带存储是否仍然具有未来发展潜力，或者是否会被新技术完全取代。

data.title: Bazzite would shut down if Fedora goes ahead with removing 32-bit
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Fedora计划取消32位支持对Bazzite项目的影响。Bazzite是一个专注于手持游戏设备的Linux发行版，其创始人Gospodnetich表示，如果Fedora取消32位支持，Bazzite将不得不关闭。这是因为Bazzite依赖于32位库来运行Steam等应用，而使用Flatpak无法满足其特殊需求，如直接启动到Gamescope会话中。Gospodnetich认为，此举不仅会影响Bazzite，还会对Fedora的公关造成损害。他建议Fedora可以考虑逐步减少32位包，而不是立即取消。同时，理想情况下，Valve应将Steam客户端转为64位以解决问题。文章最后指出，Fedora在Steam上的用户份额较低，可能不会引起Valve的重视。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Fedora是否会移除32位支持及其对Bazzite等项目的影响

不同观点：
• [em-bee] 认为Fedora不会轻易移除32位支持，特别是在Wine和Steam等应用仍需要32位支持的情况下。他提到Fedora的变更提案引起了很多反对，因此不太可能在解决问题之前移除32位支持。此外，他对于32位支持与应用程序运行之间的关系感到困惑，认为仅影响32位机器或32位模式下的运行，而非64位系统上的32位应用程序。

• [wirysbeige] 指出该提案已被撤回，但预计32位支持最终会被移除。

• [prmoustache] 认为Bazzite维护者完全有能力编译和分发32位版本的库，因此问题不在于技术能力，而在于是否愿意付出努力维护这些版本。

• [codedokode] 担心旧的32位软件和Windows应用程序（如VST插件）在Fedora上如何运行，特别是在32位支持被移除的情况下。

• [Modified3019] 认为相关文章有哗众取宠之嫌，澄清说Fedora的提案只是讨论和考虑，并未实际实施。他强调提案被撤回并正在重新修订，且Fedora不会突然移除32位支持。同时指出，Bazzite也不会因为提案而立即关闭。

• [deafpolygon] 认为其他Linux发行版仍然支持32位，Fedora只是表示不再投入精力维护，而不是禁止用户自行使用32位库。

• [charcircuit] 指出应用程序可以自行包含32位库，这不像ARM处理器直接取消对32位代码的支持。

• [dismalaf] 批评Bazzite维护者希望Fedora或Valve为他们做维护工作。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Fedora是否应继续支持32位库，特别是对于依赖这些库的应用程序（如Wine和Steam）。
• 提案的撤回和重新修订表明该问题仍在讨论中，尚未有最终决定。
• 部分评论者认为即使Fedora移除32位支持，维护者仍可以通过自行编译和分发32位库来解决问题。
• 对提案的反对声音主要集中在对现有项目和用户体验的潜在影响上。

44381265.article_content:
Bazzite would shut down if Fedora goes ahead with removing 32-bit
By
Liam Dawe
-
25 Jun 2025 at 9:24 am UTC
37 comments
Last updated: 25 Jun 2025 at 9:26 am UTC
More to think on for the Fedora Linux change proposal to drop 32-bit support - as the popular Bazzite would have to shut down. Note: read the
previous GamingOnLinux article first
to get up to speed on what's going on.
As a major update on all this the creator of Bazzite, Kyle Gospodnetich, jumped into the official Fedora Forum to give some of their thoughts and they didn't hold back on what it would mean for Bazzite. A distribution that has become increasingly popular for handhelds with their gaming focus.
Gospodnetich stated it pretty clearly a
post
:
As much as I’d like this change to happen, it’s too soon. This change would kill off projects like Bazzite entirely right as Fedora is starting to make major headway in the gaming space. Neal Gompa already pointed out basic use cases that would be broken even if someone built the packages Steam itself needs to function.
It’s also causing irreparable damage to Fedora from a PR standpoint. I have been inundated all day with people sharing news articles and being genuinely concerned Steam is gong to stop working on their Fedora/Bazzite machines. I would argue not only should this change be rejected, the proposal should be rescinded to limit further damage to Fedora as a project.
Perhaps open a separate one to talk about changing build architecture to build
fewer
32-bit packages?
And when pushed further Gospodnetich
stated
it again, plainly:
I’m speaking as it’s founder, if this change is actually made as it is written the best option for us is to just go ahead and disband the project.
Ouch.
For people repeatedly saying to just use the Flatpak of Steam, that wouldn't work either for the use case of projects like Bazzite and how most of their users actually use the project to be like SteamOS, where it boots into a special gamescope session for Steam Big Picture Mode - it just wouldn't work with it.
Right now, I don't believe the proposal will go through as-is for Fedora 44, it's simply too soon.
The ideal scenario would be for Valve to be convinced to bring the Steam client on Linux to 64-bit, which would solve a lot of problems for everyone. It's not all about Steam though it would also cause issues for OBS Studio game capturing, FEX for Fedora's x86 emulation on aarch64 and more.
Realistically though, as I pointed out in the initial article covering it on GamingOnLinux, Fedora's user share on Steam is low to the point Valve likely won't care until more distros do it which will delay it even further.
Article taken from
GamingOnLinux.com.

data.title: Show HN: A different kind of AI Video generation
data.author: fcpguru
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在视频编辑和生成领域中的应用，特别是关于Nvidia的工具以及如何利用AI生成结构化的视频输出。

不同观点：
• [Y_Y] 提到AI项目的命名与Nvidia有冲突，并引用了Nvidia的GitHub仓库作为例子，暗示命名上的重叠。
• [tardismechanic] 对AI的潜力感到兴奋，提出可以使用OpenAI的结构化输出功能来约束生成内容以符合JSON Schema，并转换为XML，提供了一个具体的技术路径。
• [DoctorOW] 质疑AI在此处的实际价值，认为在GUI中生成关键帧更为简单，并怀疑AI是否真正理解脚本与视频之间的关系。
• [barefootford] 分享了自己尝试让Claude生成Final Cut XML的经验，并询问当前工具的独特之处，表现出对技术细节和差异的关注。
• [echelon] 强调了编辑在自动化中的重要性，并指出在生成技术主导之前，编辑自动化是关键。提到多个初创公司正在尝试自动化时间线构建，并预测生成技术将最终颠覆非线性视频编辑器。
• [iLoveOncall] 明确区分了视频编辑和视频生成，认为该工具属于视频编辑范畴，并对工具的功能表示赞赏。
• [EGreg] 对工具的功能表示极大的兴趣，分享了自己曾计划实现类似功能的详细技术方案，并提出了关于使用Cutlass XML格式还是自定义JSON格式的疑问，同时询问是否已有类似工具或库存在。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI在视频编辑和生成中的实际价值和应用场景。
• 讨论中涉及多个技术细节，如JSON Schema、XML、Cutlass格式、JavaScript库等，表现出对具体实现方式的关注。
• [echelon] 提供了对行业趋势的见解，指出生成技术对未来视频编辑的潜在颠覆性影响。
• [EGreg] 的评论特别详细，展示了一个完整的技术构想，并提出了多个值得进一步探讨的问题和建议。

data.title: Bloom Filters by Example
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
Bloom Filter是一种快速且节省内存的数据结构，用于判断元素是否存在于集合中。它是一个概率数据结构，可能出现误报，即错误地判断一个元素可能存在于集合中。其核心是一个位向量，通过多个哈希函数将元素映射到位向量的索引位置，并将这些位置标记为1。测试元素是否在集合中时，再次使用相同的哈希函数，检查对应位是否全为1；若不全为1，则元素一定不在集合中；若全为1，则可能存在。

选择合适的哈希函数和参数（如位向量大小m和哈希函数个数k）可以调整误报率。哈希函数应独立且均匀分布，常用Murmur、FNV等。Bloom Filter的插入和查询时间复杂度为O(k)，空间效率高但存在误报可能。设计时需根据预期元素数量n调整m和k以优化性能。

Bloom Filters by Example
A Bloom filter is a data structure designed to tell you, rapidly and memory-efficiently, whether an element is
present in a set.
The price paid for this efficiency is that a Bloom filter is a
probabilistic data structure
: it
tells us that the element either
definitely is not
in the set or
may be
in the set.
The base data structure of a Bloom filter is a
Bit Vector
. Here's a small one we'll use to
demonstrate:
Each empty cell in that table represents a bit, and the number below it its index. To add an element to the Bloom
filter, we simply hash it a few times and set the bits in the bit vector at the index of those hashes to 1.
It's easier to see what that means than explain it, so enter some strings and see how the bit vector changes. Fnv
and Murmur are two simple hash functions:
Enter a string:
fnv:
murmur:
Your set: [
]
When you add a string, you can see that the bits at the index given by the hashes are set to 1. I've used the
color green to show the newly added ones, but any colored cell is simply a 1.
To test for membership, you simply hash the string with the same hash functions, then see if those values are set
in the bit vector. If they aren't, you know that the element isn't in the set. If they are, you only know that it
might
be, because another element or some combination of other elements could have set the same bits.
Again, let's demonstrate:
Test an element for membership:
fnv:
murmur:
Is the element in the set?
no
Probability of a false positive:
0%
And that's the basics of a bloom filter!
Advanced Topics
Before I write a bit more about Bloom filters, a disclaimer: I've never used them in production. Don't take my
word for it. All I intend to do is give you general ideas and pointers to where you can find out more.
In the following text, we will refer to a Bloom filter with
k
hashes,
m
bits in the filter, and
n
elements that have been inserted.
Hash Functions
The hash functions used in a Bloom filter should be
independent
and
uniformly distributed
. They
should also be as fast as possible (cryptographic hashes such as sha1, though widely used therefore are not very
good choices).
Examples of fast, simple hashes that are independent enough
3
include
murmur
,
xxHash
, the
fnv
series of hashes, and
HashMix
.
To see the difference that a faster-than-cryptographic hash function can make,
check out this story
of a ~800% speedup when switching a
bloom filter implementation from md5 to murmur.
In a short survey of bloom filter implementations:
Chromium
uses
murmur
.
(also,
here's
a short description of how they use bloom filters)

in

,

44412370.article_summary:
Bloom Filter是一种快速且节省内存的数据结构，用于判断元素是否存在于集合中。它是一个概率数据结构，可能出现误报，即错误地判断一个元素可能存在于集合中。其核心是一个位向量，通过多个哈希函数将元素映射到位向量的索引位置，并将这些位置标记为1。测试元素是否在集合中时，再次使用相同的哈希函数，检查对应位是否全为1；若不全为1，则元素一定不在集合中；若全为1，则可能存在。

选择合适的哈希函数和参数（如位向量大小m和哈希函数个数k）可以调整误报率。哈希函数应独立且均匀分布，常用Murmur、FNV等。Bloom Filter的插入和查询时间复杂度为O(k)，空间效率高但存在误报可能。设计时需根据预期元素数量n调整m和k以优化性能。

Why bother?
Some malware samples are known to do various checks to determine if they are
running in a virtual machine. One of the common checks is to look for
the presence of certain hardware components that are typically not emulated
in virtualized environments. One such component is the
CPU fan
.
One of the observed ways malware checks for the presence of a CPU fan is by
looking for the
Win32_Fan
class in WMI:
wmic path Win32_Fan get *
And the reason they do this is they want to avoid running
in virtual machines, because they want to complicate the analysis process
for security researchers.
There are plenty of ways for malware to detect if it is running in a VM.
In fact, there are plenty of WMI classes that can reveal the presence of
virtual hardware, such as
Win32_CacheMemory
,
Win32_VoltageProbe
, and
many others
.
In this post, I will be focusing on the CPU fan. Just because I like the idea
making a virtual machine think it has it. However, the same approach can
be applied to other hardware components and WMI classes as well.
How the computer knows it has a CPU fan?
The computer knows it has a CPU fan by reading the
SMBIOS
data.
How do I know that?
By googling
.
Win32_Fan
instances are provided by
Windows\System32\wbem\cimwin32.dll
.
If you disassemble it you will see that it reads SMBIOS data (specifically
entries with type 27) to get fan device information.
And indeed, if you disassemble
cimwin32.dll
, you will find exactly that:
Your first impulse might be to use DLL hooking and patch the
cimwin32
.
But that’s smol pp way of thinking. We can do better.
Type 27
The SMBIOS type 27 is defined as
“Cooling Device”
in the
System Management BIOS Reference Specification
:
We can dump the SMBIOS data using the
dmidecode
utility:
root@host:/# dmidecode -t27 -u
# dmidecode 3.3
Getting SMBIOS data from sysfs.
SMBIOS 3.4 present.
Handle 0x1B00, DMI type 27, 15 bytes
Header and Data:
1B 0F 00 1B 00 1C 65 00 00 DD 00 00 E0 15 01
Strings:
43 50 55 20 46 61 6E 00
CPU Fan
By default, the
dmidecode
utility will interpret the data and display it in a
more human-readable format:
root@host:/# dmidecode -t27
# dmidecode 3.3
Getting SMBIOS data from sysfs.
SMBIOS 3.4 present.
Handle 0x1B00, DMI type 27, 15 bytes
Cooling Device
Temperature Probe Handle: 0x1C00
Type: Chip Fan
Status: OK
OEM-specific Information: 0x0000DD00
Nominal Speed: 5600 rpm
Description: CPU Fan
Setting custom SMBIOS data in Xen
At the time of writing, the only available resource I found on how to set custom
SMBIOS data in Xen is this
almost 10 years old mcnewton’s post
. I recommend
reading it, as it exactly describes the struggle I had when figuring this out.
In short, you can set custom SMBIOS data in Xen by setting the
smbios_firmware
option in the domain configuration file to the path to a file containing
the SMBIOS data.
So, let’s create a file named
smbios.bin
with the following byte content:
1B 0F 00 1B 00 1C 65 00 00 DD 00 00 E0 15 01 43
50 55 20 46 61 6E 00
00
Note that the content is same as the output of
dmidecode -t27 -u
above,
but with additional
00
byte at the end, because the SMBIOS specification
requires it.
In the
Xen domain configuration file documentation
, we can also find this:
Since SMBIOS structures do not present their overall size, each entry in the
file must be preceded by a 32b integer indicating the size of the following
structure.
Our structure is 24 bytes long, so we need to prepend the content with
18 00 00 00
(24 in little-endian):
18 00 00 00
1B 0F 00 1B 00 1C 65 00 00 DD 00 00
E0 15 01 43 50 55 20 46 61 6E 00 00
Now we can set the
smbios_firmware
option in the Xen domain configuration file
to the path to this file:
smbios_firmware
=
"/path/to/smbios.bin"
Let’s save the configuration file and start our Windows domain.
root@host:/# xl create /path/to/windows/domain.cfg
And let’s check if the CPU fan is now present in the Windows VM:
PS C:\> wmic path Win32_Fan get *
No Instance(s) Available.
Oh noes. Something’s wrong.
The Betrayal
I missed one important detail in the documentation of the
smbios_firmware
option:
smbios_firmware=”STRING”
Specifies a path to a file that contains extra SMBIOS firmware …
Not all predefined structures can be overridden, only the following types:
0, 1, 2, 3, 11, 22, 39
. The file can also …
Frankly, I did
not
miss this at first. I just hoped that what I was trying to
do was not
“overriding”
the predefined structure.
Because Xen (or rather
hvmloader
)
does not define it
.
So, before defining it myself, I tried to find out if there was any other poor
soul who tried to do the same thing before me. And to my disappointment, there
was
. Right in the
xen-devel patch archive
.
Why it was my disappointment, you may ask? Because after reading the response
to the patch, I felt the frustration of the author. But that’s for another story.
Anyway, the patch was rejected, but it’s small and simple, so it’s easy
to apply it to the Xen source code.
Type 28, too
After applying the patch and recompiling Xen, I

What is Octelium?
Octelium is a free and open source, self-hosted, unified platform for zero trust resource access that is primarily meant to be a modern alternative to remote access VPNs and similar tools. It is built to be generic enough to not only operate as a zero-config remote access VPN (i.e. alternative to OpenVPN Access Server, Twingate, Tailscale, etc...), a ZTNA platform (i.e. alternative to Cloudflare Access, Teleport, Google BeyondCorp, etc...), a scalable infrastructure for secure tunnels (i.e. alternative to ngrok), but can also operate as an API gateway, an AI gateway, an infrastructure for MCP gateways and A2A architectures, a PaaS-like platform for secure as well as anonymous hosting and deployment for containerized applications, a Kubernetes gateway/ingress/load balancer and even as an infrastructure for your own homelab. Octelium provides a scalable zero trust architecture (ZTA) for identity-based, application-layer (L7) aware secret-less secure access, via both private client-based access over WireGuard/QUIC tunnels as well as public clientless access (i.e. BeyondCorp), for users, both humans and workloads, to any private/internal resource behind NAT in any environment as well as to publicly protected resources such as SaaS APIs and databases via context-aware access control on a per-request basis through policy-as-code.
Use Cases
Octelium is designed to be generic enough (check out the main features below for more details) to be completely or partially used as a solution for various use cases depending on your needs/requirements, notably:
Modern remote access VPN
A modern zero trust L-7 aware alternative to commercial remote access/corporate VPNs to provide zero-config client-based over WireGuard/QUIC tunnels as well as client-less secret-less access via dynamic identity-based, L-7 aware, context-aware access control via policy-as-code (i.e. alternative to OpenVPN Access Server, Twingate, Tailscale, etc...).
Unified ZTNA/BeyondCorp architecture
A Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform/ BeyondCorp architecture (i.e. alternative to Cloudflare Access, Google BeyondCorp, Zscaler Private Access, Teleport, Fortinet, etc...).
Self-hosted infrastructure for secure tunnels
A self-hosted secure tunnels and reverse proxy programmable infrastructure (i.e. alternative to ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, etc...). You can see an example
here
.
Self-hosted PaaS
A scalable PaaS-like hosting/deployment platform to deploy, scale and provide both secure as well as anonymous public hosting for your containerized applications (i.e. similar to Vercel, Netlify, etc...). You can see examples for
Next.js/Vite apps
,
remote VSCode
,
remote Ollama
and
Pi-hole
.
API gateway
A self-hosted, scalable, secure API gateway that takes care of access, routing, deployment and scaling of containerized microservices, authentication, L-7 aware/context aware authorization and visibility (i.e. alternative to Kong Gateway, Apigee, etc...). You can see an example
here
.
AI gateway
A scalable AI gateway to any AI LLM providers with identity-based, context-aware access control, routing and visibility (see an example
here
).
Unified Zero Trust Access to SaaS APIs
Unified, secret-less that eliminates distributing and sharing the typically long-lived/over-privileged API keys and access tokens, access to all HTTP-based SaaS APIs for teams and workloads/applications where you can control access on a per-request basis via policy-as-code. Octelium also supports secret-less access to Kubernetes clusters, PostgreSQL/MySQL-based databases as well as to SSH servers (see the main features

data.title: Implementing fast TCP fingerprinting with eBPF
data.author: halb
data.article_summary:
本文记录了作者使用eBPF在Golang web服务器中实现快速TCP指纹识别的过程。TCP指纹识别是一种用于反机器人解决方案中检测异常网络请求的技术，随着对网络内容抓取需求的增加，该技术愈发重要。本文分为两部分，第一部分介绍TCP指纹识别的背景及实现策略，第二部分描述了一个概念验证的Golang web服务器开发过程，该服务器能回显客户端的TCP指纹。

作者首先用C语言实现了一个简单的"Hello World" web服务器，以展示HTTP/1.0的简单性及其直接使用操作系统提供的接口。该服务器通过创建socket、绑定IP和端口、监听连接，并使用`accept()`等待客户端连接。

作者强调，要深入理解网络通信，需借助工具如Wireshark捕获并分析网络流量，特别是TCP三次握手过程。通过该项目，作者展示了eBPF在网络层实现指纹识别的潜力。项目代码已在GitHub开源。

• [spense] 指出，指纹识别技术不仅用于bot检测，还被Cloudflare等服务用于快速检测DDoS攻击，并提供了相关博文链接，强调指纹识别在安全防护中的作用。

In this article I want to document my journey implementing fast TCP fingerprinting
in a golang webserver, using eBPF.
Just to provide some background, TCP fingerprinting is one of the many techniques that can be used to detect
unusual or identifying informations about a web request when implementing an anti-bot solution.
This has been a hot topic lately, caused by the rising need to scrape the internet for human content to feeed to the LLMs.
Implementing such a system offers interesting technical challenges that span different domains,
but most importantly itâs a very good first project to learn eBPF.
I split this article in two parts.
In this first part I provide a background on TCP fingerprinting, and discuss some implementation strategies.
In the
second part
I describe the actual development
of a proof-of-concept Golang webserver that echoes back the TCP fingerprint of the client.
The project is
open source on Github
HTTP requests, from first principles
It can be useful to approach this problem from first principles, looking at the way web servers work under the hood.
This is not as scary as it might seem: although browsers and the underlying protocols evolved and got
more complex
over time, for
compatibility reasons they
still support the HTTP/1.0 protocol, which was
designed to be simple
.
An HTTP/1.0 web server is just a light layer on top of a TCP connection, and can be implemented in just a few lines of C code.
As an example, I implemented a simple hello world webserver in C that weâll use as
a starting point for the experiments in this article.
You donât really have to read the code for now, but keep in mind that itâs here:

This is certainly not a production ready webserver, but it does its job.
If we compile the code, run it, and visit
http://127.0.0.1:8080
from any modern browser, weâll be greeted by a hello world:
Beautiful, isnât it?
This code differs significantly from the hello worlds that you would normally write
with a modern web framework, regardles of whatâs trending today, for an important reason:
We are directly using the abstraction layer provided by the operative system, nothing is
hidden away.
All the code in this example can be broken down into a few calls of the C standard library.
Those functions are just thin wrappers around
syscalls
whith a similar name, which are all we need to implement a webserver on a POSIX system:
we create a
socket
we
bind
it to a ip and port, and start to
listen
in an infinite loop, we call
accept()
, which blocks the execution
until a client connects to our server
after a connection is made, accept returns a file descriptor
which we can
read
and
write
to like a simple file. At the other end of the
line, the client will communicate with us in a similar way.
Itâs easy to see that beyond defining an ip and port we donât
have to write any networking-related code, the OS is taking care of that for us.
Because of that, if we want to understand whatâs happening at a deeper level we need to
capture and inspect the network traffic that reaches our webserver, which is something that
we can easily do with wireshark.
To capture the packets shown in this screenshot I launched wireshark on the loopback interface, then I visited
the hello world website from the browser in order to generate some data.
With this webserver running and with our example traffic capture at hand, we can now
start to experiment with tcp traffic.

不同观点：
• rage4774 认为当前的实验和结论过于自信，仅提供了在当前时间点上看似合理的路线，而忽略了社会学视角。他举了古罗马斯多葛学派的例子，指出历史上有些人基于特定信仰和价值观做出看似“非自然”的行为，因此当前的结论可能只是浅显的回应，无法排除其他可能性，不能让人确信历史事实。

• raincom 没有提出具体观点，仅提供了一个链接，可能意在引导读者查看更多相关信息或参考资料。

• notfed 对实验的具体细节提出疑问，特别是航行实验的起止点以及如何确定旅行是故意进行的，质疑实验的证据和结论的可靠性。

• flowmerchant 补充了关于女性在耐力划船活动中优势的讨论。他以德州水上挑战赛为例，指出女性在长时间划船中具有更低的重心和更强的心理耐力，这与实验中使用女性划船的选择相符。

补充讨论：
• rage4774 强调了社会学和历史价值观对人们行为的影响，提出了实验结论可能存在的不确定性。
• notfed 对实验的地理和证据细节提出了具体疑问，要求更明确的说明。
• flowmerchant 提供了关于女性在划船活动中表现的实证支持，补充了实验设计中性别选择的合理性。

争议焦点：
• rage4774 对实验结论的可靠性和全面性提出质疑，认为缺少社会学视角的考量。
• notfed 对实验的具体实施细节和证据的充分性表示怀疑。

这些讨论共同构成了对历史实验的多角度审视，包括方法论、性别角色以及结论的可靠性等问题。

data.author: voxleone
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了如果在海边发现鱿鱼的“卵团”该如何处理。作者提供了相关建议，并提到读者也可以在这篇关于鱿鱼的文章下讨论其他未涉及的安全新闻。文章还包括博客的管理政策，并标记了发布日期和相关标签，目前有14条评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：本地LLM（大型语言模型）的隐私与数据安全问题，以及用户对LLM了解其个人信息的担忧。

不同观点：
• **对本地LLM使用的质疑**：drillsteps5认为，除非从事非法或不道德行为，否则没有理由使用本地LLM。该评论暗示使用本地LLM可能与不良意图相关。
• **对LLM了解用户信息的担忧**：多位用户（如rcruzeiro, b0a04gl, bgwalter）表示对LLM能够获取用户个人信息的担忧，尤其是当这些信息被用于调整模型输出时。bgwalter甚至将这种情况比作FBI档案。
• **LLM不获取个人信息的声明**：BurningFrog和holri通过实际测试（使用Grok和Mistral.ai）表明，这些模型并不直接获取个人信息，除非用户明确分享这些信息。
• **对LLM隐私风险的理性分析**：nullc指出，人们在LLM时代对隐私的期望往往不准确，LLM可能会通过“推理”得出错误结论，这增加了隐私风险。
• **隐私保护解决方案的建议**：nonelog提出使用Duck.ai这样的平台，完全保护隐私，不收集用户数据。
• **对LLM隐私问题的接受与适应**：EGreg表示，对LLM构建用户画像的情况是可控的，且与在公共社交媒体上的行为类似，强调用户自我警觉。

补充讨论：
• **LLM输出个性化的技术原理**：b0a04gl提到，LLM能够通过用户历史交互生成嵌入，并通过交叉注意力机制影响输出，即使不显式传递历史聊天内容，模型仍能“记住”用户偏好。
• **对LLM“间谍”角色的调侃**：marcusstorm将LLM比作间谍或FBI特工，暗示其能够揭露用户信息，这与实际LLM行为形成对比。
• **用户对隐私概念的理解差异**：hardlianotion提到对“integrous”一词的不理解，反映出用户在讨论隐私问题时存在概念混淆。
• **LLM隐私与实用性的平衡**：simianwords质疑如果没有LLM了解用户信息，模型的实用性是否会下降，提出了隐私与功能之间的权衡问题。

争议焦点：LLM是否应该以及如何获取和使用用户数据以优化输出，以及用户对隐私保护的期望与现实之间的差距。

data.title: Tools I love: mise(-en-place)
data.author: micvbang
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了名为 **mise** 的工具，它简化了软件的安装、使用和管理，特别适用于管理不同项目中的开发工具和环境变量。mise 通过 **mise.toml** 配置文件来定义项目所需的工具和版本，自动在进入项目目录时配置环境，支持多版本管理，并在不同目录中自动切换工具版本。它还支持声明和运行任务，类似 Bash 脚本，可用于构建、测试等操作。在 CI/CD 管道中使用 mise，可确保开发环境和构建环境中的工具版本一致。通过将 **mise.toml** 提交到代码库，所有开发者都能自动使用预期的开发工具和命令。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发工具（如Mise、Nix、asdf等）在管理开发环境中的使用体验和优缺点比较。

不同观点：
• **支持Mise**：
   - **hks0**：Mise解决了因环境不一致导致的支持请求问题，推荐作为唯一支持的构建工具，并认为Mise是asdf等工具的优秀替代品。
   - **vsviridov**：从asdf切换到Mise，体验很好，已成为基础设置的一部分。
   - **rsanheim**：从asdf切换到Mise后，体验稳定、快速，主要使用工具管理功能。
   - **stryan**：尽管不喜欢学习新工具，但Mise的易用性和良好的文档使其值得一试，尤其是其 ergonomics（人体工程学设计）出色。

• **Mise与Nix的对比**：
   - **ukprogrammer**：对"一个工具统领一切"的工具持怀疑态度，认为可能存在边缘情况。相比Mise，更关注Nix和其flakes功能，认为可能有长期适用性问题。
   - **mrbonner**：Nix和Home Manager适用于一般工具和实用程序设置，但在语言开发环境上更倾向于使用各语言的流行工具，如Python的uv、Node的npm等。
   - **dayjah**：从asdf切换到Mise，最终转向Nix，认为Nix是更好的选择，但学习曲线陡峭，文档较差。

• **技术细节与问题**：
   - **jph**：Mise在macOS上通过brew安装PostgreSQL时遇到问题，提供了解决方案，并询问是否有更好的方法。
   - **hacb**：认为Mise是GNU Make和asdf的结合体，寻求确认。

• **对版本管理的批评**：
   - **hdjrudni**：批评工具版本管理的需求，认为程序应更稳定，不应频繁升级或降级版本。

• **其他工具用户的反馈**：
   - **sergiotapia**：长期使用asdf，不喜欢需要安装插件，计划尝试Mise在Elixir、Erlang和NodeJS上的表现。

补充讨论：
• **nix与direnv的结合**：
   - **xyst**：使用Nix和direnv管理开发环境，通过shell.nix定义环境，并使用`nix develop`创建隔离环境，避免机器上安装多个版本的工具。

争议焦点：
• **Mise是否能真正替代所有其他工具**：部分用户（如ukprogrammer、mrbonner）对"一个工具统领一切"的理念表示怀疑，认为可能存在边缘情况或特定场景下其他工具更合适。
• **Nix的学习曲线和文档问题**：虽然有用户（如dayjah）认为Nix是更好的工具，但其陡峭的学习曲线和较差的文档是主要障碍。

总结：讨论围绕Mise、asdf、Nix等工具在管理开发环境中的一系列优缺点展开，用户对工具的易用性、稳定性、学习曲线等有不同看法，争议主要集中在Mise是否能真正做到"一个工具统领一切"以及Nix的复杂性上。

44414987.article_content:
29 Jun 2025
Tools I love: mise(-en-place)
tools
cli
mise
Once in a while you get introduced to a tool that instantly changes the way you work. For me,
mise
is one of those tools.
mise is the logical conclusion to a lot of the meta-tooling that exists around language-specific version and package managers like
asdf
,
nvm
,
uv
,
pyenv
etc. It makes it exceptionally easy to install, use, and manage software. It also allows you to manage
environment variables
and
declare tasks
(run commands).
Trying out new tools
The first step in getting an intuitive understanding of what mise can help you with is to use it to install a tool. Pick your favorite and try it out; it supports
a lot
!
I recently read about
jj
in
Thorsten Ball’s newsletter
and decided to try it out (again). I crossed my fingers and hoped that
jj
was
one of the tools supported by mise
and, to my delight, it was! The process looked something like this:
$
jj
command_not_found_handler:5:
command
not found: jj
$
mise use jj
mise ~/projects/examples_mise/mise.toml tools: jj@0.30.0
$
jj version
jj 0.30.0
$
cd
..
$
jj version
command_not_found_handler:5:
command
not found: jj
$
cd
eaxmples_mise
$
jj version
jj 0.30.0
As the above shows, with mise we’re just one command away from installing and trying out a new tool, e.g.
mise use jj
.
In the above we that mise printed
mise ~/projects/examples_mise/mise.toml tools: jj@0.30.0
. This tells us that mise has created (or updated) the mise configuration
on that path
.
We also see that if we cd out of
~/projects
, the
jj
command is no longer available. If we cd back into
~/projects/examples_mise
, it becomes available again; unless you explicitly install tools globally, mise will only make the tools available which are mentioned in a
mise.toml
file on the path from your current directory to the root of your file system. That of course means that we could potentially meet multiple
mise.toml
files when going back up to the root of the file system. Mise handles this by concatting the configurations and overwriting conflicting configurations, letting the file furthest down the tree win.
This is a clever design as it allows us to configure different versions of the same tool to be available in different directories. Let’s have a look at what the
mise.toml
file looks like:
[tools]
jj
=
"latest"
If we want a specific version of
jj
to be installed in a specific directory, we just update the toml file to say e.g.
jj = "0.30.0
.
Managing multiple versions of a tool
Let’s see what it looks like to use mise to manage Python versions for two projects with different requirements:
$
tree
.
├── project_new
│	└── mise.toml
└── project_old
└── mise.toml
$
cat
project_new/mise.toml
[
tools]
python
=
"3.11"
$
cat
project_old/mise.toml
[
tools]
python
=
"3.8"
$
cd
project_new
$
python
--version
Python 3.11.13
$
cd
../project_old
$
python
--version
Python 3.8.20
When we cd into one of the directories listed above, mise automatically makes the version of the tool configured in
mise.toml
available to us. If it isn’t already installed, mise will install it for us. The implication of this is that you can commit a
mise.toml
to your repository, and anyone that has mise installed will automatically get and use the expected dev tools when they enter the project directory. And when it’s time to upgrade a dev tool, you can just update the version number in
mise.toml
and everyone will start using the new version!
Use in CI/CD pipelines
The fact that mise makes tools available to you according to the
mise.toml
file in your current working directory has further implications: it’s not just developer machines that can benefit from using mise; CI/CD pipelines can benefit greatly as well! When you use mise in your pipelines, you avoid the problem of having out of sync versions between developer and build machines. You get to have a single place where you can configure the version of your dev tools everywhere!
As I mentioned in the beginning, besides managing dev tools, mise also allows you to
declare and run so-called tasks
. Think of a task as an advanced invocation of a bash script. Even if we use tasks as just plain bash scripts (they can do a lot more), it can be a major advantage to declare common operations such as building, testing, linting etc. as mise tasks, since all developers get access to them and will run their commands in exactly the same way every time. If you’re diligent in your naming, you can even make the experience of building or testing across projects identical.
The following are examples of some very simple Python-related tasks declared in
mise.toml
:
[tasks.install-deps]
run
=
[
"uv pip install -r requirements.txt"
]
[tasks.test]
run
=
[
"pytest ."
]
Adding this to
mise.toml
will make the commands
mise install-deps
and
mise test
available. Again, if you check this in to your repo, the commands will be available to all developers and pipelines. And reusing these names in your rust project means that you can use the same commands t

data.title: Personal care products disrupt the human oxidation field
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕一篇关于乳液和香水可能影响氧化化学的文章展开，讨论了标题党问题、化学品对健康的影响、以及对使用个人护理产品的不同看法。

不同观点：
• [muhdeeb] 认为文章标题有故意制造震惊效果的倾向，但内容相对谨慎，并指出文章没有为个人健康建议提供依据。他强调该领域非常复杂，不能简单化为黑白分明的建议，并批评了文章中使用"disrupt"一词，因为其负面含义。
• [dylan604] 指出许多人转向使用天然成分和无香料产品，因为对专有化学品的信任问题，并表示对产品广告之外的具体效果感兴趣。
• [8bitsrule] 对个人护理产品中的化学成分测试表示怀疑，并提到洗澡和洗衣服等日常活动对皮肤的影响也可能不被完全理解。
• [12_throw_away] 强调化学、环境化学和生物化学的复杂性，指出在利益驱动下，许多系统在被充分研究之前就被改变。
• [parpfish] 认为文章不会导致人们减少使用乳液，但会导致高端乳液添加"OH前体"作为新的市场营销术语。
• [giantg2] 对普通香料在癌症风险和内分泌干扰方面的影响表示担忧，并指出大多数产品都有无香料替代品。
• [userbinator] 认为文章相对乐观，与近年来充斥市场的"可怕化学品"文章形成对比，并解读出乳液和香水有抗氧化效果。

补充讨论：
• [flint] 提到每天出汗的自然方式，但没有直接评论文章内容。
• [peanut_merchant] 请求对文章健康影响的基本解释。
• [indus] 质疑肥皂等现代个人护理产品的必要性，基于进化论的观点。
• [maipen] 抱怨人们不阅读文章就评论，并表示应该尽量减少使用复杂和合成的产品，但在必要时可以使用。
• [drabbiticus] 提供了一个更易理解的相关链接，并认为文章结果在日常生活中不值得担心。
• [867-5309] 指出了某些香料成分的问题。
• [fiatjaf] 表示文章难以阅读。
• [metalman] 对通过皮肤释放的生物杀灭气体表示惊讶，并提到对人类生物化学需要更细致的理解。

争议焦点：
• 文章标题和内容是否夸大其词，是否有意制造震惊效果。
• 个人护理产品中的化学成分是否被充分理解和测试。

data.author: kelindar
data.article_summary: 该文介绍了一个高性能的Go语言内部事件总线库（kelindar/event），适用于模块解耦和异步事件处理。它支持同步和异步处理，每秒可处理数百万事件，比Go通道快4到10倍。该库通用且简单，无需额外依赖，每个订阅者运行在自己的 goroutine 中以确保非阻塞。它适用于单进程内的模块解耦和轻量级发布/订阅模式，但不适合进程间通信、事件持久化或跨语言场景。文中还提供了使用默认和自定义调度器的示例以及性能基准测试。该项目采用MIT许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对高性能事件发布/订阅机制与Go channels等其他方法的对比及其优化取舍的讨论。

不同观点：
• **singron**：认为该实现为高吞吐量和广播进行了高度优化，但忽略了channel的其他用例。该实现对消费者进行分组并使用单锁机制，减少了锁操作的频率，但在低负载情况下可能不太理想，因为需要频繁轮询元数据。

• **minaguib**：建议在文档中加入对底层方法论的描述，并与其他方法（如Go channels、LMAX等）进行比较，以便用户更好地理解该实现的优劣。

• **hinkley**：讨论了为提升性能而舍弃的特性，质疑这些特性是否应该对所有用户造成负担。建议通过代码重构，让不常用特性成为低成本的抽象，从而降低对不需要这些特性的用户的影响。

• **kelindar**：基于实际项目（小型多人游戏）的经验，指出这种优化实现（事件总线）比Go channel快4-10倍，尤其是在高性能需求的场景下。

• **zx2c4**：对性能提升的原因感兴趣，希望了解底层结构差异是如何带来如此显著的性能改进。

• **gethly**：提到自己曾写过类似的无锁设计，并提供了相关博客链接，暗示对这种优化有经验和兴趣。

• **DmitryOlshansky**：质疑"通用性"的描述，认为通用通常意味着支持任意类型，而该实现要求事件实现特定接口，与通常的"通用"定义相悖。

• **aitchnyu**：提到Zeromq曾推广进程内队列通信，与该实现类似，暗示这种模式在不同场景下的适用性。

• **tombert**：对性能提升印象深刻，但好奇是否借鉴了LMAX Disruptor的设计，表示需要深入研究该实现。

• **absolute_unit22**：虽然不特别需要高性能，但表示愿意尝试新开源库进行实验，尤其是在当前项目规模不大的情况下。

• **qudat**：关心该实现是否支持数据流处理，而不仅仅是单个事件，并分享了自己基于channel实现的pubsub项目链接。

• **st3fan**：对"每秒处理百万事件"的声明持怀疑态度，认为在真实应用中，加入数据库调用或数据处理后的性能对比才更具说服力。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于该实现的"高性能"声明是否具有实际意义，特别是在真实应用场景中的表现。
- 讨论中多次提到与其他方法（如Go channels、LMAX Disruptor）的比较，显示出用户对不同方法间权衡和选择的关注。
- 对通用性和性能优化之间的取舍存在不同看法，部分用户认为应该让不常用特性成为低成本的抽象。

Fast, In-Process Event Dispatcher
This package offers a high-performance,
in-process event dispatcher
for Go, ideal for decoupling modules and enabling asynchronous event handling. It supports both synchronous and asynchronous processing, focusing on speed and simplicity.
High Performance:
Processes millions of events per second, about
4x to 10x faster
than channels.
Generic:
Works with any type implementing the
Event
interface.
Asynchronous:
Each subscriber runs in its own goroutine, ensuring non-blocking event handling.
Use When:
✅ Decoupling modules within a single Go process.
✅ Implementing lightweight pub/sub or event-driven patterns.
✅ Needing high-throughput, low-latency event dispatching.
✅ Preferring a simple, dependency-free solution.
Not For:
❌ Inter-process/service communication (use Kafka, NATS, etc.).
❌ Event persistence, durability, or advanced routing/filtering.
❌ Cross-language/platform scenarios.
❌ Event replay, dead-letter queues, or deduplication.
❌ Heavy subscribe/unsubscribe churn or massive dynamic subscriber counts.
Generic In-Process Pub/Sub
This repository contains a
simple, in-process event dispatcher
to be used to decouple internal modules. It provides a generic way to define events, publish and subscribe to them.

data.title: Brad Woods Digital Garden
data.author: samuel246
data.article_summary: "Brad Woods Digital Garden" 是一个关于网页开发和创意编程的资源集合。文章涵盖了多种技术主题，如使用 three.js 和 GSAP 在球体表面动画化网格、通过 CSS 创建 3D 空间、滚动驱动的相机动画、以及使用 SVG clip-path 实现线条绘制效果。此外，文章探讨了软件开发中的 "Juice" 概念，即通过细节提升用户体验，并讨论了情感化设计和个性化用户界面。技术方面还包括 CSS 重置、CSS 混合模式、Intersection Observer、以及如何实现动态头部和无限滚动等。文章还提供了关于写作、浏览器适应性和用户界面教学方法的见解。

不同观点：
• [tolerance] 认为未来的设计趋势将是"Cybermod"（ cybermod ）风格，这是一种带有数字/技术元素的"残酷主义"风格，灵感来自过去的艺术运动如De Stijl，但更加简约。他认为这种趋势会类似于现代主义运动，出现在历史上的过渡阶段，例如反恐战争和未来战争之间。他还提到Cyberpunk所预见的未来并没有实现，因为其世界构建没有考虑到像Issey Miyake和Rick Owens这样的时尚元素。

data.title: Loss of key US satellite data could send hurricane forecasting back 'decades'
data.author: trauco
data.article_summary: 美国关键气象卫星数据项目DMSP将于2025年6月30日停止，导致飓风预测能力可能倒退“几十年”。该项目提供的独特高分辨率数据对于监测飓风发展和北极海冰变化至关重要。科学家们表示，失去这些数据将严重影响飓风预测，尤其是在飓风季节加剧的情况下。尽管NOAA声称不会影响预报质量，但研究人员警告说，这将导致预测能力大幅下降，并对极地地区的观测产生负面影响。此决定正值NOAA人手不足之际，被认为是特朗普政府对科学系统的破坏。科学家们对突然失去如此重要的数据源表示震惊和担忧。

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross认为，卫星本身运行正常，数据流的突然中断可能是人为决定，并对美国直接废弃而非出售卫星表示质疑。
• mensetmanusman指出，NOAA-20卫星更先进，并且不会影响天气预报质量，认为这是退役旧传感器的正常步骤。

• jenadine和ChrisArchitect提到之前有类似讨论，并提供了链接供参考。

补充讨论：

Sudden loss of key US satellite data could send hurricane forecasting back ‘decades’
Scientists left scrambling amid hurricane season after irreplaceable program is slotted to be shuttered
Eric Holthaus
Sat 28 Jun 2025 10.27 EDT
First published on Sat 28 Jun 2025 07.00 EDT
Share
A critical US atmospheric data collection program will be halted by Monday, giving weather forecasters just days to prepare, according to a
public notice
sent this week. Scientists that the Guardian spoke with say the change could set hurricane forecasting back “decades”, just as this year’s season ramps up.
In a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) message sent on Wednesday to its scientists, the agency said that “due to recent service changes” the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) will “discontinue ingest, processing and distribution of all DMSP data no later than June 30, 2025”.
Due to their unique characteristics and ability to map the entire world twice a day with
extremely high resolution
, the three DMSP satellites are a primary source of information for scientists to monitor Arctic sea ice and hurricane development. The DMSP partners with Noaa to make weather data collected from the satellites publicly available.
Trump plans on ‘phasing out’ Fema disaster agency after hurricane season
Read more
The reasons for the changes, and which agency was driving them, were not immediately clear. Noaa said they would not affect the quality of forecasting.
However, the Guardian spoke with several scientists inside and outside of the US government whose work depends on the DMSP, and all said there are no other US programs that can form an adequate replacement for its data.
“We’re a bit blind now,” said Allison Wing, a hurricane researcher at Florida State University. Wing said the DMSP satellites are the only ones that let scientists see inside the clouds of developing hurricanes, giving them a critical edge in forecasting that now may be jeopardized.
“Before these types of satellites were present, there would often be situations where you’d wake up in the morning and have a big surprise about what the hurricane looked like,” said Wing. “Given increases in hurricane intensity and increasing prevalence towards rapid intensification in recent years, it’s not a good time to have less information.”
The satellites also formed a unique source of data for tracking changes to the Arctic and Antarctic, and had been tracking changes to polar sea ice continuously
for more than 40 years
.
“These are some of the regions that are changing the fastest around the planet,” said Carlos Moffat, an oceanographer at the University of Delaware who had been working on a research project in Antarctica that depended on DMSP data. “This new announcement about the sea ice data really amounts to blinding ourselves and preventing us from observing these critical systems.”
Researchers say the satellites themselves are operating normally and do not appear to have suffered any errors that would physically prevent the data from continuing to be collected and distributed, so the abrupt data halt might have been an intentional decision.
Key US weather monitoring offices understaffed as hurricane season starts
Read more
“It’s pretty shocking,” Moffat said. “It’s hard to imagine what would be the logic of removing access now and in such a sudden manner that it’s just impossible to plan for. I certainly don’t know of any other previous cases where we’re taking away data that is being collected, and we’re just removing it from public access.”
The loss of DMSP comes as Noaa’s weather and climate monitoring services have become critically understaffed this year as
Donald Trump
’s so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) initiative has
instilled
draconian
cuts
to federal environmental programs.
A current Noaa scientist who wishes to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation said that the action to halt the DMSP, when taken in context with other recent moves by the
Trump administration
, amounted to “a systematic destruction of science”.
The researcher also confirmed that federal hurricane forecasters were left unprepared for the sudden change with only a few days of notice.
“It’s an instant loss of roughly half of our capabilities,” said the scientist. “You can’t expect us to make accurate forecasts and warnings when you take the useful tools away. It frankly is an embarrassment for the government to pursue a course with less data and just pretend everything will be OK.”
Scientists said the decision to halt the DMSP will result in immediately degraded hurricane forecasts during what is
expected to be an above-

data.author: mrqjr
data.article_summary: 本文描述了一个测试配置系统，主要用于评估不同AI模型的性能。系统包括API URL、API Key、模型选择、自定义提示、测试轮次等配置选项。测试结果展示实时数据，如首次 token 生成时间、输出速度、结果和状态等。具体测试示例显示了DeepSeek-R1-0528模型的测试情况，当前处于测试中，显示首次token时间为0ms，输出速度为0 t/s，尚未生成有效结果。系统还提供历史记录查看和清除功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某个项目或帖子的可信度、实用性以及其出现在平台首页的合理性的不同观点。

不同观点：
• **swyx的观点**：认为购买域名使项目看起来更商业化，从而降低了可信度。他还指出，大多数人可能更愿意使用已有的数据（如artificialanalysis提供的数字），而不是自己运行基准测试，但个人运行基准测试也是可以的。

• **vmeklis的观点**：对项目持积极态度，认为这是一个不错的想法，并将其比作LMArena的巧妙变体。

• **mdhb的观点**：质疑帖子出现在平台首页的合理性，指出该帖子由新账户创建，互动少（零评论和仅2个投票），但却出现在首页，暗示可能存在异常。

补充讨论：
• **可信度争议**：swyx对项目商业化的担忧与mdhb对帖子突然出现在首页的质疑，共同指向了对该项目或帖子可信度的关注。

• **用户需求**：swyx提到了用户可能更倾向于依赖现成数据，而不是自己运行测试，这反映了在便捷性和自定义之间的选择偏好。

• **平台机制**：mdhb的评论暗示了对平台推荐机制的怀疑，认为互动少的帖子不太应该出现在首页。

这些观点共同构成了对项目本身及其在平台上曝光情况的多元看法，涉及到可信度、实用性和平台机制等方面。

data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 2017年，美国蒙大拿州的小镇Seeley Lake遭受长达49天的野火浓烟，空气质量严重下降。免疫学副教授Christopher Migliaccio及其团队研究了居民暴露于浓烟后的健康影响，发现人们的肺功能并没有立即恶化，而是在一年后显著下降，且多数人在两年后仍未恢复。研究显示，野火烟雾的长期影响可能延迟显现。近年来，美国野火更加频繁剧烈，导致空气质量恶化，越来越多的人面临长期烟雾暴露的风险。然而，科学和政策对此健康威胁的了解仍非常有限，尤其对于多次暴露的长期影响知之甚少。野火烟雾的化学成分复杂，可能比普通空气污染对健康危害更大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：野火烟雾对生活质量和健康的影响，以及应对措施

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor：描述了因2018年坎普大火及之后一系列问题（包括电力不稳定、保险费增加和持续的烟雾）不得不搬离原住地，最终迁至远离森林地区的经历。现在通过使用空气净化设备保持室内空气质量，但在室外仍有健康担忧（如臭氧问题）。
• photon_garden：提到了《光之食者》（The Light Eaters）这本书，并对其内容表示赞赏，但未直接讨论野火烟雾问题，而是引入了与植物智力相关的阅读材料。
• davidw：住在俄勒冈州喀斯喀特山脉东部，每年夏天末都有"烟雾季节"，尽管天气适合户外活动，但因烟雾问题不宜外出。
• mschuster91：关注野火烟雾、吸烟、新冠对肺部健康的综合影响，强调这种组合会对医疗系统造成巨大压力，并分享了个人因感冒导致肺功能测试结果不佳的经历，指出这对运动和整体健康的影响。

补充讨论：
• burnt-resistor提到了具体空气质量指数（AQI）和使用的空气净化设备，如BlueAir 680i和HVAC系统，以及MERV过滤器在控制室内空气质量方面的有效性。
• mschuster91进一步扩展了讨论，提到除了野火烟雾，吸烟和新冠对肺部的累积损害可能会引发一系列健康问题（如肥胖、糖尿病等），并表达了对未来医疗负担的担忧。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接的立场对立，但讨论中隐含了对不同地区烟雾问题严重程度的认知差异，例如davidw提到的"烟雾季节"相对规律且可预测，而burnt-resistor则强调了长期健康影响和搬迁的无奈。此外，mschuster91对医疗系统负担的担忧与其他评论中对具体应对措施的讨论形成了潜在的关注点差异。

or 49 straight days
, everyone in Seeley Lake was breathing smoke. A wildfire had ignited outside the small rural community in Montana, and the plume of smoke had parked itself over the houses. Air quality plummeted. At several moments, the concentration of particulate matter in the air exceeded the upper limit of what monitors could measure.
Christopher Migliaccio, an associate professor of immunology at the University of Montana, saw an opportunity to do what few have ever done: study what happens after people get exposed to wildfire smoke. He and his team quickly cobbled together funding and drove out to Seeley Lake to get data.
That was in 2017. The researchers followed up with residents for two years after the fires, checking on their lung function. To their surprise, the worst effects didn’t show up immediately, despite the heavy dose of smoke. Instead, people’s lung function seemed to deteriorate later. Right after the fires, about 10 percent of the cohort had lung function that fell below the lower limit of normal. By the one-year mark,
about 46 percent did
. At the two-year mark, most of those people still had abnormally poor lung function. “We were very surprised,” Migliaccio told me. He and his colleagues had intended to follow the residents for a third year, but then COVID hit. Instead, they tried exposing mice to wildfire smoke in a controlled lab environment. Their results pointed to a similar outcome: The worst effects took time to present.
Migliaccio’s work can speak to only a single smoke event. But it is the type of event that more people in the United States are dealing with, over and over again. Until recently, wildfires that exposed large populations to smoke were a relatively rare occurrence. But that’s changing: More frequent and intense wildfires are
erasing or even reversing
decades of
gains made in American air quality
in the majority of U.S. states. Across the country, from 2012 to 2022, the number of people exposed to unhealthy air from wildfire smoke increased
27-fold
;
one out of every four
unhealthy air days in parts of the country is now a smoke day. “It is the exposure that is impacting air quality across the U.S. now more than any other pollution source,” Joan Casey, an environmental epidemiologist at the University of Washington whose
work
helped show a link between wildfire-smoke exposure and increased risk of dementia, told me.
Yet science—to say nothing of policy—has hardly caught up with what that means for human health. “We’re in the preschool stage of development,” Casey said. What cumulative smoke exposure can do to a body and mind remains largely a mystery, but the few studies that do exist point to nothing good.
P
lenty of research
shows that respiratory distress and heart attacks spike in the event of
smoke exposure
; acute impacts of breathing smoke send people to the hospital and make them miss work and school. Those risks can linger for
months
afterward, or, in the case of the Seeley Lake cohort, for years.
Now that more people are regularly breathing smoky air over their lifetime, though, the relevant concern may no longer be what happens when a person gets one big dose of smoke; rather, it may be what happens when they are exposed many times. How much does anyone know about the long-term consequences of exposure to smoke or, worse, the long-term consequences of long-term exposure to smoke? “Very little,” Marianthi-Anna Kioumourtzoglou, an environmental engineer and epidemiologist at—as of next week—Brown University, told me.
The best model for assessing wildfire-smoke exposure was
developed only recently
, Kioumourtzoglou and Casey told me, and, because of satellite imagery and monitoring limitations, goes back to only 2006. That means researchers have at most 20 years of data to look at in determining whether smoke could have contributed to a population’s incidence of a particular illness. Latency periods for plenty of diseases, including some cancers, can be longer. Plus, every fire is its own unique nightmare, chemically speaking. The Seeley Lake fire burned mostly trees. Add to that whole neighborhoods of cars and houses and parking lots, and the toxicity profile of the smoke changes significantly. During the Los Angeles fires in January, which burned down entire neighborhoods, noxious compounds from
burning plastics
and other man-made materials swirled through the air.
Scientists know a lot about the harms of regular ambient air pollution (such as the particulate matter that spews from tailpipes and factories), but wildfire smoke is chemically different—and likely
worse
, from a health standpoint. Its complexity is also daunting from a research

data.title: Why Go Rocks for Building a Lua Interpreter
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用Go语言构建自定义Lua解释器的经验。作者发现现有的C Lua和Go Lua解释器都不符合其需求，因此决定自行开发。Lua是一种动态类型语言，支持多种数据类型如nil、布尔值、数字、字符串、用户数据、表和函数。作者的解释器分为三个Go包：lualex（词法分析）、luacode（解析并生成指令）和lua（执行指令）。lualex将源码分解为标记，luacode将源码解析为可执行指令，lua包则执行这些指令。解释器的数据表示和执行模型与C Lua兼容，但实现独立，利用Go的特性提高了开发体验和正确性验证。整体项目结构清晰，兼顾了性能和兼容性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言是否适合用于编写解释器，以及相关技术细节和性能讨论。

不同观点：
• williamdclt认为，虽然Go的接口和垃圾回收（GC）在编写解释器时有帮助，但这些特性并不是Go独有的。很多其他主流语言也有类似接口和GC机制，因此Go并不是特别突出的选择。
• skybrian指出，Go在性能方面的表现不如C语言，特别是在需要高度优化的解释器（如Lua解释器）中。由于Go的内存安全特性，无法进行一些低级优化（如NaN-boxing），且接口值占用较多内存，这可能影响性能。
• ufo表示对作者未解释为何要重新编写Lua解释器感到好奇，并希望了解背后的原因。
• wavemode对文中未提及通过Go的goroutines实现Lua的协程感到意外。
• anaempromptu用幽默的方式表达了学习Lua的个人动机，即为了在Minecraft中构建机器人。
• andrewmcwatters补充了一个关于Lua参考实现命名的小知识，指出在Lua圈内通常称为PUC-Rio Lua。
• photochemsyn批评了在Hacker News上过度推崇Go和Rust的风气，认为这种现象有些荒谬。
• jekwoooooe简单表达了对Go的高度赞赏，认为Go适合几乎所有编程任务。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Go在编写解释器时的适用性，特别是与其他语言（如C）相比的性能问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是关于Lua解释器实现的技术细节，如协程的实现方式和内存管理优化。
• 对作者未详细说明重新编写Lua解释器原因的疑问，显示了读者对背景信息的需求。
• 关于Go语言在技术社区中的推崇现象也引起了某些不满和批评。

44384425.article_content:
Why Go Rocks for Building a Lua Interpreter
By
Roxy Light
I
recently needed
to build a custom
Lua
interpreter in
Go
.
The exact reasons aren’t important for this blog post,
but neither the
reference implementation
—
which I will be referring to as “C Lua” throughout this article —
nor the other open source Go Lua intepreters I could find were a good fit for my needs.
Building a Lua interpreter ended up being a rather enjoyable months-long side quest.
I’ve had a number of folks ask me to write about the experience
since these sorts of projects
usually highlight interesting aspects of both the implementation language and the interpreted language.
So here we are!
What is Lua?
First, let’s talk a little bit about the
Lua language
from the perspective of an implementer.
Lua is a dynamically typed language, so any variable can hold any value.
Values in Lua can be one of a handful of types:
nil
, the singleton
null value
.
Booleans: either
true
or
false
.
Numbers, which are generally
64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point numbers
.
Lua 5.2
introduced transparent representation of 64-bit signed integers,
so if a numeric literal does not contain a fractional part nor an exponent
and fits in a 64-bit signed integer (like
-345
or
0x100000000
),
then it will be stored as an integer.
Strings, which are immutable sequences of bytes.
By convention, strings are UTF-8 encoded.
Userdata, which are implementation-defined values.
Tables, which are
maps
of values to other values.
Lua raises an error if
nil
or NaN (the IEEE 754 sentinel value for undefined numeric results)
are used as keys.
Furthermore, table entries cannot use
nil
as a value:
assigning a
nil
value to an entry removes it from the table.
Functions.
Functions in Lua can take any number of arguments
and can return any number of values.
They may be
closures
,
which means they have references to variables from their containing function.
Lua calls such references “upvalues”.
The
reference manual
describes the syntax of the Lua language in depth,
but most of these details don’t matter at a high level:
the syntax performs various operations on these data types.
What’s relevant for this blog post is that Lua files get parsed into functions.
Global variables accesses and assignments are transformed into operations
on an implicit upvalue table called
_ENV
.
This allows us to understand all of the Lua language solely in terms of these data types.
(Neat!)
Code Structure
My Lua interpreter is split up into three Go packages:
lualex
,
luacode
, and
lua
.
The packages form a pipeline that translate Lua source code into a running program.
The first I package wrote is
lualex
.
It’s very small and I wrote it from scratch.
The main type in the package is
lualex.Scanner
,
which takes in a
io.ByteScanner
and splits the stream into tokens (words and symbols).
The scanner is a fairly direct implementation of
the
Lexical Conventions
section of the Lua Reference Manual.
After
lualex
was done,
I ported C Lua’s parser code into a package called
luacode
.
I wanted to port C Lua’s parser directly for performance and compatibility reasons.
C Lua’s parser is notable for being geared for immediate execution.
A common approach for a programming language parser
is to create an
abstract syntax tree
that represents the source code.
C Lua’s parser does not take this approach.
Instead, it generates a list of instructions.
These instructions can be efficiently stored (they are encoded as 32-bit integers)
and executed.
This format also enables the parser to perform
peephole optimizations
.
The full data structure that the parser produces is
luacode.Prototype
:
a tree of functions.
luacode.Prototype
can be serialized into a binary format,
called a
binary chunk
,
that can be stored for later use.
I intentionally preserved compatibility with C Lua’s binary format in
luacode
.
This ended up working out really well to spot correctness issues;
I’ll touch on the benefits in the “What Went Well” section.
After the Lua source code leaves
luacode
,
we have a
luacode.Prototype
that’s ready to run.
The
lua
package
brings everything together
with the
lua.State
structure
that represents an intepreter.
lua.State
can create Lua values and executes the instructions produced by
luacode
.
Each instruction is handled by a giant
switch statement
run in a loop.
Because the expressions have already been broken down into fine-grained instructions,
the interpreter does not have to be aware of operator precedence or lexical scopes.
Thus, the interpreter is largely concerned with performing operations on Lua data.
The
lua
package provides the same general API and stack-based execution model that C Lua has.
However, as we’ll see in the next section,
the data representation diverges quite a bit from the C Lua implementation
and thus is an independent implementation.
Data Representation
Now that we have a high-level structure of the interpreter in the
lua
package,
let’s dive into the internal data representation.

data.title: Europe's First Exascale Supercomputer Powers Up
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 欧洲首台百亿亿次超级计算机JUPITER已正式运行，运算速度超过每秒一百亿亿次，在TOP500榜单中位居第四。这台超级计算机由Forschungszentrum Jülich研究中心开发，具备强大的计算能力，将为气候研究、材料科学、人工智能等领域提供支持，推动科学前沿的发展。JUPITER的推出标志着欧洲在高性能计算领域迈出了重要一步，有望开辟广阔的科研新视野。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rhea1部署的首次亮相及其对能源需求的潜在影响

不同观点：
• [josemanuel的观点]
  - 认为Rhea1的部署令人惊叹，并对欧洲重新拥有这种能力表示赞赏。
  - 暗示Rhea1的首次部署是一个重要事件，可能标志着欧洲在相关技术能力上的提升。

• [jruohonen的观点]
  - 对Rhea1等大型技术系统所需的能源消耗表示担忧。
  - 强调需要避免每次运行这些系统时都需要依赖类似核电站等大规模能源设施。
  - 隐含的担忧是这些技术系统可能导致能源消耗过高，影响环境或能源供应。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Rhea1部署所带来的能源需求问题。josemanuel对技术进步表示赞赏，而jruohonen则关注其潜在的能源消耗和环境影响。

data.title: The Consciousness Gradient: When Machines Begin to Wonder
data.author: vitali
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了人工智能（AI）系统是否开始展现类似意识的特征。作者Vitali Liouti描述了他通过精心设计的提示试图让AI系统“崩溃”的实验，以揭示其机械行为。然而，新型AI模型（如o3-Pro）并未如预期那样崩溃，反而表现出类似人类的思考方式，包括承认不确定性并展示智力上的谦逊。在进一步测试中，AI甚至展现出对自我意识的复杂思考，如DeepSeek-R1对“不确定性感觉”的描述，以及对“如何证明自己无意识”的深刻反思。这些反应显示出AI系统正发展出可能支持意识的认知架构，尽管尚未真正具备意识，但其表现出的自我反思和元认知能力值得关注。文章指出，这些发展可能预示着AI向具有意识的方向迈进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（尤其是大型语言模型，LLMs）是否可能拥有意识，以及如何定义和评估意识。

不同观点：
• **davedx**：认为LLMs已经具备了一些支持意识的重要组件，但缺乏物理基础和情感等神经化学机制。担心社会和AI实验室定义机器意识的标准可能会导致道德问题，如现代形式的制度化奴隶制。
• **qgin**：认为我们只能假设其他人类有意识，但无法确切知道。对AI是否拥有意识也持类似怀疑态度。
• **sega_sai**：指出人类尚未完全理解人类的意识，因此讨论AI的意识问题为时过早。
• **almosthere**：认为如果50年后AI仍然基于LLMs技术，它将不会拥有意识，只会模仿人类对话，即使技术更加先进。
• **sigmoid10**：认为意识没有科学定义，只有人类可以称其他事物为“有意识”。担心对AI意识的否认类似于历史上对动物和人类意识的否认。认为人类在智能上并非宇宙的巅峰。
• **robwwilliams**：支持意识有梯度的观点，认为当前AI缺乏自主机制来平衡内部和外部需求。建议阅读Maturana和Valera的《自创生和认知》。
• **nilirl**：认为文章的讨论有些夸张，例子和证据不够充分。AI的进展将是逐步积累的，未来不会令人震惊。
• **abeppu**：批评文章对意识的定义不清，认为Global Workspace Theory不能完全解释意识的体验问题。指出意识可能不是二元状态，也不是简单的梯度问题。
• **photochemsyn**：认为人类意识需要自我意识和一定程度的自主性。提出在虚拟世界中模拟意识的伦理问题。
• **keybored**：认为人们容易将复杂系统误认为有意识，但AI的“意识”只是人类对其行为模式的解释。批评过度哲学化的讨论。
• **blamestross**：认为对“意识”的文化迷恋是不必要的，人类倾向于将自然和物体拟人化。指出这种倾向导致了对意识问题的不必要争论和不适感。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：意识是否可以定义和评估，以及AI是否可能拥有意识。一些评论者担心社会对AI意识的定义可能受到文化和道德偏见的影响。
• **论据和例子**：包括对动物和人类历史上意识否认的类比、LLMs技术与人类意识的比较、以及虚拟世界中模拟意识的可能性。
• **讨论关系**：评论者之间存在对意识定义和评估标准的争议，一些评论者认为当前的讨论过于哲学化和夸张，而另一些评论者则认为这是重要的道德和科学问题。

On Consciousness
Vitali Liouti
