data.title: We accidentally solved robotics by watching 1M hours of YouTube
data.author: alexcos
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了通过观看100万小时的YouTube视频意外解决了机器人技术的问题。传统的语言模型（如Behemoth）尽管在语言处理上非常强大，但在实际物理操作上表现不佳。研究发现，机器人需要理解物理而非语言。为此，V-JEPA 2模型通过预测视频中的下一个时刻来学习物理运动，而不是预测下一个词。该模型使用了一个10亿参数的ViT-g编码器来理解视频本质，并通过掩码策略填补视频中的缺失部分。模型训练数据从2百万个视频扩展到22百万个视频和1百万张图片，并采用了渐进分辨率训练方法。最终，V-JEPA 2-AC通过理解可操作的物理实现了机器人控制，并在不同实验室环境中展示了零样本泛化能力，成功率在特定任务中达到65-100%。

主要讨论点：对文章内容及相关研究的评价与争议

不同观点：

• [dimatura] 指出文章中提到的利用YouTube数据的想法在机器人学界早已有之，并举例2023年的相关研究。虽然使用YouTube作为数据源是个合理的思路，但如何实现才是关键和难点。
• [canyp] 质疑仅通过视觉学习物理概念的模型，认为空间意识不仅仅依赖视觉，例如后空翻和接飞盘等活动涉及到更多的感知能力。
• [imranq] 表示文章难读，建议增加更清晰的解释和结构，以帮助理解。
• [Voloskaya] 批评文章包含许多谬误和历史改写，阅读体验痛苦。

• [rzzzt] 提供了一个有趣的单位转换，增加了一些轻松的讨论气氛。

44414171.article_content:
how we accidentally solved robotics by watching 1 million hours of YouTube
29 Jun, 2025
the existential crisis we all share
imagine
this: you've just spent $640 billion training the chonkiest language model known to humanity (lol) and decide to call it "Behemoth". it can annoy you on whatsapp, try to solve calculus, and argue with you about anything with a sophistication of a philosophy PhD.
but ask it to grab a coffee mug from your kitchen counter? ngmi
turns out scaling LLMs forever still leaves robots as clueless. internet-scale language misses the fundamental physics of
stuff actually moving around in 3D space
. and no amount of "think step by step" or COT prompting helps to teach your chatterbox where the trash is in the kitchen
but if i told you that the solution was hiding in plain sight? what if the secret sauce wasn't more tokens, but more...
videos
?
the "why didn't we think of this sooner" moment
here's the thing everyone forgot while we were busy making ai agents book flight tickets:
robots need to understand physics, not language
.
so enter V-JEPA 2, which basically said "hey, what if we fed a neural network 1 million hours of youtube and taught it to predict what happens next?" except instead of predicting the next word, it predicts the next
moment in reality
.
this is "deploy a robot in a completely new lab and watch it successfully pick up objects it's never seen before" level of real.
the beauty under the hood
the core insight:
predict in representation space, not pixels
remember when everyone was obsessed with making AI generate pretty pictures? well, V-JEPA 2 said "screw
noise
" and decided to predict in
latent space
instead (i know this word is thrown around alot but bear with me)
why? because trying to predict every pixel is like trying to predict every blade of grass in a field when what you really care about is whether the ball is going in the goal.
the magic happens in three parts:
the encoder
: a ViT-g with 1 billion parameters that looks at video and goes "ah yes, i understand the essence of this physical situation"
the predictor
: a smaller nn that takes masked video tokens and tries to fill in the blanks, like the a sophisticated game of video madlibs
3D-RoPE
: because regular position embeddings are for 2D peasants
the masking strategy
instead of showing the model everything, V-JEPA 2 randomly masks out chunks of video (called "tubelets" - yes, that's the technical term). the model then has to predict what's happening in those missing pieces.
data scaling: from "some videos" to "all the videos"
before
: 2 million videos (cute)
after
: 22 million videos + 1 million images (now we're talking)
they basically hoovered up everything: something-something v2, kinetics, howto100m, and a billion youtube videos
model scaling: bigger is better (sometimes)
they scaled from 300M to 1B parameters because apparently size does matter. the ViT-g encoder is basically the endgame of vision transformers.
progressive resolution training: the "boiling frog" approach
here's the clever bit: instead of immediately training on massive high-res videos (which would require selling a kidney to afford the compute), they started small and gradually cranked up the resolution during training.
(curriculum learning bros keep on winning)
16 frames at 256² → 64 frames at 384²
V-JEPA 2-AC: my favourite bit
having a world model that understands physics is cool, but robots need to understand
actionable
physics. like "if i move my arm this way, what happens to the world?" and the dynamics behind this action
so they took the pretrained V-JEPA 2, froze it solid, and attached a 300M parameter transformer that learns to predict what happens when you actually
do
stuff. (a model that can just do stuff, hell yeah)
the training data?
just
62 hours of robot videos. not "successful robot videos" or "carefully curated robot videos." just raw footage of a franka arm doing franka arm things, successes and failures included. really interesting bit, alot of future work to do expirements with good data curation and win/lose ratio.
the magic of energy minimization
when it's time to actually control a robot, V-JEPA 2-AC plays a game of "hot and cold":
look at current state
look at goal state
imagine a bunch of possible action sequences
pick the one that gets you closest to the goal
execute first action
repeat until done (or until something breaks)
model predictive control on world model is one of the coolest things this paper has done
zero-shot generalization (aka the money shot)
they took this model, trained entirely on one dataset, and deployed it on franka arms in completely different labs. different lighting, different objects, different everything.
success rates:
reach: 100% (because apparently moving to a point in space is trivial when you understand physics)
grasp cup: 65% (cups are apparently hard)
pick and place: 65-80% (depending on object complexity)
compare this to baseline approaches that basically failed at everything exce

data.title: Commodore acquired for a 'low seven figure' price – CEO from retro community
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: YouTube主播Christian 'Peri Fratic' Simpson自称成为Commodore公司的新任CEO，并透露已达成一项七位数的收购协议，价值约100万至500万美元。他计划重振这一经典品牌，并集结了多位前Commodore知名人物，如Bill Herd和Albert Charpentier，来协助复兴。尽管已投入大量资金，但仍在寻找天使投资人来支持新项目。Peri Fratic还预告了一款即将发布的新硬件，预计两周后揭晓。尽管有人质疑新Commodore是否能重现昔日辉煌，但他辩称通过恢复商标、招募原班人马等方式，正在努力使其名副其实。

44417417.article_content:
(Image credit: Peri Fractic on YouTube)
YouTube’s Christian ‘Peri Fratic’ Simpson claims to be “the acting CEO of Commodore Corporation.” The
surprise Commodore buyout deal
hinted at three weeks prior, seems to have been put into motion. In a new episode on the rebranded Retro Recipes x Commodore channel, Peri Fratic provides details of the seven-figure deal, outlines his vision for the company, and lists a growing number of ex-Commodore luminaries who will be joining him to relaunch the beloved brand. Last and definitely not least, the video ends in a signature tease – this time it’s a tease for new hardware.
Wait… Who’s the New CEO of Commodore?! • Let's Buy Commodore Part 2 - YouTube
Watch On
Finance still not certain
Concerning the deal, a key point from the above video is that Peri Fratic “signed a share purchase agreement” with the previous owners of Commodore Corporation. It has been agreed that a price “in the low seven figures” will be paid to seal the deal. That should mean the deal is worth somewhere between $1m and $5m.
(Image credit: Peri Fractic on YouTube)
Apparently many backers of this project, including Peri Fratic, have already put in lots of cash to make this buyout happen, taking out second mortgages, selling the family silver, etc. However, the search is still on for angel investors to launch the new ship. Lots of details and discussion about funding are provided, but left us wondering what would happen if not enough suitable investors come forward, and what kind of timescale needs to be adhered to, to finalize the contract?
You may like

First reverse engineered Sony PS1 motherboard enables fixing broken systems
Rare Steam Deck prototype sold for $2,000 on eBay — Features a 6-year-old AMD Picasso APU with Zen+ and Vega
Some big names from Commodore’s history sign up
With this agreement in place, the new Commodore has already got a new slogan. It will go forward with its ‘Retro Futurism’ plans, “honoring our past, innovating the future.” Furthermore, Perifrantic has been busy appointing (acting) CEO, CFO, COO, and many more key positions – many of whom honor the past.
Some big names that will play a part in the new future Commodore include, in order of mention: Bill Herd (Commodore Pioneer), Albert Charpentier (Father of the
C64
), Michael Tomczyk (Vic Tzar of the Vic 20), James Harrison (Tech support manager), David Pleasance (ex VP becomes Heritage and legacy advisor), Hans Olsen (demo and convention facilitator), Tim Morgan (PR officer), and more.
Image
1
of
2
(Image credit: Peri Fractic on YouTube)
(Image credit: Peri Fractic on YouTube)
Not the real Commodore?
Perifrantic makes an interesting point in anticipation of critics that will chime in to assert “this will never be the original Commodore.” In his defense, the retro tech enthusiast says “what if we got 47 trademarks from 1982, or original Commodore engineers back, original executives, assistants, ROMs,
Amiga
? I mean, at some point, it does start to become the real Commodore, right?”
Also in the FAQ section of the video we get a rendition of the aims of the new Commodore sans corporate-speak. It will exist to “streamline the usage of the brand and logo, along with releasing some of our own products,” it is stated.

As well as the financial backing, which is still not guaranteed, Peri Fratic is seeking other talented folk. Specifically, merchandise designers, social media manager, and anyone who owns a license from a classic 1980s or 90s game should get in touch with the new (acting) Commodore CEO.
New Commodore launch project teaser
We are left with a cliffhanger with regard to the new ‘Commodore ____’. The video cuts out to an unpacking/loading type screen before Peri Fratic can hoist the new device from his lap into view. That announcement seems to be 20,160 minutes away (as of yesterday), which indicates a wait of two weeks.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章是斯科特·阿伦森对量子计算先驱雷蒙德·拉弗拉姆的悼念，强调了他对量子计算领域的重大贡献以及对其英年早逝的悲痛。拉弗拉姆早期与斯蒂芬·霍金合作，在宇宙学和量子容错计算方面有重要影响，特别是他与合作者提出的KLM定理，为光学量子计算奠定了基础，影响了PsiQuantum和Xanadu等公司的创立。阿伦森还提到KLM定理对计算复杂性理论的意外贡献。文章最后表达了对拉弗拉姆的深切怀念，以及他对科学界和个人职业生涯的重大影响。

44393657.article_content:
Shtetl-Optimized
The Blog of Scott Aaronson
If you take nothing else from this blog: quantum computers won't
solve hard problems instantly by just trying all solutions in parallel.
Also, please read Zvi Mowshowitz's masterpiece on how to fix K-12 education!
«
Trump and Iran, by popular request
BusyBeaver(6) is really quite large
»
Raymond Laflamme (1960-2025)
Even with everything happening in the Middle East right now, even with (relatedly) everything happening in my own family (my wife and son sheltering in Tel Aviv as Iranian missiles rained down), even with all the rather ill-timed travel I’ve found myself doing as these events unfolded (Ecuador and the Galapagos and now
STOC’2025
in Prague) … there’s been
another
thing, a huge one, weighing on my soul.
Ray Laflamme
played a major role in launching the whole field of quantum computing and information, and also a major role in launching my own career.  The world has lost him too soon.
I’ve
lost him too soon.
After growing up in Quebec—I still hear his French-Canadian accent, constantly on the verge of laughter, as I’m writing this—Ray went into physics and became a PhD student of Stephen Hawking.  No, not a different Stephen Hawking.  If you’ve read or watched anything by or about Hawking, including
A Brief History of Time
, you might remember the story where Hawking believed for a while that time would reverse itself as the universe contracted in a Big Crunch, with omelettes unscrambling themselves, old people turning into children, etc. etc., but then two graduate students persuaded him that that was totally wrong, and entropy would continue to increase like normal.  Anyway, Ray was one of those students (Don Page was the other).  I’d always meant to ask Ray to explain what argument changed Hawking’s mind, since the idea of entropy decreasing during contraction just seemed
obviously
wrong to me!  Only today, while writing this post, did I find a
1993 paper
by Hawking, Laflamme, and Lyons that explains the matter perfectly clearly, including three fallacious intuitions that Hawking had previously held.  (Even though, as they comment, “the anatomy of error is not ruled by logic.”)
Anyway, in the mid-1990s, starting at Los Alamos National Lab and continuing at the University of Waterloo, Ray became a pioneer of the then-new field of quantum computing and information.  In 1997, he was a coauthor of one of the
seminal original papers
that proved the possibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation with a constant error rate, what we now call the
Threshold Theorem
(Aharonov and Ben-Or had such a result independently).  He made lots of other key early contributions to the theory of quantum error-correcting codes and fault-tolerance.
When it comes to Ray’s scientific achievements
after
his cosmology work with Hawking and
after
quantum fault-tolerance—well, there are
many
, but let me talk about two.  Perhaps the biggest is the
KLM (Knill-Laflamme-Milburn) Theorem
.  It would be fair to say that KLM started the entire field of optical or photonic quantum computation, as it’s existed in the 21
st
century.  In one sentence, what KLM showed is that it’s possible to build a universal quantum computer using only
identical single-photon states,
a network of “linear-optical elements” (that is, beamsplitters and phaseshifters) that the photons travel through, and
feedforward measurements—that is, measurements of an optical mode that tell you how many photons are there, in such a way that you can
condition
(using a classical computer) which optical elements to apply next on the outcome of the measurement.
All of a sudden, there was a viable path to building a quantum computer out of photons, where you
wouldn’t
need to get pairs of photons to interact with each other, which had previously been the central sticking point.  The key insight was that feedforward measurements, combined with the statistical properties of identical bosons (what the photons are), are enough to
simulate
the effect of two-photon interactions.
Have you heard of
PsiQuantum
, the startup in Palo Alto with a $6 billion valuation and hundreds of employees that’s right now trying to build an optical quantum computer with a million qubits?  Or
Xanadu
, its competitor in Toronto?  These, in some sense, are companies that grew out of a theorem: specifically the KLM Theorem.
For me, though, the significance of KLM goes beyond the practical. In 2011, I used the KLM Theorem, together with the fact (known since the 1950s) that photonic amplitudes are the
permanents
of matrices, to give a
new proof
of Leslie Valiant’s celebrated 1979 theorem that calculating the permanent is a #P-complete problem. Thus, as I pointed out in a talk two years ago at Ray’s COVID-delayed 60
th
birthday conference, entitled
Ray Laflamme, Complexity Theorist (?!)
, KLM had said something new about computational complexity, without any intention of doing so.  More generally, KLM was crucial backdrop to my and Alex Arkhipov’s later work

data.title: Reverse Engineering the Microchip CLB
data.author: _Microft
data.article_summary: Microchip在新推出的PIC16F13145微控制器系列中加入了一个名为配置逻辑块（CLB）的外设，它类似于一个小型FPGA（32个查找表），可与芯片内部连接。然而，官方并未提供如何自行配置CLB的文档，仅推荐使用在线配置工具。CLB不作为特殊功能寄存器（SFR）出现在寄存器映射中，也无法直接访问，只能通过支持CLB编程的开发环境（如Microchip的MPLAB® IDE）进行配置。作者决定自行逆向工程CLB，并分为三个部分介绍：背景与逆向工程、硬件测试、以及动手尝试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Microchip CLB（可配置逻辑块）的应用和特性分析

不同观点：
• **Kragen**：Kragen总体上对Microchip的CLB持积极态度，认为快速、确定性的数字逻辑与微控制器的灵活性有很强的协同作用。他指出CLB可以减少查阅繁杂的寄存器和外围设备文档的麻烦，并提到RP2040的pioasm协处理器是类似问题的另一种解决方案。不过，Kragen对Microchip没有利用CLB来替代硬连线外设（如SPI、I²C等）表示失望。他还分析了CLB的延迟性能，认为虽然比一些CMOS逻辑器件慢，但仍比微控制器的中断处理和指令执行速度快得多。

• **RicoElectrico**：RicoElectrico对Microchip没有提供CLB的手动配置文档表示不满，认为依赖在线配置工具是“SaaS-ification”的过度渗透，甚至影响了保守的嵌入式市场。他对这种缺乏自主配置信息的做法表示强烈反对。

• **throwaway81523**：throwaway81523希望看到CLB的实际应用示例，并对CLB只有32个LUT（查找表）的配置表示质疑，认为至少应该有几百个LUT才能实现更有意义的应用，如构建专门的SERDES（串行解串器）。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节争议**：Kragen对CLB的延迟性能与不同器件的对比分析，提供了具体的技术数据支持（如232ns的传播延迟，7.5ns每BLE的延迟等），显示了对硬件性能的深入关注。

• **配置工具的争议**：RicoElectrico对配置工具的批评引发了对嵌入式市场SaaS趋势的更广泛讨论，表明对工具链和文档开放性的关注。

• **应用范围的讨论**：throwaway81523对LUT数量的质疑和对具体应用示例的需求，提出了CLB在实际应用中的潜力和局限性问题。

44416589.article_content:
Microchip added a
very cool peripheral
called the Configurable Logic Block (CLB) to there
new
PIC16F13145
microcontroller family. It’s
essentially a small FPGA
(32 LUTs) that can connect to the internals of the chip.
However, they
don’t document how to configure it yourself
, only referring you to their online
configurator
tool
that submits jobs to an API that places and routes to LUTs.
The [CLB] Interface does not appear as an SFR in the Register Map and is
not directly user-accessible
;
it is accessible
only through a programming system
such as Microchip MPLAB® Integrated Development Environment
(IDE) that supports programming the CLB.
-
PIC16F13145 Datasheet
So I decided to reverse engineer it myself!
Broken into 3 parts:
Background and Reverse Engineering
Hardware Testing
Try it Yourself!

data.author: not-matthias
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者对反作弊系统（特别是EasyAntiCheat）更新追踪的研究。EasyAntiCheat在被Epic Games收购前后，通过不同CDN分发更新，更新URL结构有所变化。作者通过逆向工程和二进制分析，研究如何解密其更新模块，找到解密算法并将加密数据转换为PE文件。然而，该文件还被VMProtect保护，进一步分析需要脱壳。文章概述了作者的研究过程和发现，包括对不同反作弊系统的更新追踪方法的总结。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏反作弊系统的有效性、安全性及其实现方式

不同观点：
• [nulld3v] 提到BattleEye反作弊系统存在严重漏洞，黑客可以利用该漏洞随意永久封禁任何玩家。这引发了对反作弊系统安全性的质疑，并提出为什么还信任这些系统的疑问。
• [rak] 通过引用ESEA的例子指出，反作弊客户端曾经包含比特币挖矿程序，揭示了反作弊系统可能存在的其他不当行为。
• [nichochar] 认为CSGO的反作弊系统比其他游戏更为先进，可能是因为竞争场景的需求，但也提到对Faceit和ESEA缺乏讨论。
• [varun_ch] 提出游戏开发者应限制客户端可访问的数据量，将更多操作放在服务器端验证，以减少作弊的可能性，并讨论了这种方法的成本和可行性。
• [PeterStuer] 抱怨Vanguard反作弊系统在非标准游戏设置下的不稳定性，如多显示器和Hyper-V环境。
• [bpbp-mango] 对Valorant的内核级反作弊技术感到过于侵入，表达了对隐私和系统安全的担忧。

补充讨论：
• [butz] 质疑内核级反作弊技术是否即将过时，提到Crowdstrike曾经发生的事故，暗示技术发展的方向可能在改变。
• [preciousoo] 认为一些高级反作弊系统提供了人性化的信息包，并指出Riot游戏的反作弊措施较为有效。
• [ibaikov] 和 [fisian] 偏离主题，讨论了网站设计的字体和代码字体，显示出对技术细节的关注。
• [sylware] 和 [b8] 提到反作弊系统在不同平台的兼容性和版本对比，涉及到技术实现和用户体验的问题。
• [chaoz_] 指出FACEIT反作弊系统的影响力，并质疑Valve为何无法复制其成功，认为Valve可能为了不流失用户而选择不增加安装难度。

争议焦点：
• 内核级反作弊技术的侵入性和有效性之间的平衡。
• 反作弊系统的安全漏洞与开发者信任问题。
• 客户端数据限制与服务器验证之间的技术和经济考量。
• 不同反作弊系统（如BattleEye、Vanguard、FACEIT）的优劣对比。

44416421.article_content:
Tracking Anticheat Updates
Posted on
2025-06-26
::
8
Min Read
::
anticheat
security
A few years ago when I was into reverse engineering and binary analysis (and game modding), I did a lot of research into anticheats work. I was curious about tracking their updates, since that would allow me to:
Know when a new version is released
Understand what changes were made
Use older versions for research purposes
So I ended up researching different ways on how to track updates of various anticheats. Some of them are already very well documented, while others haven't been explored much. This post will summarize my findings and outline how they work.
EasyAntiCheat
EasyAntiCheat is widely recognized as one of the most advanced anticheats, and is used in many popular games like Rust, Fortnite, Apex Legends, and more.
Prior to the acquisition by Epic Games, EAC was using their own CDN to distribute updates:
https://download.eac-cdn.com/api/v1/games/{game_id}/client/{system}/download/?uuid=1239688
.
game_id
: unique identifier for each game (e.g. 154 for Apex Legends)
system
: target platform/system (e.g.
wow64_win64
,
mac64
,
linux32_64
).
After the acquisition, they switched to the EpicGames CDN, which has a slightly different URL structure:
https://modules-cdn.eac-prod.on.epicgames.com/modules/{product_id}/{deployment_id}/{system}
. The parameters to this URL are completely different:
product_id
: unique identifier for each game (e.g.
429c2212ad284866aee071454c2125b5
for Rust)
deployment_id
: unique identifier for each deployment (e.g.
76796531e86443548754600511f42e9e
for Rust). This doesn't change when an update is released and is used to identify different game versions.
system
: same as in the old CDN
After downloading the module for a game, we'll have a file which contains data with a very high entropy which is the first indication that it is encrypted or compressed:
$ bat encrypted.bin | ent
Entropy = 7.989390 bits per byte.
Looking at the data, we also can't really identify any patterns or strings. However, across versions the header seems to always stay the same (
a7 ed
): Very interesting 🤔
$ hexyl encrypted.bin | head
┌────────┬─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬────────┬────────┐
│00000000│ a7 ed 96 0c 0f 0f 12 19 ┊ 1c 1b 1e 20 22 26 2a e5 │×××_••••┊••• "&*×│
│00000010│ e8 33 36 39 3c 3f 42 85 ┊ 88 4b 4e 51 54 57 5a 5d │×369<?B×┊×KNQTWZ]│
│00000020│ 60 63 66 69 6c 6f 72 75 ┊ 78 7b 7e 81 84 87 8a 8d │`cfiloru┊x{~×××××│
│00000030│ 90 93 96 99 9c 9f a2 a5 ┊ a8 ab ae 31 34 b7 ba cb │××××××××┊×××14×××│
│00000040│ ed 9c 8e d7 80 8c a8 c3 ┊ b1 94 2b fa d2 5c a6 be │××××××××┊××+××\××│
│00000050│ cc 86 86 db dd d5 db d8 ┊ d6 98 91 d5 e3 f3 f7 00 │××××××××┊×××××××⋄│
│00000060│ b4 a5 ed ae be 16 15 c3 ┊ c1 12 cc a5 d7 e9 bd da │×××××••×┊×•××××××│
│00000070│ 2c 26 1f ec 97 79 79 93 ┊ 8c 6b 6e 71 74 77 7a cd │,&•××yy×┊×knqtwz×│
│00000080│ 15 c8 86 d5 d9 93 95 c9 ┊ 4d 6e 58 09 a4 a7 aa ad │•×××××××┊MnX_××××│
A few years ago, I spent a
night
early morning with a friend to find the decryption algorithm. We searched for anything that closely resembled such an algorithm, eventually found it, made a quick POC and got it working 🔥. Here's what the code looks like:
void
decode
(
char
*
memory_block
,
int
total_size
)
{
char
*
buffer
=
(
char
*
)
memory_block
;
int
file_size
=
total_size
;
if
(
file_size
>=
2
)
{
buffer
[
file_size
-
1
]
+=
3
-
3
*
file_size
;
int
current_index
=
file_size
-
2
;
if
(
file_size
!=
2
)
{
do
{
buffer
[
current_index
]
+=
-
3
*
current_index
-
buffer
[
current_index
+
1
]
;
--
current_index
;
}
while
(
current_index
)
;
}
buffer
[
0
]
-=
buffer
[
1
]
;
}
}
After decrypting the binary blob, we'll finally have a PE image (
EasyAnticheat.packed.dll
):
$ hexyl EasyAnticheat.packed.dll | head
┌────────┬─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬────────┬────────┐
│00000000│ 4d 5a 90 00 03 00 00 00 ┊ 04 00 00 00 ff ff 00 00 │MZ×.•...┊•...××..│
│00000010│ b8 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 ┊ 40 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 │×.......┊@.......│
│00000020│ 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 ┊ 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 │........┊........│
│00000030│ 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 ┊ 00 00 00 00 80 00 00 00 │........┊....×...│
│00000040│ 0e 1f ba 0e 00 b4 09 cd ┊ 21 b8 01 4c cd 21 54 68 │••×•.×_×┊!×•L×!Th│
│00000050│ 69 73 20 70 72 6f 67 72 ┊ 61 6d 20 63 61 6e 6e 6f │is progr┊am canno│
│00000060│ 74 20 62 65 20 72 75 6e ┊ 20 69 6e 20 44 4f 53 20 │t be run┊ in DOS │
│00000070│ 6d 6f 64 65 2e 0d 0d 0a ┊ 24 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 │mode.___┊$.......│
│00000080│ 50 45 00 00 4c 01 03 00 ┊ 34 81 52 68 00 00 00 00 │PE..L••.┊4×Rh....│
Unfortunately, we're not yet done. According to
Detect it Easy
, the binary is protected with VMProtect, which means we can't just read the
.text
or
.data
section. However, to further analyze the binary and extract the driver and usermode module we'll have to find a way to unpack it.

emulation
and
native execution
. Both methods just execute

data.title: ZeroRISC Gets $10M Funding, Says Open-Source Silicon Security Inevitable
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放源代码硅芯片和根信任（Root of Trust, RoT）技术的进展及其应用

不同观点：
• [kaszanka] 对开放源代码硅芯片持怀疑态度。他认为，即使芯片的部分设计是开源的，当像麦当劳这样的应用因为设备不被认为是“可信赖的”而无法运行时，开源的RTL（寄存器传输级）设计并不能带来实质性的安慰。他讽刺地建议将相关技术改名为带有“Open”字样的名称，以反映其开放性。
• [transpute] 对开放源代码硅芯片和开放固件持积极态度。他引用了Google和lowRISC的项目，强调了OpenTitan和Caliptra项目在2025年将为Chromebook和服务器带来的根信任能力，并提到微软基于Ibex CPU核心开发的CHERIoT-Ibex设计，认为2025年将是开放源代码硅和开放固件根信任的一年。
• [tonetegeatinst] 对“开放硅”的定义提出疑问。他想知道这是否仅仅意味着设计规格和库是开源的，还是意味着可以自由进行芯片攻击研究而不必担心法律诉讼。
• [snvzz] 对RISC-V持批评态度，认为其遵循了RISC-V的市场营销手册，暗示其开放性可能更多是市场营销策略而非实际技术优势。

补充讨论：
• 开放源代码硅芯片的实际应用和其在提高设备安全性方面的有效性是讨论的重点。
• 不同的观点反映了业界对开放源代码硬件的复杂态度，有人质疑其实际效果，有人则对其未来充满希望。
• 具体项目如OpenTitan和Caliptra的进展被用来支持对开放硅未来发展的积极预期。
• 法律和安全性问题也被提及，特别是在进行芯片攻击研究时的法律风险。

• [tonetegeatinst] 对“开放硅”的定义提出疑问。他想知道这是否仅仅意味着设计规格和库是开源的，还是意味着可以自由进行芯片攻击研究而不必担心法律诉讼。
• [snvzz] 对RISC-V持批评态度，认为其遵循了RISC-V的市场营销手册，暗示其开放性可能更多是市场营销策略而非实际技术优势。

补充讨论：
• 开放源代码硅芯片的实际应用和其在提高设备安全性方面的有效性是讨论的重点。
• 不同的观点反映了业界对开放源代码硬件的复杂态度，有人质疑其实际效果，有人则对其未来充满希望。
• 具体项目如OpenTitan和Caliptra的进展被用来支持对开放硅未来发展的积极预期。

Honda Joins Space Race By Launching Successful Reusable Rocket
By
Peter Lyon

Contributor.
Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights.
Peter Lyon is based in Tokyo and writes about the car industry.

Honda's reusable rocket blasts off in northern Japan.
Photo by Honda
Honda is well-known in industry circles as one of the few carmakers who produces a multitude of non-car products including motorcycles, ATVs, power equipment such as generators, lawnmowers, outboard motors and snowploughs, the HondaJet and
robots such as ASIMO
. Now it’s entered rocket research and development in earnest.
Japan’s second-biggest carmaker has just successfully conducted a launch and landing test of its experimental reusable rocket in northern Japan. And given that Elon Musk’s SpaceX has just recorded its fourth failed rocket launch in a row, they will no doubt be paying attention to how Honda approaches its launches.
Honda's rocket climbed to 890 feet before landing just 15 inches away from where it took off.
Photo by Honda
Honda’s rocket flew for 57 seconds and then landed
At Honda’s test facility in Taiki Town located in Hokkaido, Japan’s northern-most island, the company launched a
reusable rocket
that flew for almost a minute to an altitude of 890 feet and then landed with pinpoint accuracy just 15 inches from where it took off, according to Honda.
The rocket weighs 2800 lbs which equates to a small car.
Photo by Honda
MORE FOR YOU
Honda is creating its own ‘space town’
Developed in-house by Honda R&D Company, the rocket—which weighs 2800 lbs or around the same weight as a small car—shot up vertically, blasting off using its four legs from the company’s test site in the northern island of Hokkaido.
Honda says its Hokkaido facility “has been developing itself as a ‘space town’ through the joint efforts of public and private sectors,” including the
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
(JAXA). The 21-foot high rocket, ascended for 57 seconds before landing around 15 inches from the target touchdown point using its four retractable legs that also aided in its take-off.
Honda first revealed its goal to go into space in late 2021. But while the carmaker has been tight-lipped about its R&D progress, it is using existing technology from other areas, such as automated driving systems, to assist in the development of its first reusable rocket.
The company says that the reason for developing its own launch system is the need for more satellites that will potentially benefit its other businesses.
According to Honda, its rocket research is still in its infancy, and no decisions have yet been made on potential commercialization of these rocket technologies. The company has the ambitious goal to enable a suborbital launch by 2029 but success here will require significant testing and perhaps a few failures.
A suborbital flight – upwards of 62 miles above sea level – would be a significant achievement for Honda, even though that is not far enough to put a satellite into orbit. It will be interesting to see if Honda goes all the way, and ends up competing with other private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin that are capable of conducting orbital flights.

data.title: Zero Trust for Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)
data.author: pranay01
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了**ZTB（Zero Trust BYOC）**模型，旨在为"自带云"（BYOC）环境提供零信任安全框架。BYOC模型让企业能够在客户的云环境中部署平台，满足隐私、控制或合规要求。然而，构建安全的BYOC模型面临诸多挑战，尤其是在身份验证和客户基础设施隔离方面。文章指出，当前缺乏对零信任BYOC模型的明确定义，因此提出了**ZTB**概念。

**ZTB**基于零信任原则，涵盖以下核心原则：
1. **数据平面隔离**：客户数据必须留在其云环境中，元数据仅在明确许可下共享。
2. **控制平面拉取通信**：客户环境必须主动发起与供应商的通信，供应商不得主动连接客户环境。
3. **组件级零信任**：BYOC中的所有组件必须相互验证和授权，不得隐式信任。
4. **最小权限访问**：所有访问必须遵循最小权限原则，并设置时间限制。

这些原则确保数据主权、减少安全风险，并简化合规性管理。ZTB旨在为BYOC模型提供一个明确、可操作的安全框架，类似于零信任网络在网络安全中的作用。

Introducing ZTB - Defining Zero Trust for Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)
Author:
Pavankalyan Chiluka
Isn’t the "Bring Your Own Cloud" (BYOC) model the latest hot topic in the evolution of cloud-native architecture, especially for companies offering cloud-hosted platforms that must be deployed in the customer’s cloud for privacy, control, or compliance reasons?
Over the past few weeks, we have been rigorously researching and discussing how to build a secure BYOC model. And it hasn’t been easy since the journey was filled with nuanced architectural decisions from handling identity propagation to isolating customer infrastructure. Somewhere in the middle of these technical trenches, a recurring question kept bothering us:
Is there a guideline for what a secure BYOC should be like?
This question led us to research how different companies approached BYOC, not just technically, but also how they talk about security. As we started digging into best practices for BYOC setups, we began to see a curious pattern. A pattern that we are much aware of in the field of Security, called as Zero-Trust.
Various companies follow the guidelines of Zero Trust loosely in their BYOC offerings. We mapped these against the core principles of Zero Trust security itself. And finally, we started seeing the gap —
no one
had a concrete, actionable definition of what a
Zero Trust BYOC (ZTB)/Secure BYOC
model is.
So We Decided to Define what Zero Trust BYOC is
Just like the Zero Trust Network (ZTN) became a standard way to reimagine network security, we believe BYOC needs a clear, opinionated model rooted in Zero Trust principles. We’re calling this:
ZTB
—
Zero Trust BYOC
.
What Does Zero Trust Mean?
Before jumping ahead to our definition for
ZTB
—
Zero Trust BYOC. Let’s talk about Zero Trust
Zero Trust is more than a buzzword — it’s a mindset shift in how we approach access, trust boundaries, and security guarantees. Originally coined to counteract the failures of perimeter-based security, the
Zero Trust Security Model
follows a simple premise:
Never trust, always verify.
In traditional systems, if a service is on the network, it’s trusted. In a Zero Trust model:
Every interaction is authenticated and authorised.
No implicit trust is granted based on location (e.g., being on the same VPC).
Security policies are identity-aware and context-sensitive.
Data sovereignty and access control boundaries are always enforced.
In the networking world, this led to
Zero Trust Networks (ZTNs)
where east-west traffic is authenticated and encrypted, identities are workload-bound, and policies are centrally enforced, not implied by IPs or firewalls.
Now, we're bringing that same rigour and discipline to
Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)
architectures.
What Makes a BYOC Model Zero Trust?
If Zero Trust means no implicit trust between networked entities, and enforcement based on strong identity and verification, then a
Zero Trust BYOC (ZTB)
model must enforce the same principles
across all layers
of the deployment: networking, identity, access, audit, and data control.
We believe the following principles must be present for a BYOC deployment to qualify as “Zero Trust”:
Principle 1: Data Plane Isolation
The customer’s data and compute
MUST
stay entirely within their cloud account. No customer data leaves the customer's cloud environment. Optionally, Metadata or telemetry (anonymised or synthetic) can be shared with the vendor’s control plane with explicit opt-in.
WHY
:
Following this preserves
data sovereignty
and makes compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and financial regulations easier. Minimises the blast radius in case of a control plane compromise. Reduces vendor liability and builds customer trust.
Principle 2: Pull-Based Control Plane Communication
The customer environment
MUST
initiate any communication with the vendor — never the other way around. Vendor control plane
SHOULD NEVER
initiate inbound connections to the customer’s environment.
WHY
:
Following this prevents vendor-initiated access to customer environments and aligns with Zero Trust Network principles, where
access is granted, not assumed
. This also simplifies network boundary enforcement (e.g., no need to open ingress rules).
Principle 3: Component-Level Zero Trust
No component within the BYOC deployment implicitly trusts another just because it’s on the same network or cluster. All internal services
MUST
authenticate and authorise each other, using signed identities (e.g. JWTs, IAM roles).
WHY
:
This blocks lateral movement in case of compromise and follows the Zero Trust principle, where no components trust each other. Enforces strong access boundaries even within a single customer deployment.
Principle 4: Least Privilege Access
Every system, user, and automation
MUST
have only the minimal access required, for only as long as needed. IAM roles
MUST
be scoped, the token
SHOULD BE
time-limited, and RBAC policies
MUST
be enforced in Kubernetes.

data.title: Earth is trapping much more heat than climate models forecast
data.author: GeoAtreides
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论地球能量收支的不平衡加剧，导致气候变化可能加速。研究发现，过去20年中，地球吸收的热量与散发的热量之间的不平衡翻了一倍多，从约0.6瓦特每平方米增加到约1.3瓦特每平方米。尽管大部分额外热量（约90%）被海洋吸收，但地表温度已上升1.3-1.5°C。这种变化速度超过了气候模型的预测，可能与云层变化有关，例如反射性白云减少、反射性较差的云增加。文章还提到，监测这些变化的资金不确定性可能影响未来的跟踪能力。这一能量失衡表明，气候变化在未来几年可能加速恶化。

主要讨论点：气候变化的原因及其应对措施

不同观点：
• [bmacho] 认为气候变化的原因尚未完全解释清楚，并引用新研究指出云层变化是重要因素。具体而言，云层覆盖中高反射的白色云减少，而反射性较差的云增多，可能与2020年后航运燃料中硫含量减少有关。此外，他以讽刺语气提出通过释放某种气体即可解决气候问题，暗示对气候变化应对的简单化看法。

• [vardump] 强调应严肃对待气候科学，并指出气候科学与政治无关。他似乎对一些人轻视气候问题的态度感到不满，呼吁更认真地对待科学研究。

• [vivzkestrel] 提出一个假设性问题，询问如果全球人口一夜之间全部转为素食，是否能减少60%的排放。这表明他/她关注饮食习惯对气候变化的影响，特别是畜牧业对温室气体排放的贡献。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一在于气候变化的成因和应对措施。一方面，[bmacho] 强调云层变化等自然因素的影响，并以讽刺方式质疑人为干预的必要性；另一方面，[vardump] 则希望人们更加重视科学研究，避免将气候问题政治化。

• [vivzkestrel] 的问题引发了对人类生活方式改变（如饮食习惯）在应对气候变化中的潜力的讨论。虽然这是一个假设性问题，但它涉及到实际的减排策略，特别是在农业和畜牧业领域。

• 总体来看，讨论涉及自然因素（如云层变化）和人类活动（如饮食改变、政治化态度）在气候变化中的作用，不同观点之间存在一定的张力。

How do you measure climate change? One way is by recording temperatures in different places over a long period of time. While this works well, natural variation can make it harder to see longer-term trends.
But another approach can give us a very clear sense of what’s going on: track how much heat enters Earth’s atmosphere and how much heat leaves. This is Earth’s energy budget, and it’s now well and truly out of balance.
Our
recent research
found this imbalance has more than doubled over the last 20 years. Other researchers have come to the
same conclusions
. This imbalance is now substantially more than climate models have suggested.
In the mid-2000s, the energy imbalance was
about 0.6 watts
per square metre (W/m2) on average. In recent years, the average was about 1.3 W/m2. This means the rate at which energy is accumulating near the planet’s surface has doubled.
These findings suggest climate change might well accelerate in the coming years. Worse still, this worrying imbalance is emerging even as funding uncertainty in the United States
threatens our ability
to track the flows of heat.
Energy in, energy out
Earth’s energy budget functions a bit like your bank account, where money comes in and money goes out. If you reduce your spending, you’ll build up cash in your account. Here, energy is the currency.
Life on Earth depends on a balance between heat coming in from the Sun and heat leaving. This balance is tipping to one side.
Solar energy hits Earth and warms it. The atmosphere’s heat-trapping greenhouse gases keep some of this energy.
But the burning of coal, oil and gas has now added more than
two trillion tonnes
of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. These trap more and more heat, preventing it from leaving.
Some of this extra heat is warming the land or melting sea ice, glaciers and ice sheets. But this is a tiny fraction. Fully
90% has gone
into the oceans due to their huge heat capacity.
Earth naturally sheds heat in several ways. One way is by reflecting incoming heat off of clouds, snow and ice and back out to space. Infrared radiation is also emitted back to space.
From the beginning of human civilisation up until just a century ago, the average surface temperature was about 14°C. The accumulating energy imbalance has now pushed average temperatures
1.3-1.5°C higher
.
Ice and reflective clouds reflect heat back to space. As the Earth heats up, most trapped heat goes into the oceans but some melts ice and heats the land and air. Pictured: Icebergs from the Jacobshavn glacier in Greenland, the largest outside Antarctica.
Ashley Cooper/Getty
Tracking faster than the models
Scientists keep track of the energy budget in two ways.
First, we can directly measure the heat coming from the Sun and going back out to space, using the sensitive radiometers on monitoring satellites.
This dataset
and its predecessors date back to the late 1980s.
Second, we can accurately track the build-up of heat in the oceans and atmosphere by taking temperature readings. Thousands of
robotic floats
have monitored temperatures in the world’s oceans since the 1990s.
Both methods show the energy imbalance has grown rapidly.
The doubling of the energy imbalance has come as a shock, because the sophisticated climate models we use largely didn’t predict such a large and rapid change.
Typically, the
models forecast
less than half of the change we’re seeing in the real world.
Why has it changed so fast?
We don’t yet have a full explanation. But new research suggests changes in clouds is a
big factor
.
Clouds have a cooling effect overall. But the area covered by highly reflective white clouds
has shrunk
, while the area of jumbled, less reflective clouds has grown.
It isn’t
44416051.article_summary: 文章主要讨论地球能量收支的不平衡加剧，导致气候变化可能加速。研究发现，过去20年中，地球吸收的热量与散发的热量之间的不平衡翻了一倍多，从约0.6瓦特每平方米增加到约1.3瓦特每平方米。尽管大部分额外热量（约90%）被海洋吸收，但地表温度已上升1.3-1.5°C。这种变化速度超过了气候模型的预测，可能与云层变化有关，例如反射性白云减少、反射性较差的云增加。文章还提到，监测这些变化的资金不确定性可能影响未来的跟踪能力。这一能量失衡表明，气候变化在未来几年可能加速恶化。
44416051.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [bmacho] 认为气候变化的原因尚未完全解释清楚，并引用新研究指出云层变化是重要因素。具体而言，云层覆盖中高反射的白色云减少，而反射性较差的云增多，可能与2020年后航运燃料中硫含量减少有关。此外，他以讽刺语气提出通过释放某种气体即可解决气候问题，暗示对气候变化应对的简单化看法。

• [vardump] 强调应严肃对待气候科学，并指出气候科学与政治无关。他似乎对一些人轻视气候问题的态度感到不满，呼吁更认真地对待科学研究。

data.author: anonymousiam
data.article_summary: 比特币存款公司（Bitcoin Depot）首席法律官Chris Ryan表示，警方使用暴力破开比特币ATM并取走现金的做法涉嫌执法过度。Ryan指出，ATM内的资金属于公司，损坏机器可能违反银行和刑事法律，公司将追究相关机构的责任。上周，德州Jasper县警长为了帮助一名被骗2.5万美元的受害者，强行破开比特币存款公司的ATM，但机器内的资金已不属于受害者，警方应追查加密货币转入的电子钱包地址。该公司强调，他们一向配合执法部门，若通过正当渠道，他们会打开机器。Ryan还提到，这种事件每年发生多达20次，而暴力破开ATM造成的损失通常由当地司法部门承担。这类事件反映了执法部门对加密货币运作缺乏了解，导致错误处理类似诈骗案件。
data.comments_summary:

44417524.article_content:
(Image credit: Jasper County Sheriff's Office - Texas / Facebook)
Bitcoin Depot Chief Legal Officer, Chris Ryan, said that police departments using brute force to open Bitcoin ATMs and seize the cash inside is bordering on law enforcement overreach. Sawing them open might even be breaking banking and criminal laws, added Ryan. The executive told
Decrypt
that the money inside Bitcoin Depot ATMs rightfully belongs to the company, and that any damage to its machines will be held against the offending organization.
“You’ve got these rogue law enforcement officers thinking that they’re doing the right things by these consumers,” Ryan said. “What they’re actually doing is creating another victim, which is us, with the damage of our property and seizing of our funds.”
Just last week, the
Jasper County Sheriff broke into a Bitcoin Depot ATM
after one of its constituents reported getting scammed out of $25,000. Although the victim went through proper channels, and they were able to secure a search warrant, the money inside the ATM is legally no longer the property of the victim. Instead, the authorities should be going after the wallet address where the cryptocurrency was deposited.
You may like
$124 million armored truck crypto money laundering operation busted
$400 million Coinbase hack was an inside job
Man behind $245m Bitcoin theft has bizarre tale that includes kidnapped parents, fraud, and money laundering
Because the Sheriff used a power tool to break open the ATM to get its contents, Bitcoin Depot said that its machine — which cost $14,000 each — was completely totaled. This is particularly unfortunate because the company said that it always cooperates with law enforcement and will open the machine for them when going through the proper channels.
Requests like this happen up to 20 times a year, Ryan said to
Decrypt
, and that doesn’t even include cases where the police just straight up break their machines open. As for the latter, the company would charge the jurisdiction for the damage — something many can’t afford.
Crypto ATMs are similar to regular deposit machines, wherein they accept cash and credit the same amount to your bank account. But instead of going into your account, it would instead go into your nominated wallet address. Depositors that use the machine are required to confirm that they’re depositing the money into their own wallets, and it even warns users using third-party addresses that they might be getting scammed.
So, if someone was scammed out of their cash with a regular deposit machine, the police would not break the ATM — instead, they would coordinate with the courts and the bank to freeze the account and potentially get the money back. This should be the same pathway that victims should take when scammed through crypto. Unfortunately, many people, including law enforcement and the courts themselves, do not understand how crypto works. Because of that, we get incidents like these where police forcibly open crypto ATMs, causing damage to a third party's property.

While Bitcoin Depot and other similar operations are legitimate, they’re
often used by scammers
because of how fast and easy it is for them to get the stolen funds. Even though you can easily track crypto transactions due to the public nature of the ledger, getting them back is often difficult because of anonymity. Moreover, if the scammer does not use an exchange that works with the authorities, it’s difficult, often nearly impossible, to get the money back. Because of these attributes, scammers are increasingly switching from gift cards to Bitcoin ATMs.

data.title: Unhooking from Amazon Ebooks
data.author: Timothee
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者尝试摆脱亚马逊电子书生态系统的经历。尽管全家已逐渐减少使用亚马逊的产品，但在Kindle电子书上仍然依赖亚马逊。作者通过越狱Kindle来支持epub格式，希望将更多资金直接给予作者。越狱过程相对简单，但需要仔细操作。越狱后使用KOReader应用来阅读epub书籍，但亚马逊购买的书籍仍需用原生Kindle阅读器阅读，因为DRM保护限制。

手动同步新购买的书籍和去除DRM是两个主要挑战。虽然Calibre软件可以帮助去除DRM，但过程繁琐且无法完全自动化。此外，亚马逊在电子书市场几乎垄断，许多出版商只通过亚马逊销售书籍，且经常有打折活动，增加了摆脱亚马逊的难度。作者承认Goodreads服务不尽如人意，但仍在使用。总体而言，摆脱亚马逊的体验并不理想，过程复杂且不便。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕亚马逊Kindle及电子书管理、DRM（数字版权管理）、非亚马逊平台替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• **亚马逊删除 sideload 书籍的问题**：[pnw] 提到通过Calibre载入的电子书可能会被亚马逊静默删除，即使这些书籍属于公共领域。这被认为与Calibre处理标签的方式有关，但用户认为这种行为非常不妥。
• **"通过USB传输" 选项的取消**：[Metalnem] 指出亚马逊取消了"下载并通过USB传输"的选项，导致用户无法移除DRM，这促使他停止购买Kindle电子书。
• **使用开源平台的建议**：[freefaler] 提供了一个开源平台链接，暗示可以作为替代方案。[linotype] 则建议直接购买非亚马逊的电子书阅读器，如Kobo，以避免复杂的破解操作。
• **DRM的拒绝态度**：[msgodel] 表示任何带有DRM的电子书对他来说都不存在，即他完全拒绝购买和使用DRM保护的内容。
• **Calibre 的替代使用方法**：[neilv] 建议可以将Calibre用于转换书籍格式，然后在本地或通过USB传输到阅读器，避免直接使用Calibre的GUI。
• **转换格式与原生阅读器的选择**：[rahimnathwani] 认为无需破解Kindle或安装KOReader，只需将EPUB转换为MOBI格式即可用Kindle原生阅读器阅读。
• **非亚马逊的同步与发现平台**：[tcoff91] 提到使用Storyteller平台来获得类似Whispersync的体验，并建议使用Libation和Calibre来去除DRM。[mikhailt] 则提到正在开发的Readest平台，可能适合用来同步书籍和阅读进度。[tresni] 推荐了hardcover.app作为同步阅读状态的工具，并提供KOReader插件。
• **图书馆借阅与非DRM音频书**：[davidw] 提到从图书馆借阅电子书，而[politelemon] 建议使用BookBub等平台寻找电子书优惠，同时提到libgen作为获取电子书的非正规途径。[protocolture] 则直接使用.txt文件和FTP服务器来管理自己的电子书。

补充讨论：
• **作者与亚马逊的关系**：[dsign] 从作者角度出发，指出亚马逊的高分成比例和低 discoverability（可发现性）问题，认为作者也应脱离亚马逊以获得更好的创作和销售环境。
• **Goodreads的替代品需求**：[xvilka] 表达了对开放且去中心化的Goodreads替代品的需求。

争议焦点：
• **亚马逊删除 sideload 书籍的合法性与合理性**：用户对亚马逊删除未从其平台购买的书籍表示不满，认为即使是公共领域的书籍也不应受到这种限制。
• **DRM 的使用与拒绝**：部分用户完全拒绝DRM书籍，认为DRM限制了他们的阅读自由，而其他用户则通过各种工具和方法试图绕过DRM。

44415388.article_content:
Unhooking from Amazon ebooks
Over the years we, as a family, have been moving our purchases away from Amazon, except in one single place: Kindle ebooks. For me it's that I'm incapable of reading physical books (
but my kindle unlocked my reading
), and with a Kindle, I was limited as to where I buy my books.
When I read that it was relatively easy to
jailbreak all the Kindle models
I used this as my opportunity to move to buying epub books and hopefully more of that money goes to the authors (in an ideal world…).
Here's how it's going so far. In short: not
quite
as well as I'd like.
Jailbreaking
I won't cover the process here, but it wasn't too difficult. You have to properly identify your model (which is tricky enough), and then carefully follow the step by step process. It's lots of reading, clicking, double checking and waiting. The Kindle needs to be connected to the computer doing the work, it's tedious but gives you more features.
Importantly (for me) was that the full original system is intact. The jailbreak process adds a "book" (app) called KUAL which is the doorway to the custom e-reader - specifically I installed
KOReader
(though I've no idea if there's other readers available!).
KOReader
This is the app that will read the epub format (and most other e-book formats). A little frustrating that the Amazon purchased books are read using the original Kindle reader (they're the
AZW3
ebook format - which has Amazon's DRM protection).
The UI is…not entirely intuitive. I spent probably the course of a week messing around with different settings, losing where the menu options were, being unsure why there's two types of config panels and completely missing the pagination on the settings. Eventually I found that there's a "Menu Search" (in the right hand side hamburger menu in "Help").
There's some nice features for when the Kindle is turned off, besides having the book cover, I've got it set to show the cover, title, how long I've been reading it for and my current progress (search for "wallpaper"). I particularly like the "book map" feature (though, I can't say I visit often):
Getting ebooks / not giving money to Amazon
This is really the draw for me. The short version is: this is not straightforward in the slightest, and Amazon have done a pretty good job of making the user experience pretty smooth (I believe, but don't have personal experience, that a Kobo reader has a similar workflow).
With Amazon, I can find the book I want using my phone, buy it, and sync my Kindle and it's ready to be read. I've managed to do this abroad even without wifi because I can hotspot my Kindle to my phone to pick up the new book.
There's two problems to overcome to get this kind of experience:
Automatic syncing of newly purchased books
DRM stripping
There's a few ways to handling syncing, none of them entirely straight forward.
If you're familiar with
Calibre
, From here there's a KOReader plugin that your Kindle can connect to and "send to main" will send the book to KOReader - though this is obviously not automated.
There is a "cloud sync" option in KOReader that can connect to Dropbox (and FTP if you like). This could get books across, but the biggest issue I came up against is the DRM removal.
DRM stripping can all be done in Calibre, but through my exploration, I couldn't find a way to automate this, even from the command line.
From my (little) experience, there's two parts to the DRM removal (so your bought book can be read on KOReader):
The book comes in a .ascm format - a pointer file that is serviced by
Adobe Digital Editions
which only then gives you a DRM encoded epub (or PDF).
Once I've got the epub, I can use
Calibre's DeDRM tools
so that my book is finally portable.
The problem with all this is that it requires that you drive the software to do the work.
I did find a
DeASCM plugin
which worked on the Adobe Digital Editions sample book, but didn't work on the
book I had bought
from Google's store (though it
had
successfully fulfilled the DRM fulfilment, but just couldn't get the epub out).
So the workflow I have is clunky, and definitely not compatible if I'm away from home reading a book (and it's usually holidays that I'll impulse buy a book).
The other downsides
There's a few other factors against me when trying to cut Amazon out of the chain of suppliers:
Amazon have a near monopoly on ebooks. Okay, maybe not quite, but every book publisher I've visited since jailbreaking my Kindle has pointed me (often exclusively) to Amazon to buy their book.
Amazon have deals on books all the time - which, if I'm honest with myself, is appealing (because I save money) but almost certainly doesn't help the authors.
As much as
Goodreads
sucks, I do use the "mark as reading" and have pulled
my book highlights
from their service into my blog. I do have a work around for KOReader, but again it's even more manual.
Fiction (or the fiction I read) is almost always in this DRM-land (and I'm slow AF reading non-fiction, so I don

手动同步新购买的书籍和去除DRM是两个主要挑战。虽然Calibre软件可以帮助去除DRM，但过程繁琐且无法完全自动化。此外，亚马逊在电子书市场几乎垄断，许多出版商只通过亚马逊销售书籍，且经常有打折活动，增加了摆脱亚马逊的难度。作者承认Goodreads服务不尽如人意，但仍在使用。总体而言，摆脱亚马逊的体验并不理想，过程复杂且不便。
44415388.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕亚马逊Kindle及电子书管理、DRM（数字版权管理）、非亚马逊平台替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• **亚马逊删除 sideload 书籍的问题**：[pnw] 提到通过Calibre载入的电子书可能会被亚马逊静默删除，即使这些书籍属于公共领域。这被认为与Calibre处理标签的方式有关，但用户认为这种行为非常不妥。
• **"通过USB传输" 选项的取消**：[Metalnem] 指出亚马逊取消了"下载并通过USB传输"的选项，导致用户无法移除DRM，这促使他停止购买Kindle电子书。
• **使用开源平台的建议**：[freefaler] 提供了一个开源平台链接，暗示可以作为替代方案。[linotype] 则建议直接购买非亚马逊的电子书阅读器，如Kobo，以避免复杂的破解操作。
• **DRM的拒绝态度**：[msgodel] 表示任何带有DRM的电子书对他来说都不存在，即他完全拒绝购买和使用DRM保护的内容。
• **Calibre 的替代使用方法**：[neilv] 建议可以将Calibre用于转换书籍格式，然后在本地或通过USB传输到阅读器，避免直接使用Calibre的GUI。
• **转换格式与原生阅读器的选择**：[rahimnathwani] 认为无需破解Kindle或安装KOReader，只需将EPUB转换为MOBI格式即可用Kindle原生阅读器阅读。
• **非亚马逊的同步与发现平台**：[tcoff91] 提到使用Storyteller平台来获得类似Whispersync的体验，并建议使用Libation和Calibre来去除DRM。[mikhailt] 则提到正在开发的Readest平台，可能适合用来同步书籍和阅读进度。[tresni] 推荐了hardcover.app作为同步阅读状态的工具，并提供KOReader插件。
• **图书馆借阅与非DRM音频书**：[davidw] 提到从图书馆借阅电子书，而[politelemon] 建议使用BookBub等平台寻找电子书优惠，同时提到libgen作为获取电子书的非正规途径。[protocolture] 则直接使用.txt文件和FTP服务器来管理自己的电子书。

补充讨论：
• **作者与亚马逊的关系**：[dsign] 从作者角度出发，指出亚马逊的高分成比例和低 discoverability（可发现性）问题，认为作者也应脱离亚马逊以获得更好的创作和销售环境。
• **Goodreads的替代品需求**：[xvilka] 表达了对开放且去中心化的Goodreads替代品的需求。

争议焦点：
• **亚马逊删除 sideload 书籍的合法性与合理性**：用户对亚马逊删除未从其平台购买的书籍表示不满，认为即使是公共领域的书籍也不应受到这种限制。
• **DRM 的使用与拒绝**：部分用户完全拒绝DRM书籍，认为DRM限制了他们的阅读自由，而其他用户则通过各种工具和方法试图绕过DRM。

主要讨论点：对“后现代”一词的使用及其与各种当代政策和理念的关系

不同观点：
• TimorousBestie认为作者错误地将“后现代”用作指代“我不同意的观点”，并将批判性种族理论（CRT）、多样性、公平与包容（DEI）、警察种族主义、识字教育、科学资助、COVID政策等广泛问题归为“后现代”范畴。这种用法是不准确的。
• TimorousBestie指出，真正的知识分子应能够在后现代主义（如德里达、福柯、勒维纳斯、拉康等人的著作）与各种政策或组织之间建立明确的联系，而不是简单地将不同政策归为后现代现象。
• 另一隐含观点可能来自原文作者或支持者，他们将拜登称为“第一位后现代总统”，并将后现代主义与当代许多社会和政治问题联系在一起，暗示这些理念在后现代思想中有根源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于“后现代”一词的定义和应用。TimorousBestie认为这种用法模糊且不准确，而后现代主义与当代政策的具体联系并未得到清晰阐述。
• 例子中提到的具体政策和理念（如CRT、DEI、警察种族主义等）显示了“后现代”标签被广泛且可能不当应用的范围。
• 对于拜登被称为“后现代总统”的评价特别奇怪，暗示这种说法缺乏依据或过度简化了复杂的哲学概念。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某政治人物及其政策的评价，尤其是关于限制财富积累和亿万富翁税的政策提议，以及这些政策可能带来的社会和经济影响。

不同观点：
• [Aurornis] 认为该政治人物在竞选活动中更多是在重复一些能引起部分选民共鸣的口号，而没有提供具体的政策内容。他指出，记者提出的问题比较简单，让该政治人物有机会发表观点，但仍未涉及任何实际政策。

• [ggm] 认为，限制财富积累的提议在去除政治意图后有一定的合理性，但同时也指出，有些人认为自己有权积累无限财富。他质疑是否有人能够真正创造如此巨大的价值以 justify 亿万富翁的收入，并通过“franking credits”的例子说明即使低收入人群也可能反对限制成为亿万富翁的政策。此外，他还讨论了基金经理的成本和回报问题，认为这进一步挑战了该提议的合理性。

• [hollerith] 以讽刺的语气提问，是否该政治人物也认为纽约市的亿万富翁不应该被允许离开。这个评论暗示了对限制亿万富翁自由流动政策的反对。

• [FridayoLeary] 认为需要对该政治人物进行更多讨论，因为他有可能成为纽约市市长。他警告说，如果不调整其政策，可能会造成经济和社会灾难。评论指出，关键问题不在于亿万富翁与社会其他部分的对立，而在于何种政策能为人们带来最大利益。他还提到，富人可能会因为这些政策离开纽约，导致城市失去税收。

• [billy99k] 以讽刺和挑衅的语气表示，想看看这位“疯狂的社会主义者”如何摧毁纽约市，并将责任归咎于共和党。

• [abbycurtis33] 批评讨论中对基本的供需关系缺乏理解，认为这种无知“令人震惊且悲哀”。

补充讨论：
• 涉及对财富积累限制政策的合理性及其执行难度的争论。
• 讨论了亿万富翁可能因高税收或限制政策而离开城市，对地方经济的影响。
• 提到了社会对“平等”和“社会正义”原则的追求及其潜在负面影响。
• 涉及到对具体经济概念（如基金经理的回报、franking credits）的理解和应用。
• 争议焦点在于财富限制政策的有效性和公平性，以及其对经济和社会的长远影响。

data.title: Companies Should Beware Promoting AI in Products
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI应用的优势与用户体验之间的平衡

不同观点：
• **Uehreka的观点**：  
  - 认为AI的优势必须明显且值得，才能证明投资的合理性。  
  - 举例说明ChatGPT在学生和开发者中迅速获得认可，因为它的应用场景直接且有用。  
  - 批评Meta AI的推出失败，认为其UI臃肿且建议的提示不切实际，导致用户体验差。  
  - 虽然看到Meta AI的潜在价值，但质疑用户是否会再给它机会。

• **mpweiher的观点**：  
  - 未详细展开，但通过提供的链接可能暗示对AI相关讨论或资源的兴趣。

• **paulnpace的观点**：  
  - 认为在许多互动中，被迫使用AI的服务体验变差。  
  - 直接表达对当前AI应用在服务中表现的不满，暗示AI的强制使用未必提升用户体验。

补充讨论：
- **用户对AI的第一印象重要性**：Uehreka强调Meta AI因为初次体验差可能失去用户信任，即便后续改进也未必能挽回。
- **AI应用场景的实用性**：Uehreka指出ChatGPT在特定人群中的成功是因为其直接满足了实际需求，如写文章和编码。
- **AI在服务中的强制使用问题**：paulnpace指出AI在某些服务中强制使用，反而导致用户体验下降，这与Uehreka对Meta AI的批评有相似之处。

争议焦点：
- **AI应用的实用性与用户体验之间的矛盾**：一方认为AI需要有明确的实用价值才能被接受，另一方则直接指出当前AI在实际应用中的服务体验存在问题。
- **第一印象与后续改进的关系**：Uehreka认为Meta AI因初次体验差可能失去用户信任，即便后续改进也未必能挽回，这暗示了对AI产品初次体验的高度重视。

data.title: A glob of 99M-year-old amber trapped a zombie fungus erupting from a fly
data.author: jackgavigan
data.article_summary: 科学家在9900万年前的琥珀中发现了一只头部被寄生真菌穿出的苍蝇，以及一只感染类似真菌的年轻蚂蚁。这两种真菌属于已灭绝的Ophiocordyceps属，分别命名为Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae和Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae。这类“僵尸真菌”通过操控宿主行为来传播，最终致其死亡。研究表明，这种寄生现象在白垩纪时期已经存在，并可能对当时生态系统产生复杂影响。尽管现代此类真菌主要感染蚂蚁，但苍蝇的案例显示出古代寄生多样性。该发现揭示了寄生真菌进化历史的一角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：琥珀中的真菌及其可能的影响和相关文化联想

不同观点：
• [浪漫化/文化联想的观点] 
   - [davidpfarrell] 认为真菌的主要目的是让昆虫飞入琥珀中，这种表述更像是一种富有想象力的解释。
   - [TruffleLabs] 则直接将真菌从琥珀中提取与电影题材联系起来，暗示这种现象具有潜在的影视创作价值。
   - [nervousvarun] 提到《最后生还者》（The Last of Us）这款游戏，并引用了《Common Side Effects》这本书，以幽默的态度迎接“蘑菇统治者”的到来。

• [文化作品联想的观点]
   - [bluepuma77] 联想到美国编剧David Koepp的喜剧惊悚小说《Cold Storage》，认为这类作品虽然不是他平时阅读的类型，但十分有趣。

• [科学解释与进化论的观点]
   - [pfdietz] 指出这些琥珀中的真菌不一定与今天的Ophiocordyceps真菌相关，强调了真菌对节肢动物的控制是多次独立演化而来的现象，比如影响千足虫的Arthrophaga myriapodina，这种趋同进化在自然界中其实很常见，并以树木的进化为例进行补充说明。

• [历史与进化时间的观点]
   - [downrightmike] 提到真菌的出现可能比恐龙早数亿年，强调了真菌在地球历史中的悠久性。

补充讨论：
• [幽默/调侃]
   - [WediBlino] 和 [usrbinbash] 都以幽默和夸张的方式回应，前者提到“轰炸城市和一切东西”，后者则玩笑道“这就是你想要的僵尸末日”。
   
争议焦点：
• 主要争议点集中在对真菌现象的文化联想与科学解释之间的差异。部分评论者侧重于娱乐和文化联想，而[pfdietz]则强调了科学事实和进化历史，提醒读者不要将不同种类的真菌现象混为一谈。

44391590.article_content:
Fungus can be seen growing out of the head of a fly encased in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology; Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Sign up for
CNN’s Wonder Theory science newsletter
. Explore the universe with news on fascinating discoveries, scientific advancements and more.
CNN
—
A glob of 99 million-year-old amber has preserved an ancient fly in horror show fashion: with the mushroom-like fruiting body of zombie fungus bursting forth from its head.
The insect, along with a second specimen of a young ant infected with a similar fungus, are two of the oldest examples of a bizarre natural phenomenon that involves fungal parasites hijacking the bodies of their hosts before ultimately killing them.
“Amber gives us this opportunity to visualize the ancient ecological relationships preserved in fossils,” said Yuhui Zhuang, a doctoral student at the Institute of Paleontology at Yunnan University in southwestern China.
“Overall, these two fossils are very rare, at least among the tens of thousands of amber specimens we’ve seen, and only a few have preserved the symbiotic relationship between fungi and insects,” added Zhuang, the lead author of a
study on the fossils p
ublished June 11 in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.
Zhuang and his colleagues named two previously unknown species of ancient fungi of the genus Ophiocordyceps from their research on the amber, which involved using optical microscopes to study the tiny pieces of amber and micro-computed tomography to make 3D images of the fungi-infected insects.
They found the first, named Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae, on the ant and the second, Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae, on the fly.
Some Ophiocordyceps species that prey on ant species today are known as
“zombie-ant fungi”
because the fungal parasite can manipulate the behavior of its hosts for its own benefit. The phenomenon inspired the video game behind the HBO TV show
“The Last of Us.”
HBO shares a parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, with CNN.
“The discovery of these two fossils suggests that terrestrial ecosystems were already very complex, and that Ophiocordyceps, in particular, may have begun to act as “predators” of insects in the Cretaceous period, regulating the populations of certain groups,” Zhuang said via email.
An ant infected with parasitic fungus trapped in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Zombie fungi then and now
Today, parasitic fungi, also known as entomopathogenic fungi, infect a wide range of insect groups, including ants, flies, spiders, cicadas and beetles, according to London’s Natural History Museum.
In the case of carpenter ants, the spore of the Ophiocordyceps fungus lands on the head of an ant, enters its brain through a weak area in the insect’s exoskeleton and takes control of the ant to facilitate its spread, said Conrad Labandeira, senior scientist and curator of fossil arthropods at the Smithsonian Museum of Natural History in Washington, DC, who wasn’t involved in the study.
Paleoophiocordyceps likely zombified its hosts in similar ways, according to Labandeira.
“It appears that ants, for some reason, were targeted early for zombification, and currently are the major recipients of this parasitoid fungus,” Labandeira said. He added that flies are only rarely affected by these parasitic fungi today, making a fossilized example particularly interesting.
The species of fungus that infected the prehistoric ant may be an ancestor of zombie-ant fungi, and thus likely controlled its host’s body in similar ways, said study coauthor João Araújo, mycology curator and assistant professor at the Danish Natural History Museum. Very few specimens of ancient parasitic fungi have been discovered, so little is known about their evolution.
The two insects were likely killed by the fungi before getting trapped in the sticky tree resin that ultimately forms amber, said Araújo, noting that most entomopathogenic fungi kill their hosts to produce the fruiting body.
This lost parasite diversity had a significant role in shaping the planet we live on today, said Phil Barden, an associate professor at New Jersey Institute of Technology’s department of biological sciences, who has worked on amber fossils.
“Even as we find a remarkable diversity of organisms entombed in amber, it’s important to remember that we really do only capture the smallest glimpse. For any given fossil ant or beetle, we can imagine all of the parasites, fungus, and bacteria that such insects support,” Barden, who wasn’t involved in the new study, said via email.
A spider that has been killed by an entomopathogenic fungus.
Anton Sorokin/Alamy Stock Photo
It was “fascinating to see some of the strangeness of the natural world that we see today was also present at the height of the age of the dinosaurs,” said study coauthor Edmund Jarzembowski, a professor and associate
44391590.article_summary: 科学家在9900万年前的琥珀中发现了一只头部被寄生真菌穿出的苍蝇，以及一只感染类似真菌的年轻蚂蚁。这两种真菌属于已灭绝的Ophiocordyceps属，分别命名为Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae和Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae。这类“僵尸真菌”通过操控宿主行为来传播，最终致其死亡。研究表明，这种寄生现象在白垩纪时期已经存在，并可能对当时生态系统产生复杂影响。尽管现代此类真菌主要感染蚂蚁，但苍蝇的案例显示出古代寄生多样性。该发现揭示了寄生真菌进化历史的一角。

44393307.article_content:
Touching the back wall of the Apple store
23 Jun, 2025
Here's a dumb story. When I was in high school, my friends and I had a game we used to play at the mall: we would go into the Apple store and try to make it to the back wall of the store, touch it, and exit out the front without an Apple staff person talking to us.
We were fascinated with the Apple store in the mall because it was essentially an interactive luxury goods store where they'd let you actually
grasp
all the luxury goods with your teenager hands. I have no idea what the current policy is in Apple stores, but in the 2000s, the Apple store in my local mall allowed crowds of greasy teens to wander in and start very obviously just fucking around and poking and prodding everything. They would, however, always try to talk to us and ask us whether they could help us.
So we made up a game where you'd try to get through the store and to the back wall and out again without being spoken to. There were no real strategies here - it was all down to luck and just physically avoiding the Apple store workers. It was not, in my experience, possible to melt into the environment and look like someone who shouldn't be spoken to. Apple store staff would speak to
anyone.
If the store was crowded enough, you could melt into the crowd a bit, but it was no guarantee. The back of the store was always the easiest place to get caught, and touching the back wall was a pretty conspicuous, attention-grabbing action. I think I only won the game a couple times. I had friends who won by sprinting out of the store once or twice.
I bought my first iPod - an iPod 5, I think? - with the salary from my first big summer job. It was more of a stipend than a proper salary, because I was a camp counselor at a summer camp for girls with diabetes, and I was working deranged schedules, and living at my workplace, and my only sustained chunk of free time every day was between 8 PM and midnight, so I was effectively working for 20 hours a day.
They did not pay us a ton for this! But I made enough money from that job to buy an iPod when I returned home for a few weeks before going to my freshman year of college.
Anyway, I remember feeling shocked and kind of disembodied and terrified to have
a reason,
finally, to personally purchase something from the Luxury Goods Store Which Is Also An Interactive Playplace. I remember that I was acting very strangely during the entire process, speaking oddly to the salesperson, kind of terrified to be spending that much money... but I couldn't get myself to lighten up. Part of my brain was saying "this place is bullshit and I use it to clown on the staff," and part of my brain was saying
"I want the luxury good!!
and I am going to purchase it now." Much dissonance. I got the iPod and I loved it, though.
I also remember realizing at this time that the reason the Apple store allowed crowds of greasy teens in to prod everything was that we were one of the
target audiences
for the luxury goods, and it was good for Apple that we were fascinated with their store. They were not asking us if we wanted an iPod because they were trying to interrupt our game - they
really did
think we might want to buy an iPod, because we really might have been actual customers. I was still 18 years old when I bought mine. I did not look any different, really, than I had a few months before, when we were still playing our game in high school.
The MP3 player I had before that iPod was a much more generic one. I've spent the last few days occasionally checking Wikipedia and other places online to see if I can tell which one it was, and I have absolutely no idea. It might have been a Creative? It certainly wasn't a Zune. I think my parents got it at Walmart.
It left a bigger impact on my life, really, than the iPod, because it was the thing that got me into media piracy, and led me to install Linux on an old laptop, which I used exclusively for media piracy. This increased my computer proficiency dramatically (though not to the point where I became a habitual Linux user) and set off a chain of events that made me much more comfortable with amateur web development and eventually game development.
It's a shame I cannot remember what brand it was! I remember the iPod because it was a luxury good, but I think I owe that old Walmart MP3 player a lot more.
#apple

data.title: My home servers are not a homelab
data.author: nradk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“家庭实验室”（homelab）的概念，指在家中设置的用于实验和学习的服务器、网络设备等基础设施，规模和形式多样，从单个旧手机到完整的数据中心。作者有自己的服务器 setup，用于自托管服务，但并不称为家庭实验室，因为缺乏实验和学习的目的，仅用于维护和改进。作者纠结于如何准确命名这种 setup，认为“家庭服务器”（home server）并不完全合适，并提出其他可能的名称如“HomeCloud”或“HomeProd”，但未有定论。最终强调命名并非重大问题，但反映出不同用户目的和用途的差异。

44418424.article_content:
First, what is a homelab? While I don’t think there’s a dictionary definition, a homelab seems to refer loosely to the collection of servers, networking gear, and supporting infrastructure that someone has set up in their home, for experimentation and learning, either for fun or to develop skills.
Naturally, homelabs can take a wide variety of sizes and shapes. Take a quick look around
/r/homelab
on Reddit, and you’ll find setups ranging from a
single old Android phone
to a
full-fledged data center
. Whatever the scale, the ethos of the subreddit (and other Homelab communities I’ve seen outside of Reddit) seems to be centered around learning, experimentation and playing around. People often have big, expensive and crazy setups just for the heck of it.
At my home, I have a setup that looks like a homelab. It consists of a small rack housing a few computers, a switch, and a few other supporting pieces of hardware. But I don’t consider this a homelab, because I don’t use it as a
lab
. It sits there, running the ten or so services I self-host for me and my family. When I work on it, it is for regular maintainence, incremental improvement, or to install new services. I do enjoy working on it, and I’ve learned a lot along the way, but these are merely side effects.
So I hesitate to call it a homelab, and there’s this small lexical vacuum here—no other word applies well. ‘Home server’ comes close, but it feels strange to refer to the whole setup, consisting of multiple servers and other non-server equipment, in the singular as a ‘home server’. ‘Home servers’ isn’t ideal either. I usually just refer it to as my ‘self-hosting setup’. Yeah, I know I’m splitting hairs—it isn’t that big of a deal what you call things. But I think it is interesting that within the set of people who keep servers in their home, there are two subsets (with considerable overlap) whose reasons for doing so are sort of orthogonal. The ‘homelab’ moniker perfectly fits one group, and it would be nice for the self-hosters whose setups are not homelabs to have a cool name too. ‘HomeCloud’? ‘HomeProd’? Stick to ‘home server(s)’? I don’t have any good ideas.

data.title: WorldVLA: Towards Autoregressive Action World Model
data.author: chrsw
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为WorldVLA的自动回归动作世界模型，该模型整合了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型和世界模型。WorldVLA通过结合动作和图像的理解与生成，预测未来图像并学习环境的基本物理规则，从而改进动作生成。同时，动作模型基于图像观察生成后续动作，帮助视觉理解并促进世界模型的视觉生成。研究显示，WorldVLA的表现优于单独的动作和世界模型，展现了二者之间的相互增强效果。然而，动作模型在以自动回归方式生成动作序列时性能下降，原因是模型对动作预测的泛化能力有限，导致早期动作误差影响后续动作。为此，文章提出了一种注意力掩码策略，通过选择性掩码先前动作来显著提升动作块生成的性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型架构的发展与比较

不同观点：
• blovescoffee认为当前的**autoregressive action world model**（自回归动作世界模型）可能只是一个局部的最佳选择（local max），其优势可能会被**JEPA**（Joint Empirical Probability Approximation）相关的工作所取代。该评论者对**arch（架构）的细节**有更多期待，希望了解更多具体内容，并暗示JEPA可能在未来成为更优的方案。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：当前的模型架构是否是最佳选择，或者是否有如JEPA等其他模型架构会在未来占据主导地位。
- **论据**：blovescoffee指出，**autoregressive action world model**虽然目前表现良好，但可能只是阶段性的最佳方案（local max），未来JEPA等新方法可能会提供更大的突破。
- **隐含的讨论**：对AI模型的架构选择和未来发展方向存在不同预期，部分人可能更看好新方法（如JEPA）的潜力。

View a PDF of the paper titled WorldVLA: Towards Autoregressive Action World Model, by Jun Cen and 11 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present WorldVLA, an autoregressive action world model that unifies action and image understanding and generation. Our WorldVLA intergrates Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model and world model in one single framework. The world model predicts future images by leveraging both action and image understanding, with the purpose of learning the underlying physics of the environment to improve action generation. Meanwhile, the action model generates the subsequent actions based on image observations, aiding in visual understanding and in turn helps visual generation of the world model. We demonstrate that WorldVLA outperforms standalone action and world models, highlighting the mutual enhancement between the world model and the action model. In addition, we find that the performance of the action model deteriorates when generating sequences of actions in an autoregressive manner. This phenomenon can be attributed to the model's limited generalization capability for action prediction, leading to the propagation of errors from earlier actions to subsequent ones. To address this issue, we propose an attention mask strategy that selectively masks prior actions during the generation of the current action, which shows significant performance improvement in the action chunk generation task.

data.title: The Chan-Zuckerbergs stopped funding social causes
data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：慈善资金与社会责任在教育领域的角色与影响

不同观点：
• **ggm** 认为，国家需求的资金应通过税收来提供，而不是依赖慈善资金。如果依赖慈善资金，应将其放入一个安全的机制中，以防止不确定的结果。
• **maxglute** 对慈善资金未用于建设博物馆等实体设施表示不满，认为这是缺乏对社会责任的体现。
• **asveikau** 从家长角度出发，强调学校突然关闭对家庭造成的混乱和影响，认为亿万富翁在有能力的情况下，不继续资助学校是道德上的耻辱。
• **duxup** 对学校使用高科技设备如“语音计步器”表示质疑，认为这些技术并不能解决教育的根本问题，尤其是在缺乏纪律规定的情况下。
• **southernplaces7** 提出两种可能性：要么是 cynical liars 为了公关价值资助社会项目，现在不再关心；要么是懦夫，不能坚持他们声称道德上支持的事业。不论是哪种情况，最终受害者都是依赖这些项目的人们。
• **ars** 认为如果Chan的实验没有效果，那么不再资助是合理的，尤其是因为教育周期不可能等待20年。
• **Jedd** 引用了《No Such Thing As a Free Gift: The Gates Foundation and the Price of Philanthropy》一书，暗示对慈善资本主义的质疑。
• **max_** 提到Chan和Zuckerberg之前在Newark公共学校的资助项目也遭到质疑，认为资金被浪费了。
• **apical_dendrite** 认为Chan和Zuckerberg在处理资助退出时比Elon和Trump更负责任，后者更 abruptly 地打破了承诺。
• **itsthecourier** 分享个人经验，强调即使尽力资助他人，也应理解其中的不确定性。
• **MilnerRoute** 引用了《华盛顿邮报》的标题，强调了Chan和Zuckerberg停止资助对社会造成的直接影响。
• **jongjong** 认为亿万富翁不应介入社会事业，最好去购买游艇和豪宅，以免资助可能有害的项目，并认为让亿万富翁感觉自己赢得了人生游戏，可以减少其参与有害政治的倾向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于亿万富翁是否应该以及如何承担社会责任，特别是在教育领域。
• 一些评论质疑高科技在教育中的实际效果和适用性。
• 另一个值得注意的点是慈善资金的可持续性和不确定性，以及对依赖这些资金的社区的潜在影响。
• 不同评论者对亿万富翁在社会项目中的角色持有截然不同的看法，有人认为他们应更负责任，有人则希望他们完全退出社会事业。

data.title: Ask HN: Is the header CSS broken for you?
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网站界面变化及其在不同设备上的表现

不同观点：
• [tomhow] 确认已经知晓问题，并表示相关人员会在有空时处理，暗示问题尚未解决。
• [Averave] 通过对比网页代码的变化，指出HTML结构的改变导致了显示问题。具体变化是从使用 `<tr>` 增加空间改为 `<td style="height:10px">`，并且新方法在桌面端有效，但在移动端无效。该用户还提出了一种通过开发者工具手动修复问题的方法。
• [masklinn] 提到在手机上的一些具体变化，如主链接从两行变成三行，以及个人资料和退出登录按钮从两行变成一行。虽然这些变化使得某些操作（如点击新帖子）更麻烦，但也减少了误触退出登录的可能性。
• [ajjenkins] 确认问题存在，特别是在iOS Safari浏览器上，文章标题距离顶部过近。
• [leakycap] 对网站的小改动表示兴趣，并表示欣赏网站多年来保持一致的外观，尽管这些小变化可能并不总是受欢迎。
• [josephcsible] 和 [LordShredda] 都表示自己也注意到了这个问题，后者甚至一度以为是自己的Firefox Beta版本导致了布局错误。
• [RandomBacon] 特别指出在Firefox for Android上也观察到了这个问题。
• [kurrupttt] 持不同意见，表示自己测试时没有发现任何问题，暗示问题可能与具体设备或浏览器有关。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于HTML结构的改变是否合适，尤其是新方法在移动端的表现不佳，导致用户体验受到影响。
• 部分用户对网站的微小变化持批评态度，认为这些变化破坏了原有的用户体验，而另一些用户则对这些小改动持开放或中立态度。
• 不同设备和浏览器上的表现差异也是讨论的一个重要方面，显示出问题可能具有环境特异性。

data.title: Use keyword-only arguments in Python dataclasses
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
Python的**dataclasses**是一个方便构造数据类的好功能，可以替代字典，并支持添加方法、动态属性和子类。相比手写类，dataclasses自动生成`__init__()`和`__eq__()`等方法，简化了开发。为了提高可维护性，建议使用`kw_only=True`参数，强制使用关键字参数调用，如`MyDataClass(x=1, y='foo', z=False)`。这样有两个好处：  
1. 允许重新排序字段而不破坏调用者。  
2. 允许子类添加必需字段，不受默认值限制。  
对于需要保证向后兼容性和可扩展性的库作者尤其重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python数据类中使用关键字仅限参数的利与弊，以及数据类的其他相关特性讨论

不同观点：
• **支持关键字仅限参数**：[meander_water] 提出可以通过 `KW_ONLY` 实现关键字仅限参数，认为显式定义参数可以减少调用时出错的可能性。[spstoyanov] 也表示显式优于隐式，支持这种做法。
  
• **关键字仅限参数的弊端**：[ayhanfuat] 认为关键字仅限参数在变量名已经匹配的情况下显得繁琐，并希望Python能有JavaScript那样的简写属性语法。[flakes] 认为强制关键字参数会让API使用起来很麻烦，建议仅在参数数量较多（4-5个以上）或参数相似性较高时使用，以提高可读性。

• **对现有项目的潜在影响**：[joshdavham] 指出，虽然关键字仅限参数可以防止未来出现破坏性变化，但在现有项目中添加这种要求可能会导致不兼容问题，进而引发破坏性变化。

• **数据类的替代方案和扩展需求**：[eachro] 质疑是否还有必要使用数据类而非严格的基模型（pedantic base models）。[semiinfinitely] 则表示需要更多关于 `slots=True` 的资料。[joshdavham] 进一步询问是否有其他方法可以在函数中实现类似数据类的参数强制行为。[est] 提出数据类的初始化方式不够灵活，建议像 `mydataclass(my_dict, lint=True)` 这样的方式直接传递字典以避免手动筛选键。

补充讨论：
• **库和工具的实际体验**：[FridgeSeal] 提到 AWS Boto3 库中大量使用 `kwargs` 导致文档和IDE提示不够明确，体验糟糕。
• **实际开发中的痛点**：[est] 提到在项目中使用数据类时，不能直接传递字典，必须手动筛选支持的键，增加了使用难度。

争议焦点：关键字仅限参数在提高代码可读性和安全性方面的优势是否足以抵消其带来的繁琐和潜在的兼容性问题。

44418036.article_content:
Python
dataclasses
are a really nice feature for constructing classes that primarily hold or work with data. They can be a good alternative to using dictionaries, since they allow you to add methods, dynamic properties, and subclasses. They can also be a good alternative to building your own class by hand, since they don’t need a custom
__init__()
that reassigns attributes and provide methods like
__eq__()
out of the box.
One small tip to keeping dataclasses maintainable is to always construct them with
kw_only=True
, like so:
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(kw_only=True)
class MyDataClass:
x: int
y: str
z: bool = True
This will construct an
__init__()
that looks like this:
class MyDataClass:
def __init__(
self,
*,
x: int,
y: str,
z: bool = True,
) -> None:
self.x = x
self.y = y
self.z = z
Instead of:
class MyDataClass:
def __init__(
self,
x: int,
y: str,
z: bool = True,
) -> None:
self.x = x
self.y = y
self.z = z
That
*
in the argument list means everything that follows must be passed as a keyword argument, instead of a positional argument.
There are two reasons you probably want to do this:
It allows you to reorder the fields on the dataclass without breaking callers. Positional arguments means a caller can use
MyDataClass(1, 'foo', False)
, and if you remove/reorder any of these arguments, you’ll break those callers unexpectedly. By forcing callers to use
MyDataClass(x=1, y='foo', z=False)
, you remove this risk.
It allows subclasses to add required fields. Normally, any field with a default value (like
z
above) will force any fields following it to also have a default. And that includes
all
fields defined by subclasses. Using
kw_only=True
gives subclasses the flexibility to decide for themselves which fields must be provided by the caller and which have a default.
These reasons are more important for library authors than anything. We spend a lot of time trying to ensure backwards-compatibility and forwards-extensibility in
Review Board
, so this is an important topic for us. And if you’re developing something reusable with dataclasses, it might be for you, too.

data.title: Inline-C: Write inline C in Haskell
data.author: burnt-resistor
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Haskell库`inline-c`，它允许开发者直接在Haskell代码中嵌入C语言代码。这个库简化了Haskell与C的互操作，使得调用C函数和使用C数据结构变得更加方便。通过`inline-c`，开发者可以在Haskell源码中编写C代码片段，并自动处理两者之间的数据转换和内存管理。该库支持GHC编译器，并且适用于需要高性能或与C语言库交互的项目。注意事项包括确保C代码的正确性和处理潜在的跨语言内存管理问题。

data.title: ICE test train reaches speeds of up to 405.0 km/h
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 2025年6月28日，德铁（DB）与西门子交通在埃尔福特—莱比锡/哈勒高速线路的测试中，使用ICE试验列车达到了405公里/小时的速度。此类高速测试极为罕见，仅用于检测目的。德铁InfraGO总裁Nagl博士强调，这一成就证明了该线路基础设施的卓越性能，经过10年运营仍能支持高速运行。联邦交通部国务秘书Hirte指出，该测试彰显了德国高品质基础设施和强大工业能力。西门子交通的Velaro Novo试验列车在测试中表现优异，其新一代技术显著提升了能效和运力，并降低了成本。德铁Systemtechnik的ICE-S试验列车配备先进测量技术，用于检测和优化高速线路。Velaro Novo列车经过多年测试，展现了其灵活适应未来需求的能力。
