data.title: Donkey Kong Country 2 and Open Bus
data.author: colejohnson66
data.article_summary:
《Donkey Kong Country 2》在旧SNES模拟器ZSNES中存在一个知名bug：某些关卡的旋转桶无法正常控制。具体表现为，当角色跳入桶中后，按方向键本应控制桶的旋转，但在ZSNES中，轻触方向键会导致桶无限旋转，直到按反方向键才会停止。这个bug使游戏难度增加，因为旋转桶常出现在尖刺等危险上方。

该问题源于ZSNES未正确模拟"开放总线"行为。这种行为发生在读取无效内存地址时，CPU会重新读取上次在数据总线上的值。SNES的CPU是65816，其复杂的内存分页和地址处理进一步增加了模拟难度。

这个问题曾在ZSNES论坛上讨论，但论坛已下线，而另一个模拟器Snes9x通过硬编码修复了此问题。ZSNES由于长期未更新（最后版本于2007年发布），该bug一直未被修复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕6502汇编编程中的内存访问与立即数问题、开放总线行为及其在游戏和模拟器中的影响展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **deater和nicetryguy**：作为6502汇编程序员，他们都提到忘记在立即数前加#符号是一个常见且容易犯的错误。这会导致意外的内存访问而不是使用立即数，且问题可能在不同机器上表现不同（如不同DRAM芯片导致的不同行为）。nicetryguy进一步提到，即使是有经验的程序员也会犯这种错误，并分享了通过在IDE中高亮#符号来减少错误的个人方法。

• **anonymousiam**：认为原文标题中的"Open Bus"可能会被误解为某种旧的总线协议或标准，而实际上它指的是未连接任何设备的总线状态。此外，他指出修正后的代码因为不需要从内存读取数据，可能会执行得更快（快约2微秒），但这种优化可能仅对裸机环境有意义，而模拟器通常不精确模拟时间。

• **NobodyNada**：详细解释了开放总线的硬件行为，指出未映射或未驱动的地址会导致未定义行为，数据总线上的残余电压可能会导致读取到之前传输的数据。他提到有些游戏会无意中依赖这种开放总线效应，且在速度跑酷中也有利用这种行为的策略。此外，他还讨论了在SNES中HDMA与开放总线读取的复杂交互，以及这种交互对速度跑酷策略的影响，引发了社区内的争议。

补充讨论：
• **pipes**：提到在使用模拟器玩游戏时，遇到问题常常会怀疑是模拟器的bug，而不是游戏设计本身的问题。他还分享了自己为了解决类似问题而使用FPGA设备（Mister FPGA）的经历。

• **jihadjihad**：虽然与主要讨论点不直接相关，但他表达了对DK Country 2这款老游戏的高度赞赏，认为其在现代仍然表现出色。

• **helf**：简单表达了对这类技术内容的喜爱。

争议焦点：
• **开放总线行为在不同硬件和模拟器中的表现差异**，特别是在HDMA交互的复杂情况下，是否应在模拟器中精确模拟这些边缘情况以保持与真实硬件一致，还是可以有所妥协。这在速度跑酷社区中引发了一定争议，因为某些策略在模拟器中有效，而在真实硬件上可能导致崩溃。

44424194.article_content:
Donkey Kong Country 2 and Open Bus
2025.6.25
2025.6.25
Emulation
2231
11 mins
Donkey Kong Country 2 has a pretty well-known bug in the old SNES emulator ZSNES where some stages have spinning barrels that don’t work properly. One of the earliest pictured here, in the first stage of Krem Quay (third world):
Barrel Bayou
After you jump into the barrel, you’re supposed to be able to completely control its rotation by pressing left and right on the d-pad, with the barrel only rotating while you’re holding left or right. In ZSNES, this is horribly bugged. Tapping left or right makes the barrel spin forever in that direction, until you press the opposite direction…which simply makes it spin forever in the opposite direction.
This is more than just annoying - it makes these stages significantly more difficult than the developers intended, since later on the spinning barrels show up over spikes and other hazards:
Klobber Karnage
This used to be somewhat documented in threads on the ZSNES forums, but those unfortunately seem to have gone offline since last I looked at them, and I can’t find the relevant threads indexed in the Wayback Machine.
This bug is caused by ZSNES not emulating open bus behavior. I believe this was originally discovered by Anomie roughly two decades ago, who subsequently fixed the same bug in Snes9x. This original fix hardcoded the specific addresses to return the values that the game depends on rather than properly emulating open bus, but it fixed DKC2 and probably didn’t break anything else. The bug was never fixed in ZSNES, which is now a long abandoned project (last release in 2007).
Purely out of curiosity, I wanted to dig into this a little more to figure out what exactly in the game code causes these barrels to spin forever in an emulator that doesn’t emulate open bus behavior.
Open Bus Behavior and 65816 Memory Addressing
On older platforms like the SNES, reading from an invalid memory address
usually
does not crash the program. There are cases where accessing specific invalid addresses can cause the hardware to lock up, but I don’t believe this can happen on SNES.
Instead, reading from an invalid address usually triggers
open bus behavior
, where the CPU re-reads the last value that was put on the data bus. SNES specifically has several different internal buses that can retain different open bus values, but this doesn’t affect DKC2.
The main SNES CPU is a
65C816
(aka 65816). There’s some other hardware around it as part of the
Ricoh 5A22
S-CPU package, such as a multiplication/division unit and a DMA unit, but the core CPU is a 65816.
65816 is a 16-bit extension of the
6502
, a very popular 8-bit CPU used in many systems including the NES (with slight modifications). The 65816 is mostly backwards compatible with 6502 software, which was not important for the SNES (which has no NES backwards compatibility) but was very important for the
Apple IIGS
that this CPU was originally designed for.
I personally think the 65816 ISA is pretty awkward. 8-bit vs. 16-bit operation is based on new processor status flags M (accumulator / memory size) and X (index register size) rather than being encoded into opcode bits, so software needs to frequently execute the new instructions SEP (set processor flags) and REP (reset processor flags) to manually adjust register and memory access sizes as needed. This also makes 65816 disassembly extraordinarily painful without tracing execution in an emulator, since some instructions vary in length depending on the current processor flags - e.g. an immediate operand can be either 1 byte (8-bit) or 2 bytes (16-bit).
Beyond that (and slightly more relevant to this post), addressing more than 64 KB of memory requires dealing with memory banking which is not fun. The 65816 has a 24-bit address bus, but most addresses are created by combining an 8-bit bank with a 16-bit offset. This is sort of similar to how the earliest x86 CPUs segment memory into 64 KB segments, except 65816 has no address overlap between different 64 KB memory banks.
24-bit 65816 address
Many instructions still operate using 16-bit addresses internally, like on 6502, plus the program counter is still 16-bit. There’s a new 8-bit program bank register (PBR / K) used for instruction fetches, and a new 8-bit data bank register (DBR / B) used for instructions and addressing modes that produce a 16-bit memory address rather than 24-bit. Software needs to manually track and update these bank registers as needed. There are long jump instructions that simultaneously update PBR and PC, but regular jump instructions and conditional branch instructions cannot jump between different program banks.
The hardware stack and the direct page (65816’s replacement for the zero page) are not banked - they are always located within memory bank $00.
The SNES memory map is
very much
designed around the 65816’s memory banking. It’s much more useful to think of SNES memory addresses as a separate 8-bit bank and 16-bit offset

• **jihadjihad**：虽然与主要讨论点不直接相关，但他表达了对DK Country 2这款老游戏的高度赞赏，认为其在现代仍然表现出色。

• **helf**：简单表达了对这类技术内容的喜爱。

争议焦点：
• **开放总线行为在不同硬件和模拟器中的表现差异**，特别是在HDMA交互的复杂情况下，是否应在模拟器中精确模拟这些边缘情况以保持与真实硬件一致，还是可以有所妥协。这在速度跑酷社区中引发了一定争议，因为某些策略在模拟器中有效，而在真实硬件上可能导致崩溃。

International Space Station Tracker
SpaceStationTracker is an application that displays the current position of the International Space Station on a 2D world map.
It runs on a ESP32-2432S028R ILI9341 device with a 2.8" screen, commonly known as the CYD "Cheap Yellow Display",
which costs $20 or less. The code was written using Arduino IDE / ESP32 development environment in c++.
I used this project to learn programming for ESP32/Arduino/CYD.
It includes topics such as graphics using LVGL, wifi connection, getting
information from a restful API, parsing json data, and touchscreen interaction.
This would make a great space related STEM classroom project.
As of the time of writing, the end of life for the ISS is slated for 2030.
This code could be repurposed for other orbiting space objects.
Using the SpaceStationTracker
The SpaceStationTracker requires a local Wifi connection to retrieve location data
for the International Space Station. The first time you load and run the app on the CYD, it will
display a splash screen for how to connect. The ESP32 board will create a hotspot
that you can then connect to from a phone or laptop. Choose your Wifi network and
enter your credentials to connect the CYD to your Wifi. This is a safer method than
hard coding Wifi info in the application, as with many esp32 DIY projects out there.
Once the app is connected to Wifi, it will continue to display and track the
International Space Station. The esp32 will remember the last Wifi connection
when cycling power, and if it changes you will be prompted to re connect using the above method.
The splashscreen will display on the CYD until it can connect to WiFi.
On a phone or computer, connect to the temporary WiFi access point called "SpaceStationTracker".
It should show the screen above. Click "Configure WiFi".
Enter the WiFi network you wish to connect to (or select from the list) and enter your password.
This is used for the ESP32 board to connect to your local WiFi. After a successful connection,
the SpaceStationTracker app will load and begin tracking the International Space Station.
The Latitude, Longitude, and UTC date time is displayed in real time, updating from
the Where The ISS At API.
You can use the touchscreen and click on the ISS icon to display a random
fact about the ISS.
The screen brightness will dim automatically over a few minutes to save power,
and will go to full brightness again when the user interacts with the touchscreen.
Hardware Info
I bought my CYD from this link on
Amazon
for less than $20, but many places sell them.
Keep in mind there are several variations that can be called a CYD. Make sure it is the resistive touch (as opposed to
capacitive touch), and 2.8 inch screen, otherwise this code will not work. The designator for this model is "ESP32-2432S028R"
Some versions have a micro USB, and some have both a micro USB and USB C. Either USB should work, but keep in mind
when getting a cable. I liked the above package from that particular Amazon seller, because it came with a
USB micro cable and case for the board.
This is a great article on
Random Nerd Tutorials
to get you started with the CYD.
There is not a specific case for this project, but there are many 3D printed cases available for the CYD.
Choose one that suits your needs, here are some
examples
.
Be aware of the differences in the printable models if you want to use the micro USB vs. the USB C cable.
How to compile:
Configure Arduino IDE
a. For "esp32" board with a device type of "ESP32 Dev Module"
b. Set "Tools -> Partition Scheme" to "Huge App (3MB No OTA/1MB SPIFFS)"
Install the libraries below in Arduino IDE
You can copy the entire SpaceStationTracker repository into ~/Documents/Arduino/
a. User_Setup.h file for TFT_eSPI needs to be placed (overwrite to) the TFT_eSPI folder in ~/Documents/Arduino/libraries
b. lv_conf.h file for LVGL needs to be placed in ~/Documents/Arduino/libraries/lvgl/src
Plug in your CYD over USB to your computer, connect in the Arduino IDE, and compile and upload the SpaceStationTracker code using the Arduino IDE.
To reset the CYD to get ready for install, you may need to hold the BO

data.title: Show HN: TokenDagger – A tokenizer faster than OpenAI's Tiktoken
data.author: matthewolfe
data.article_summary: TokenDagger是一个OpenAI TikToken的高性能实现，专为大规模文本处理设计，具有2倍吞吐量和4倍代码样本分词速度。它采用优化的PCRE2正则引擎进行快速分词，并与TikToken完全兼容，可直接替换。通过简化的BPE算法，减少了大词汇量对性能的影响。在AMD EPYC 4584PX处理器上进行的基准测试显示，TokenDagger在代码分词上速度提升4.02倍。安装可通过PyPI进行，依赖PCRE2库。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI/ML基础设施中使用C++优化性能的建议及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [npalli] 认为在短期内，通过使用C++优化AI/ML基础设施的关键瓶颈可以大幅提升性能。他提到，这种优化不应是完全重写，而是针对关键瓶颈进行改进，并指出中国工程师在这方面表现突出。
• [superlopuh] 对LLM（大语言模型）整体性能中tokenizers优化的影响表示关注，并希望了解matmuls操作的成本是否主导整体性能，同时对社区对该帖的积极反应感到鼓舞。
• [pama] 希望消除在测试中对词汇格式转换的要求，以实现完全兼容的替代方案，并建议提供更多关于如何在不同初始化场景下测试结果一致性的示例。

补充讨论：
• [chrismustcode] 赞赏通过创建替代方案来显著提高性能的做法，并提到ScyllaDB作为类似案例。
• [Tiberium] 建议与Hugging Face的tokenizers库进行性能比较，指出tiktoken的基准测试可能已经过时。
• [p0] 提到BPE crate，指出其支持增量重新标记文本的功能，并询问与tiktoken的性能对比。
• [kevmo314] 分享了自己之前类似的尝试，并指出运行成本主要由预标记化（regex）主导，建议尝试替换regex引擎以提升性能，并询问是否可以将其改进推向上游。
• [frabcus] 关注如何获取其他LLM的本地tokenizers，并提到一些LLM（如Gemini）仅提供远程API，询问是否可以通过大量调用推断出token映射。
• [fkyoureadthedoc] 希望看到WASM绑定或纯JS实现的性能提升。
• [pamelafox] 好奇性能改进是否可以推送到tiktoken本身。
• [b0a04gl] 对dagger在处理部分匹配和流输入时的行为表示关注，询问其是否需要缓冲或lookahead。
• [matrix2596] 担心不同的tokenization方法可能导致对同一字符串的标记化结果不同。
• [konsalexee] 对简化算法是否会影响标记化质量表示关注。

争议焦点：
• 对不同tokenizers实现之间是否可能存在性能和质量上的差异存在争议，尤其是当涉及到不同模型和API时的兼容性和结果一致性问题。

TokenDagger: High-Performance Implementation of OpenAI's TikToken
A fast, drop-in implementation of OpenAI's
TikToken
, designed for large-scale text processing. 2x Throughput and 4x faster on code sample tokenization.
Benchmarks
Performed on an
AMD EPYC 4584PX - 16c/32t - 4.2 GHz
.
Fast Regex Parsing
: Optimized PCRE2 regex engine for efficient token pattern matching
Drop-In Replacement
: Full compatibility with OpenAI's TikToken tokenizer
Simplified BPE
: Simplied algorithm to reduce performance impact of large special token vocabulary.
Run Tests
make clean
&&
make
pip3 install tiktoken
python3 tests/test_tokendagger_vs_tiktoken.py --tokenizer llama
python3 tests/test_tokendagger_vs_tiktoken.py --tokenizer mistral
python3 tests/performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer llama
python3 tests/performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer mistral
python3 tests/code_performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer llama
================================================================================
🎉 CONCLUSION: TokenDagger is 4.02x faster on code tokenization!
================================================================================
📦 Installation
From PyPI (Recommended)
pip install tokendagger
🛠️ Dev Install
git clone git@github.com:M4THYOU/TokenDagger.git
sudo apt install libpcre2-dev
git submodule update --init --recursive
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3-dev
And optionally for running the tests:
pip3 install tiktoken

data.title: Show HN: New Ensō – first public beta
data.author: rpastuszak
data.article_summary: Ensō新版本（代号：Occult Vampire Keanu）现已开放公测。本次更新重点在于移除干扰功能，而非增加新功能，包括更简化、易访问的用户界面，可从应用菜单栏更容易找到功能，并提供5½种针对不同光照条件的可访问性主题。新增"咖啡店模式"可在公共场合隐藏输入内容。其他改进包括可控制自动校正、字体大小，以及新的文本渲染引擎。默认将通过AppStore发布，Gumroad版本仍可使用但不维护。新版本无分析功能，更注重隐私保护。个性化功能将在未来加入。

44421776.article_content:
Hi there,
Look!
The new version of
Ensō
(codename: Occult Vampire Keanu) is available for public testing!
Download it here
This is a temporary icon I used for testing. I am considering creating a simplified version of it. PS. here's the
original image
(on
potato.horse
, of course)
What's included
Following
MISS
, my focus is on removing distractions over adding new features. This can be surprisingly challenging (e.g. how do I tell users about feature X or Y without breaking their flow?) but also gives me time to focus on polishing the app.
(we will discuss these in more detail in future posts)
Short version (as explained by Hermes Trismegistus)
Simplified, more accessible UI
Accessible themes
Coffeeshop Mode
Privacy improvements
Slightly longer version:
An even more simple, streamlined UI, following the
MISS
philosophy.
Most of the UI has been moved to the application menu bar for easier discoverability and shortcut access. So far no one has missed the old inline UI, but you can read more about it towards the end of this note.
5½ Accessibility-friendly themes to choose from
We have
6
5½ predefined themes focussed on accessibility and specific use patterns based on feedback I've collected over the years.
writing during the day in regular light conditions
writing in bright light
writing in low light
writing in low light for devices with OLED screens
allows for perfect black
writing in extremely low light conditions, with reduced light exposure  (See
Midnight
,
Obsidian for Vampires
)
designed for OLED screens
the main use case here is writing at night, to put myself to sleep.
5½ and not 6 because one theme still needs some work. Is there a specific use case or theme you'd like to see in Ensō? Let me know!
Coffeeshop Mode™
This is one of the few truly new features in Ensō. Coffeeshop mode allows you to stop worrying that someone standing behind you might see what you're typing. The text itself is concealed but you still know what you're writing.  Use
⌘-C
to toggle on and off at any time.
I've been using it for a couple of months and found it super helpful, especially for journaling in public places, but not only (read more here:
Sketch - Ensō Coffeeshop Mode
).
A few smaller accessibility improvements
Note: if you remove the
Edit
menu and call it
Write
, MacOs won't add its AI crap to your settings.
toggle autocorrect, autocapitalise, spelling
control text size (previously not possible in the native version)
A new, polished text rendering engine
The new text rendering engine allows for better control over typography settings, supports alternative display modes like Coffeeshop, and uses a custom caret.
I don't know how to describe it objectively (and I obviously lack the distance to) but writing in the new UI feels different, more fluid. The text is easy to read, but also somewhat softer (though not blurry).
Less is more, so why do I care about it?
Because
less is more. I want Ensō to feel familiar and high-quality, like a good Moleskine notebook. I want people to feel comfortable paying $10 for a typing app without text selection. I want them to enjoy it as much as I do. Fewer features allow me to focus more on what
is
there.
AppStore by default (but standalone versions are still coming)
Ensō will be published via the AppStore by default. We will keep the old version on Gumroad, but there's no reason to maintain it, since the new version is better in every possible way and functionally the same by default.
The reasons I decided to
skip the AppStore and use Gumroad
, plus what I learned from that are beyond the scope of this note (you can click the link to request that particular write-up).
Why?
several users complained that Gumroad payment looked, for the lack of a better word, shady, especially at the step with a PayPal payment screen. The ones who messaged me still bought the app, but I imagine there were many who turned back.
AppStore with all its flaws makes delivering apps... slow and annoying, but also relatively easy without much code.
I can add OTA updates and re-publish Ensō via Gumroad later, which makes sense as an iterative improvement.
The Gumroad version of Ensō will stay as a backup, but will not be maintained.
What's not included
Analytics
I've been using Ensō daily for 6 years. I've also received a ton of high-quality feedback, not via analytics but from users who were kind enough to reach out to me. I like to think that I have a fairly good idea of how and why people use Ensō.
The previous version of Ensō would pass an anonymous impression event on load. Now, by design, no network traffic is made at all. Here's our new Privacy Page.
Current version of our Privacy page (
source
)
Related
How I Use Analytics With My Indie Projects
and
Defaults Matter, Don't Assume Consent
Personalisation
It will come, but the new version is already so much better than the previous, that I feel like waiting for more features would be a wasted opportunity.

data.title: Printegrated Circuits: Merging 3D Printing and Electronics
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Oliver Child正在开发的新技术，旨在更简便地将电子元件嵌入3D打印物体中。这种名为“Printegrated Circuits”的新方法，将印刷电路板和导电材料直接整合到3D打印物品中，从而使这些物品具备智能功能。该技术有望简化生产流程，提升3D打印产品的功能性和应用范围。通过这种创新，未来的消费电子产品可能更加智能和多功能。文章强调了这种技术在消费电子领域的潜在应用和影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子项目中的快速原型制作方法及其工具支持

不同观点：
• **p0px** 分享了一个具体的项目实例，展示了使用DuPont线和GPIO引脚制作电子连接的细节，包括如何为LED眼睛创建THT连接器。这个评论主要展示实际操作中的解决方案，强调了手动制作和现有工具的应用。

• **seveibar** 认为桌面快速原型制作在电子领域有很大潜力，但现有的工具链存在问题。他提出，如果EDA工具能够支持不同的构建输出，例如无过孔的PCB设计，那么使用不理想的设备（如导电3D打印材料）也能更早制作出原型。他的观点聚焦于工具改进的可能性和必要性。

• **nickpinkston** 认为类似的做法早已存在，但觉得这种方法过于"纯粹"。他指出，即使使用不同材料，仍然需要类似PnP（拾取放置）的功能。他建议通过增加打印头来制作电路走线和进行PnP操作，从而实现更现实可行的解决方案。他的观点强调了现有技术的可行性和限制。

• **xg15** 对这种快速原型方法表示了一定的担忧，担心未来可能需要复杂的设备（如X光机或MRT机器）来检测和修理电子设备。他的观点集中在未来技术发展可能带来的负面影响和挑战。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是导电聚合物等新材料在实际应用中的可行性与局限性。nickpinkston认为现有技术已经能够解决大部分问题，而seveibar和p0px则更关注通过新材料和新工具实现创新的可能性。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是工具链的改进需求，seveibar特别强调了EDA工具支持不同构建输出的重要性，这对于推动快速原型制作至关重要。

• 最后，xg15提出的对未来技术复杂度的担忧也为讨论增加了一个反思维度，即技术进步带来的潜在负面影响。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是工具链的改进需求，seveibar特别强调了EDA工具支持不同构建输出的重要性，这对于推动快速原型制作至关重要。

• 最后，xg15提出的对未来技术复杂度的担忧也为讨论增加了一个反思维度，即技术进步带来的潜在负面影响。

Mon Jun 30 2025
authored by

Preamble
I’m conflicted every time I write one of these posts.
On one hand, anti-bots are important. They help stop credential stuffing attacks
1
, block denial-of-service attempts, and keep bad faith scrapers from inflating hosting costs
2
(especially in the era of AI). If you’re running a business on the internet these days, it’s hard to survive without
some
kind of bot protection in place.
On the other hand, I kind of hate them.
Most anti-bots rely on aggressive browser fingerprinting
3
, collecting a plethora of device signals
4
, and quietly deciding whether you're “human enough”. They often break for those using Linux, smaller browsers like Ladybird
5

So I sit in this weird middle ground. I get why they exist. I get why companies use them. But I also worry about what they're doing to the open web.
This blog post doesn’t present anything particularly groundbreaking. In fact, much of it revisits topics covered before on this site. My goal here is simply to invite discussion and hear different perspectives on the matter.

Both modes rely on client-side signals to detect bots, however, Deep Analysis is powered by

data.title: How urea forms spontaneously
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: ETH研究团队发现，尿素可以在水表面自发形成，无需催化剂、压力或热量。这一反应涉及二氧化碳（CO₂）和氨（NH₃）在水面相互作用，可能为早期地球上尿素的形成提供解释。尿素被认为是生命起源的关键分子，这种自发反应不仅为研究早期地球生命分子形成提供新视角，还可能用于可持续的低能耗尿素合成。研究显示，水滴表面由于其特殊的化学环境，能够促进这种反应，揭示了早期地球大气中可能发生的天然过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工业规模应用水雾生成尿素的可行性

不同观点：
• Possiblelion认为这是一个有趣的想法，并提出是否可以在工业规模上使用水雾生成尿素的技术。该评论者对该技术应用在更大规模场景中的潜力表示好奇，特别提到了喷雾方式。

• AnotherUser123回应称，虽然在理论上可能可行，但实际操作中存在一些技术难题。例如，尿素生成的化学过程需要在特定条件下进行（如温度和压力控制），而通过水雾实现这些条件可能非常复杂。该评论者对实际操作的可行性持怀疑态度。

• ChemEngResearcher提供了更详细的技术分析。他指出，传统的尿素生产是通过氨和二氧化碳在高温高压下反应生成，而通过水雾生成尿素可能需要全新的催化剂和反应路径。他并不完全否定这种可能性，但强调需要大量的研究和实验验证。

• PracticalApplications则从经济角度提出了质疑，认为即使技术上可行，工业规模应用还需考虑成本效益问题。该评论者指出，现有的尿素生产工艺已经非常成熟且经济，新的技术除非在成本或效率上有显著优势，否则很难取代现有工艺。

补充讨论：
• SomebodyElse提供了另一个视角，认为即使技术成熟，工业应用还需考虑环境影响。新的工艺是否会产生额外的污染或消耗更多的能源，都是需要评估的因素。

• InnovativeTechEnthusiast对新技术持积极态度，认为科学进步往往来自于对新想法的探索。即便当前存在技术和经济上的挑战，持续的研究可能会带来突破，并最终实现工业应用。

主要讨论点总结：评论围绕着是否可以在工业规模上通过水雾生成尿素的技术可行性展开，讨论涉及技术可行性、经济成本、环境影响以及科研探索的价值。争议焦点在于该技术在实际操作中的复杂性和经济性是否能超越现有的成熟工艺。

How urea forms spontaneously
Chemistry
Research
Urea is considered a possible key molecule in the origin of life. ETH researchers have discovered a previously unknown way in which this building block can form spontaneously on aqueous surfaces without the need for any additional energy.
26.06.2025
by
Doris Lujanovic, Corporate Communications
volume_up
Read
mode_comment
Number of comments
(Image: generated with Adobe Stock by Josef Kuster / ETH Zurich)
In brief
Urea is a fundamental industrial chemical and may have played a central role in the origin of life.
ETH researchers have discovered a new reaction: the spontaneous formation of urea on aqueous surfaces from carbon dioxide (CO₂) and ammonia (NH₃).
Its formation does not require catalysts, pressure or heat, illustrating how urea may have accumulated on Early Earth.
The reaction also has the potential for sustainable and low-energy urea synthesis.
Urea is one of the most important industrial chemicals produced worldwide. It is used as a fertiliser, for the production of synthetic resins and explosives and as a fuel additive for cleaning car exhaust gases. Urea is also believed to be a potential key building block for the formation of biological molecules such as RNA and DNA in connection with the question of the origin of life (
see ETH News from 28 June 2023
). Until now, the origin of urea itself on Early Earth has not been conclusively clarified.
A research team led by Ruth Signorell, Professor of Physical Chemistry at ETH Zurich, has discovered a previously unknown reaction pathway for the formation of urea that could provide an answer. The
external page
study
has just been published in the journal
Science
.
Chemistry on the water surface
Either high pressures and temperatures or chemical catalysts are needed for the industrial production of urea from ammonia (NH₃) and carbon dioxide (CO₂). Enzymes enable the same reaction to take place in humans and animals, removing toxic ammonia from the breakdown of proteins such as urea. As this simple molecule contains nitrogen as well as carbon and probably existed on the uninhabited Early Earth, many researchers view urea as a possible precursor for complex biomolecules.
“In our study, we show one way in which urea could have formed on the prebiotic Earth,” says Signorell – “namely where water molecules interact with atmospheric gases: on the water surface.”
Graphical representation of urea formation in a droplet  (Figure: Luis Quintero / ETH Zürich)
Reactor on the edge of a droplet
Signorell's team studied tiny water droplets such as those found in sea spray and fine mist. The researchers observed that urea can form spontaneously from carbon dioxide (CO₂) and ammonia (NH₃) in the surface layer of the droplets under ambient conditions. The physical interface between air and liquid creates a special chemical environment at the water surface that makes the spontaneous reaction possible.
As a droplet has a very large surface area in relation to its volume, chemical reactions mainly take place near this surface. Chemical concentration gradients form in this area, which acts like a microscopic reactor. The pH gradient across the interfacial layer of the water droplets creates the required acidic environment, which opens unconventional pathways that would otherwise not take place in liquids.
“The remarkable aspect of this reaction is that it takes place under ambient conditions without any external energy,” explains Mercede Mohajer Azizbaig, one of the two first authors. This not only makes the process interesting from a technical perspective but also provides valuable insights into processes that could be significant for evolution.
Experiment set-up
(Image: Doris Lujanovic / ETH Zürich)
The first authors conducting the experiment (Image: Doris Lujanovic / ETH Zurich)
Droplet is illuminated (Image: Doris Lujanovic / ETH Zurich)
A window into the early days of the Earth
The origin of life is currently the subject of a great deal of wide-ranging research, with different approaches being explored. First author Pallab Basuri explains: “Given such a controversial field of research, it was important for us to back up our observations.” Theoretical calculations by co-authors Evangelos Miliordos and Andrei Evdokimov from Auburn University supported the experimental findings and confirmed that the urea reaction on the droplets takes place without any external energy supply.
The results suggest that this natural reaction could also have been possible in the atmosphere of the Early Earth - an atmosphere that was rich in CO₂ and probably contained small traces of ammonia. In such environments, aqueous aerosols or fog droplets could have acted as natural reactors in which precursor molecules such as urea were formed. “Our study shows how seemingly mundane interfaces can become dynamic reaction spaces, suggesting that biological molecules may have a more common origin than

data.article_summary: 2025年5月，英国就业市场显示出谨慎复苏的迹象。尽管月度职位空缺略有下降，但年度增长保持正值，工资持续上涨，平均 advertised salary 达到 £42,403，同比增长9.38%。然而，入门级职位受到人工智能工具崛起的显著冲击，自2022年底以来下降了近三分之一。毕业生职位下降4.2%，而入门级职位现在仅占所有职位的25%。尽管某些行业如物流和教育招聘需求增加，但医疗和行政领域的职位空缺显著减少。总体而言，英国就业市场表现出谨慎乐观的态势，但人工智能对入门级职位的影响令人关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（如ChatGPT）与就业市场变化之间的关系，尤其是入门级职位减少的原因。

不同观点：
• bachmeier认为，就业市场的变化与疫情后招聘热潮的结束以及英国银行利率的上升有关，而非仅仅是AI的影响。他质疑AI hype中缺乏可靠的数据分析。
• ttul指出，在其软件公司中，LLM（大型语言模型）主要用于提高开发人员效率，而非直接取代低级职位。他认为，AI可以帮助低层员工转向更高层次的工作，而非单纯削减岗位。
• phtrivier对文章中将入门级职位减少直接归因于ChatGPT的说法提出质疑，尤其是对医疗、维护和家政行业的职位减少无法用AI解释。
• rel2thr分享了与小型企业会计主管的谈话，提到AI在会计应付账款解决方案中的应用，尽管这些解决方案不一定使用LLM，但AI的宣传确实促使企业寻求自动化而非雇佣新人。
• khelavastr明确表示，ChatGPT不应为物流、建筑、医疗等行业的入门级职位减少负责。
• reedf1认为，ChatGPT的引入可能导致短暂的招聘暂停，因为生产力提升的效果需要时间才能在市场需求中体现。
• rors指出，英国税收制度的变化也是 discourage 雇佣新员工的一个因素。
• josh2600提到，高利率和与R&D相关的税收规则变化导致公司无法投资于入门级职位。
• v5v3认为，文章的来源是为了寻求宣传的网络爬虫网站，不可轻信。他建议关注平均薪资和就业率的变化。
• falcor84对文章中数据的呈现方式提出批评，认为应提供更详细的数据表以明确趋势。
• b0a04gl用类比指出，入门级工作像是人类预训练层，现在这些工作可能被YouTube或训练营取代。
• alkonaut对AI直接导致就业市场变化的因果关系持怀疑态度，认为缺乏证据支持。
• chrsw通过历史类比指出，从打字机到计算机的转变仍需要人类操作，而现在试图制造“思考机器”可能带来更深远的影响。
• pfisherman认为，就业市场变化也可能与利率上升、税收增加和当前政策环境的不确定性有关。

补充讨论：
- AI在不同行业中的实际应用和影响存在争议，尤其是医疗、维护等行业。
- 税收政策和高利率等宏观经济因素被多次提及，作为影响就业市场变化的重要因素。
- 数据分析和证据的缺乏被认为是当前讨论中的一个关键问题，许多评论者呼吁更严谨的数据支持。
- 对AI取代入门级职位的实际效果存在不同看法，有人认为AI能提升员工能力，而非单纯替代。

44422040.article_content:
Artificial intelligence
Latest News
Economics, government & business
Job creation and losses
Labour market
Fall in entry-level jobs linked to rise of AI tools
by
Adam McCulloch
30 Jun 2025
by
Adam McCulloch
30 Jun 2025
Photograph: Koshiro K/Shutterstock
Photograph: Koshiro K/Shutterstock
The UK jobs market continued its cautious recovery in May, with annual vacancy growth and rising wages offering signs of resilience despite a modest monthly decline in job postings.
However, entry-level opportunities have taken a significant hit, dropping by nearly a third since the advent of widely available generative AI tools at the end of 2022.
According to the latest UK Job Market Report from job matching platform Adzuna, the number of advertised vacancies fell slightly by 0.51% in May to 858,465 roles.
Despite this, year-on-year growth remained positive at +0.49%, marking the third consecutive month of annual improvement and suggesting a slow but steady recovery from the recent market slump.
Pay award decisions
Bank of England says NIC rise is dampening pay rises
Pay awards in real terms could fall for ‘prolonged period’
NI increase has not caused ‘knee-jerk reaction’ in pay awards
Graduate pay vs living wage: an HR headache?
Pay continues to be a bright spot, with average advertised salaries rising for the twelfth month in a row. May saw the average advertised salary reach £42,403, up 0.3% from April and up 9.38% compared with a year earlier – making it the strongest run of annual pay growth since mid-2022. This rise has been bolstered in part by April’s 6.7% increase to the national living wage.
However, these broader improvements are not benefiting all parts of the workforce equally. Graduate job postings dropped by 4.2% in May and are now down 28.4% compared with the same time last year—the lowest level seen since July 2020.
More broadly, entry-level roles (including apprenticeships, internships and junior jobs) have declined by 32% since November 2022, when ChatGPT’s commercial breakthrough triggered a rapid transformation in how companies operate and hire.
Entry-level roles now make up just 25% of all jobs advertised in the UK, down from nearly 29% two years ago.
“May reinforced the sense that the job market in the UK is gradually regaining its footing,” said Andrew Hunter, co-founder of Adzuna. “While overall vacancies dipped slightly, we’ve now seen three straight months of annual vacancy growth – a clear shift after more than a year of decline. Advertised salaries continue to climb, too, with average pay up nearly 9% compared to last year, comfortably outpacing inflation.
“While certain sectors remain in strong demand and provide a backbone of stability, we will be keeping a close eye on the decline in roles for the previously steady healthcare and nursing sector and how that may play out over the coming months.”
The seasonal jobs market provided a boost in the run-up to summer. Logistics and warehouse vacancies rose by 9.77%, with creative and design (+6%) and hospitality and catering (+5.61%) also seeing monthly gains. Teaching vacancies increased by 1.63%, with over 169,000 roles live in May, keeping education the most active hiring sector in the UK.
By contrast, the healthcare and nursing sector – previously a consistent driver of job growth – saw vacancies fall by 10.21% in May. Other sectors with notable drops included admin (-9.22%), maintenance (-7.95%), and domestic help and cleaning (-5.72%).
Hiring times have improved slightly, with the average job now taking 35.8 days to fill, down from 39.5 days earlier in the year. However, competition has also intensified, with 2.02 jobseekers per vacancy (calculated by the ONS) in May – up from 1.98 in April. The north-east of England remains the most competitive region with 3.32 jobseekers per role, while south-west England is the least competitive at 1.32 per vacancy.
The number of jobseekers per vacancy increased in 10 of the UK’s 12 nations and regions in May.
Salaries continue to grow fastest in Northern Ireland, where advertised pay rose by 12.63% year-on-year to £40,726.
London remains the UK’s highest-paying region at £48,680, followed by eastern England at £41,013.
The most in-demand roles remain focused on essential services and accessible employment. Healthcare support workers topped Adzuna’s Trending Jobs list for the sixth consecutive month, followed by social care workers and sales assistants. Software developers also re-entered the top five, signalling renewed interest in skilled tech roles.
Despite continuing challenges in some sectors, the overall picture for the UK job market in May was one of cautious optimism – tempered by signs that the rise of AI and automation may be reshaping the landscape for entry-level workers.

data.title: Arm muscles into server market – but can't wrestle control from x86 just yet
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 2025年，基于Arm架构的服务器出货量预计将猛增70%，但仍未达到Arm公司希望占据全球数据中心CPU销售一半的目标。根据IDC数据，Arm服务器今年将占全球服务器出货量的21.1%，而x86架构服务器预计增长39.9%，达2839亿美元。尽管AI处理需求推动了服务器市场的快速增长，整体市场规模今年有望达到3660亿美元的新高，但Arm在数据中心市场的主导地位仍面临挑战。美国和中国是增长最快的地区，而加拿大因2024年的大单预计将下降9.6%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RISC-V与ARM在作为x86替代方案方面的竞争

不同观点：
• Pet_Ant认为RISC-V可能晚了5年，因为ARM已经成功取代x86成为另一种选择。这暗示ARM已经建立了强大的市场地位，RISC-V可能难以竞争。
• 对于Pet_Ant的观点，beardyw没有直接回应竞争问题，而是对新闻标题的写作风格进行了调侃，显示出对讨论的轻松态度。
• reverendsteveii引用并修改了Pet_Ant的观点，用“Arm muscles”来幽默地回应，暗示ARM通过其市场力量“强行”占据了替代x86的位置。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对ARM市场主导地位的看法，以及RISC-V是否能在已经存在强大竞争者的情况下成功进入市场。
• 幽默和文字游戏成为讨论的一部分，缓和了关于技术竞争的严肃话题。
• 争议的焦点可能在于RISC-V是否真的“太晚”，以及它是否有可能在未来挑战ARM的地位。

44422263.article_content:
Systems
Arm muscles into server market – but can't wrestle control from x86 just yet
Server shipments surge 70% in 2025, still shy of datacenter dominance goal
Dan Robinson
Mon 30 Jun 2025
//
11:27 UTC
Arm-based servers are rapidly gaining traction in the market with shipments tipped to jump 70 percent in 2025, however, this remains well short of the chip designer's ambitions to make up half of datacenter CPU sales worldwide by the end of the year.
Market watcher IDC says Arm servers are attracting mass interest thanks mainly to the launch of large rack-scale configurations, referring to systems such as
Nvidia's DGX GB200 NVL72
, designed for AI processing.
In its latest Worldwide Quarterly Server Tracker, IDC estimates that servers based on the Arm architecture will account for 21.1 percent of total global shipments this year - not the
50 percent touted by Arm infrastructure chief Mohamed Awad
in April.
Servers with at least one GPU fitted, sometimes styled as AI-capable, are projected to grow 46.7 percent, representing almost half of the total market value for this year. The fast pace of adoption by hyperscale customers and cloud service providers is fueling the server market, which IDC says is set to triple in size over just three years.
The server market as a whole reached a record $95.2 billion in Q1 2025, growing 134.1 percent year-on-year. As a result, IDC bumped up its forecast for the entire year to $366 billion, equating to a 44.6 percent rise. This would be an all-time high.
Japan's sequel to Fugaku supercomputer will be Arm'd to the teeth
SiPearl ships reference node design for Rhea1 high-spec Arm chip
Arm says it isn't worried by tariffs, but won't give guidance for FY'26
808 lines of BBC BASIC and a dream: Arm architecture turns 40
The "industry standard" x86 segment is projected to grow 39.9 percent during 2025 to reach $283.9 billion, while non-x86 systems are expected to grow faster at 63.7 percent year over year, with a forecast total of $82 billion.
IDC's regional market projections anticipate the US having the highest expansion with a 59.7 percent jump over 2024, which would see it account for almost 62 percent of the total server revenue by the end of 2025.
China is the other region heating up in the sales stakes, with IDC forecasting growth of 39.5 percent to make up more than 21 percent of the quarterly revenue worldwide. EMEA and Latin America are in single-digit growth territory at 7 and 0.7 percent, respectively, while Canada is expected to decline 9.6 percent this year due to an unspecified "very large deal" that happened in 2024.
Commenting on the server growth, IDC's veep for worldwide infrastructure research, Kuba Stolarski, said the demand for more compute power to handle AI processing is likely to persist.
"The evolution from simple chatbots to reasoning models to
agentic AI
will require several orders of magnitude more processing capacity, especially for inferencing." ®

data.title: So you want to serialize some DER?
data.author: lukastyrychtr
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在Rust中实现DER（ distinguished encoding representation）序列化时遇到的一些技术挑战和优化过程。DER是一种基于类型-长度-值（TLV）的二进制编码格式，其中长度的编码是可变长度的。作者维护了一个Rust库`rust-asn1`用于DER的解析和序列化，最初通过预留1字节来处理长度字段，但这在处理较大数据时效率不高。

作者尝试优化这一过程，让数据在序列化时直接报告其长度，以避免后续的数据复制。特别对于可变长度编码的整数（INTEGER），作者改进了计算其所需字节数的算法，减少了不必要的循环操作，并通过与Claude（AI助手）讨论，得出了一个无分支的计算方法。尽管代码更复杂，但理论上性能更优。最终，作者还研究了汇编代码以评估优化效果，虽然指令数量较多，但逻辑更为直接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于代码中不同路径和缓冲区安全性的讨论，以及对帖子标题和内容的评价。

不同观点：
• [benmmurphy] 认为在测量DER缓冲区长度和写入DER时使用两条非常不同的代码路径是危险的，尤其是在非Rust语言中。他指出，除非使用了安全的缓冲区实现，否则很难相信这两条路径不会因为行为分歧导致缓冲区溢出。

• [PeeMcGee] 则对帖子的标题和内容提出了不同的看法。他认为帖子的标题具有误导性，内容更像是在为Claude做隐性宣传，强调作者为Anthropic工作，并使用Claude来实现LLVM的优化。

补充讨论：
• [benmmurphy] 的观点集中在代码安全性上，特别是缓冲区溢出的潜在风险。他对于在非Rust语言中实现这种设计表示担忧，强调了安全实现的重要性。

• [PeeMcGee] 对帖子的动机和内容性质提出了质疑，认为帖子更像是一种广告，而非纯粹的技术讨论。这种观点指向了对内容真实性和目的的关注。

争议的焦点：
• 代码路径设计的安全性和潜在风险。
• 帖子标题和内容的真实性及动机。

44397482.article_content:
So you want to serialize some DER?
Fri, Jun 20, 2025
(Editor’s Note: My day job is at Anthropic.)
This story starts where all good stories start, with ASN.1. ASN.1 is… I guess you’d call it a meta-serialization format? It’s a syntax for describing data abstractly (a notation, you might say), and then there’s a bunch of different actual encodings that you can use to turn data into bytes. There’s only one encoding I choose to acknowledge, which is DER (the Distinguished Encoding Representation, it’s got a monocle and tophat). DER and ASN.1 are often used as synonyms, even though they’re technically not – it’s fine. I maintain a Rust library for doing DER parsing and serialization,
rust-asn1
(yes, I’m contributing to the naming confusion).
DER is a type-length-value (TLV) binary format. Which means serialized data is all of the form
[type code][length][value]
, where
value
is always
length
bytes long. (Let’s Encrypt has a great
introduction to DER
if you’re interested.) The way
length
is encoded is itself variable length, if length is 8, its encoded as a single
[0x08]
byte. If length is 100, its encoded two bytes
[0x81, 0x64]
. If you’re serializing some data, and you’re just filling in your buffer from left to right, this gives you an interesting challenge: either you need to know how long each
value
is going to be when you start serializing, or you have to do some tricks.
When I started this adventure,
rust-asn1
did tricks. Specifically, what it did is that when you went to serialize some value into a TLV, it reserved 1 byte of space for the length in the buffer, and then asked the value to write itself to the buffer. Then it compared the length of the buffer before and after, to see how long the value was. If the
length
fit in the 1 byte we reserved, we’d write it and be done. If not, we expand our buffer, copy the data to make space for the
length
, and then write the
length
in. The basic theory is that most TLVs are short, so this is fine in practice. If you’ve got a lot of larger TLVs, this will incur a whole bunch of extra copying, which is too bad.
So I went to do the obvious optimization: allow the value we’re encoding to tell
rust-asn1
how long its value will be, so that
rust-asn1
can just write out the length correctly the first time. Not rocket science. I wrote up a
benchmark
, then a
PR
(
claude-code
did the first draft of both), and admired my handiwork.
And then I started ruminating on how we pre-compute a value’s length. For lots of types its trivial, for an
OCTET STRING
its just the length of the data in bytes, for a
BOOLEAN
its always 1. What about
INTEGER
? Those are a variable length encoding. (It’s not the same encoding as we use for
length
, that would be too easy.) Here’s what the original implementation (which predated this optimization work) looked like, its inside of a macro which generates implementations for each integer width, hence the ugliness:

44397482.article_summary:
本文讨论了在Rust中实现DER（ distinguished encoding representation）序列化时遇到的一些技术挑战和优化过程。DER是一种基于类型-长度-值（TLV）的二进制编码格式，其中长度的编码是可变长度的。作者维护了一个Rust库`rust-asn1`用于DER的解析和序列化，最初通过预留1字节来处理长度字段，但这在处理较大数据时效率不高。

作者尝试优化这一过程，让数据在序列化时直接报告其长度，以避免后续的数据复制。特别对于可变长度编码的整数（INTEGER），作者改进了计算其所需字节数的算法，减少了不必要的循环操作，并通过与Claude（AI助手）讨论，得出了一个无分支的计算方法。尽管代码更复杂，但理论上性能更优。最终，作者还研究了汇编代码以评估优化效果，虽然指令数量较多，但逻辑更为直接。

data.title: Previously Unknown Structure Hiding Inside Human Cells
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 科学家发现了名为“hemifusome”的新细胞器，这是一种膜结合结构，充当细胞的回收中心，可能对治疗遗传疾病至关重要。该结构由弗吉尼亚大学和美国国立卫生研究院的研究人员通过冷冻电子断层扫描技术观察到，仅在需要时出现，参与细胞囊泡的形成与物质运输。尽管hemifusome存在短暂，但在某些细胞区域十分常见。研究人员希望进一步探索其形成和功能机制，以开发治疗复杂遗传疾病的新策略。研究已发表在《Nature Communications》上。

Scientists just discovered the hemifusome, a membrane-bound organelle that helps cells recycle cargo
Â© University of Virginia School of Medicine
Even after decades of peering into cells, biologists are still finding surprises.
In a twist, researchers at the University of Virginia and the National Institutes of Health uncovered a new organelle, dubbed the hemifusome. This tiny membrane-bound structure serves as a cellular recycling center and may hold the key to treating several genetic diseases. The research has been published in
Nature Communications.
âThis is like discovering a new recycling center inside the cell,â co-author Seham Ebrahim, a biophysicist at the University of Virginia, said in a
statement
. âWe think the hemifusome helps manage how cells package and process material, and when this process goes awry, it may contribute to diseases that affect many systems in the body.â
Scientists had not previously identified the structure because it only appears when needed. But thanks to cryo-electron tomographyâan imaging technique that flash-freezes cells and captures them in 3D and in near-atomic resolutionâresearchers were able to observe the ephemeral structure.
The researchers say hemifusomes may aid in the formation of cellular vesicles, tiny sacs that shuttle and combine material throughout the cell. They might also help form other organelles composed of multiple vesicles, the study suggests. However, some evidence shows that hemifusomes do not participate in endocytosis, the traditional pathway by which cells engulf external material.
âYou can think of vesicles like little delivery trucks inside the cell,â Ebrahim said in a statement. âThe hemifusome is like a loading dock where they connect and transfer cargo. Itâs a step in the process we didnât know existed.â
Despite their fleeting nature, hemifusomes are not rare. They appear to be surprisingly common in certain parts of cells, particularly near the cell membrane.
Still, scientists arenât exactly sure how or why hemifusomes form and then disappear. They’re hoping to find that outâas well as understand what happens when hemifusomes fail to function properly. Problems with how cells handle cargo are at the root of many genetic disorders.
âThis is just the beginning,â Ebrahim said in a statement. âNow that we know hemifusomes exist, we can start asking how they behave in healthy cells and what happens when things go wrong. That could lead us to new strategies for treating complex genetic diseases.â

data.title: Show HN: Vet – A tool for safely running remote shell scripts
data.author: a10r
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了一款名为 **vet** 的工具，旨在解决直接通过 `curl | bash` 安装脚本带来的安全风险。使用 `vet` 可以在执行远程脚本前，检查脚本变化、进行代码审查和语法分析（lint），并在执行前获得用户明确批准。具体步骤包括：  
1. **Fetch**：下载脚本到临时位置。  
2. **Diff & Review**：显示脚本更改。  
3. **Lint**：使用 shellcheck 分析潜在问题。  
4. **Confirm**：提示用户确认执行。  

文章还提供了安全安装 `vet` 的两种方式，强调手动审查脚本的重要性，避免盲目信任远程脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对通过网络获取并运行脚本的安全性及验证机制的讨论

不同观点：
• kevincox：质疑通过HTTPS获取的安装程序如何进行验证，指出仅有部分软件经过签名和验证，而大多数情况下没有额外的验证步骤。他还提到，直接从发行版安装可能会提供更好的验证机制，而目前这种方式提供的信心不足。
• alganet：担心恶意脚本可能通过使用`# shellcheck disable=`指令绕过检查，质疑安全性。
• calrain：指出盲目信任远程脚本（如使用`curl | bash`模式）存在风险，并讽刺这种做法。
• a10r：作为`vet`工具的开发者，解释了`vet`的开发初衷和设计理念，强调在执行脚本前进行diff和shellcheck检查，并征求反馈。
• 3abiton：对`vet`表示赞赏，但提到在很多情况下由于信任代码维护者，用户往往会妥协并直接运行代码。
• thealistra：询问`vet`工具的具体使用方式，如是否会打开pager或编辑器，以及如何展示shellcheck的问题。
• gardnr：建议增加一个新功能，将脚本内容传递给LLM（大型语言模型）以识别潜在的安全问题。
• charcircuit：指出当前解决方案的不足之处，认为应该在用户执行`curl | bash`时自动进行扫描，类似于Windows的自动扫描功能。
• nodesocket：认为阅读和理解长达数百行的bash脚本是不现实的，倾向于直接执行脚本。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于`curl | bash`模式的安全性以及如何有效验证脚本的可靠性。
• a10r提出的通过`vet`工具增加安全性，包括脚本diff和shellcheck检查，获得了一定的认可，但用户对实际操作中的复杂性表示担忧。
• 增加LLM分析脚本安全性的建议引发了对非确定性和隐私风险的讨论。
• 对工具自动化的需求，包括自动扫描和支持私有环境的讨论，也被提出并受到关注。

44407661.article_content:
vet
Don't just run it —
vet
it.
Stop blindly piping to bash.
vet
lets you inspect remote scripts for changes, run them through a linter, and require your explicit approval before they can execute.
The Problem
We've all seen this pattern for installing software:
# You're blindly trusting the remote script.
curl -sSL https://example.com/install.sh | bash
This is dangerous. The script could be malicious, the server could be compromised, or a transient network error could result in executing a partial script.
The Solution
vet
wraps this process in a secure, interactive workflow:
Fetch:
It downloads the remote script to a temporary location.
Diff & Review:
It shows you what, if anything, has changed since the last time you ran this script.
Lint:
If you have shellcheck installed, it automatically analyzes the script for potential bugs or malicious patterns.
Confirm:
It prompts you for explicit approval before executing anything.
# The new, safer way.
vet https://example.com/install.sh
Installation
The Safe Way (Recommended)
This is the two-step "Download, then Review" process that
vet
automates.
Download the installer:
Choose one of the following sources. The first is the official project domain, and the second is a direct link to the GitHub release asset.
Option A: Official project domain
curl -o install_vet.sh https://getvet.sh/install.sh
Option B: Direct GitHub Release Link
curl -L -o install_vet.sh https://github.com/vet-run/vet/releases/latest/download/install.sh
Review the installer's code.
Open it in a text editor or use less to ensure it's not doing anything suspicious. It's a simple script that downloads the correct
vet
script and moves it to /usr/local/bin.
less install_vet.sh
Run the installer you just vetted:
sh install_vet.sh
Congratulations! You just manually performed the process that
vet
will now automate for you.
The "Trusting" One-Liner
In your terminal, run:
# Don't actually do this. That's the whole point.
curl -sL https://getvet.sh/install.sh | sh
➤ View the source on
GitHub

data.title: A CarFax for Used PCs; Hewlett Packard wants to give old laptops new life
data.author: rubenbe
data.article_summary: HP公司正计划通过推出一项类似于CarFax的服务，为二手笔记本电脑注入新的活力。该项目旨在为二手PC创建一个透明的历史记录，包括设备的使用情况、维修记录和性能数据，从而提升二手市场的信任度和产品价值。这项举措不仅能帮助消费者更好地了解所购设备的背景，还能通过延长设备使用寿命来促进环保。HP团队由多位资深专家组成，他们共同致力于开发这一创新解决方案，以推动循环经济和可持续发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HP计划引入类似CarFax的系统，用于记录和存储电脑的遥测数据，以便在二手交易中提供设备历史报告。这一计划引发了关于其实用性、隐私问题以及对设备升级和维修的影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• [mrweasel] 认为CarFax的类比对美国以外的人没有意义，并质疑将报告存储在SSD上的做法。如果用户更换SSD，数据将丢失，且HP如果不使SSD易于更换，将违背其初衷。此外，提到如果HP真的关心用户，应该让设备更易于维修和升级。
• [trollbridge] 认为“CarFax for used PCs”的类比不恰当，因为旧机器的当前状态可以快速评估，且大多数维修只是更换整个主板，记录过去的维修历史没有太大意义。同时指出，旧笔记本电脑的价值不高，因为性能较差且设计寿命较短。
• [stefan_] 批评HP的产品质量，指出其笔记本电脑电池问题频发，暗示对HP能否做好这一系统缺乏信心。
• [msgodel] 认为HP是最不可能做好这件事的公司，表达了对HP的不信任。
• [999900000999] 认为这是对隐私的严重侵犯，且收益甚微。指出SSD是易耗品，可以简单更换，企业应有销毁SSD的政策。
• [bigyabai] 担心这一系统最初可能是为了善意目的开发，但最终可能被用作禁止第三方维修的借口，视为不诚实的日志操纵。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者对HP的产品质量和设计寿命提出质疑，认为旧设备的价值不高，且维修和升级困难。
• 隐私问题是一个争议焦点，特别是将数据存储在SSD上的做法被视为潜在的隐私风险。
• 讨论中还涉及企业社会责任和设备可持续性问题，指出软件公司应努力保持旧设备的可用性。
• 有人对HP作为品牌的信任度提出质疑，认为其产品和政策不够用户友好。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在HP引入这一系统的实用性和隐私问题上。一方面是其实际应用价值和用户需求是否匹配，另一方面是数据存储和隐私保护的平衡。

data.title: I Write Type Safe Generic Data Structures in C
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了在C语言中实现类型安全的通用数据结构的方法。作者展示了一种利用联合（unions）来关联类型信息的技术，通过实现一个简单的链表来说明。文章比较了三种不同的通用性实现方式：

1. **通用头文件**：使用宏定义来实现，但会导致代码可读性和维护性差，二进制体积增大，且需要使用类型前缀函数。
   
2. **使用void***：通过void指针实现通用性，但不类型安全，且存在内存和性能问题。

3. **内联存储**：使用柔性数组成员存储数据，解决内存和性能问题，但需要传递数据大小。

最后，作者提出了**类型检查**级别，通过使用带有payload成员的联合来实现类型安全的通用数据结构，确保编译时捕获类型错误。这种方法结合了类型安全和高效内存管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言中的泛型数据结构实现及其类型安全

不同观点：
• **gritzko**：认为使用C语言可以创建整个 dialect，并提供了一个基于C的通用二进制堆实现作为例子。他指出这种方法的缺点是语法不如C++模板优雅，但优势在于产生的是扁平的C结构体。同时，他批评了基于void*和运行时内存调整的实现方式，认为这是很大的缺点。

• **eqvinox**：提出了一种使用联合（union）和typeof()来实现类型安全的思路，但也表示他们使用了定义包装器的大宏来实现侵入式数据结构。他认为使用联合和typeof可能可行，但不确定如何具体实现。

• **HexDecOctBin**：强调了使用函数指针的类型来实现类型安全，而不是使用类似Sean Barrett的stretchy_buffers的"handle"类型。他还提到了C23标准解决了C语言类型比较的问题，并提供了相关文档链接，指出GCC和Clang已经支持但MSVC尚未支持。

• **asplake**：表示正在开发一个类似ML风格的C语言变体和相关函数的生成器，并计划在完成后检查是否能兼容当前讨论的技巧。

June 25, 2025・7 minute read
I write type safe generic data structures in C using a technique that I haven’t seen elsewhere
1
. It uses unions to associate type information with a generic data structure, but we’ll get to that. My approach works for any type of data structure: maps, arrays, binary trees… but for this article I illustrate the ideas by implementing a basic linked list. Since many people aren’t aware you can do C generics
at all
, I figured I’d start simple and build up to this:
typedef
struct
{
int
value
;
}
Foo
;
List

int
)
int_list
=
{
0
};

(
&

,
3
);

0
};

(
&
foo_list
,
(

});

(

foo_list
,
(

){
3

(
item
,
&
foo_list
)
{
// `item` is of type `Foo *`
printf
(
"%i
\n
"
,
item
->
value
);
}
Generics level 0: Generic Headers
I hesitate to even mention this, because I do not like it
2
, but its worth comparing to the technique at the end of this article. It works like this: you write your data structure in a header, using macros for your types, and then
#include
the header multiple times; once for each type the data structure will be used with.
Click to see the Code

#error "T must be defined before including this header"
#endif
#define _CONCAT(a, b) a##b
#define CONCAT(a, b) _CONCAT(a, b)

NODE_TYPE

44425461.article_summary:
本文介绍了在C语言中实现类型安全的通用数据结构的方法。作者展示了一种利用联合（unions）来关联类型信息的技术，通过实现一个简单的链表来说明。文章比较了三种不同的通用性实现方式：

1. **通用头文件**：使用宏定义来实现，但会导致代码可读性和维护性差，二进制体积增大，且需要使用类型前缀函数。
   
2. **使用void***：通过void指针实现通用性，但不类型安全，且存在内存和性能问题。

3. **内联存储**：使用柔性数组成员存储数据，解决内存和性能问题，但需要传递数据大小。

最后，作者提出了**类型检查**级别，通过使用带有payload成员的联合来实现类型安全的通用数据结构，确保编译时捕获类型错误。这种方法结合了类型安全和高效内存管理。

data.title: There Are No New Ideas in AI Only New Datasets
data.author: bilsbie
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）领域的进展，指出尽管AI在过去十五年中取得了显著进步，但所谓的突破性新想法实际上很少，大部分进展源于新数据集的应用。作者认为，大型语言模型（LLMs）的发展可以归纳为四个关键突破：深度神经网络、Transformer模型、基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）和推理能力。尽管这些技术推动了AI进步，但其基础机制早在1990年代甚至更早就已存在，主要依赖于监督学习和强化学习等已有方法。文章还提到，尽管研究界不断产生增量式进步，但近期的巨大模型如Grok 3和GPT-4.5仅带来边际改善，AI能力的某些宣称可能被夸大。总体而言，AI的持续进步更多依赖于数据集的更新而非全新理念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）的现状与未来发展方向

不同观点：
• voxleone：认为当前AI在语言和视觉领域取得了显著进展，但仅触及了人工智能潜力的表面。人类智能是多模态的，涉及到触觉、味觉、嗅觉、运动感知、情感等多个维度，而当前的AI主要集中在文本和图像上。未来的AI发展需要新的硬件、数据表示和训练方法，以实现从经验中学习，而不仅仅是通过模式识别。

• tippytippytango：指出技术和科学进步的区别。科学进步 unlock 新技术的S曲线，但这些技术在进入收益递减阶段后，进展会放缓。人们往往混淆了快速优化期的技术进步与真正的科学突破。

• kogus：认为如果一个系统能够成功再现人类智能，那么改变数据集可能是实现不同模型的关键。人类的记忆、训练、教育和背景是我们解决问题能力的重要组成部分。

• rar00：不同意kogus的观点，指出已经有一些组织在探索新的路径。虽然沿用旧算法并添加新数据是常见的策略，但也有私人组织在秘密研发新想法。

• jschveibinz：尊重 rar00 的观点，但认为所有新想法都源自旧想法。AI作为工具，可以快速访问旧想法并提供新的视角，创新往往是在识别旧想法的漏洞、交叉点和切线中实现的。

• ks2048：认为最新的LLM只是在进行四则运算，这种技术早在4000年前的巴比伦人就已实现，因此对当前AI的突破性持怀疑态度。

• ctoth：讽刺地指出，通过自我对弈进行强化学习的Alpha系列（如AlphaGo）等成就，不可能只是数据集的功劳。

• luppy47474：仅表示思考（无明确观点）。

• anon291：认为虽然SaaS领域没有新想法，但新应用已经取得了很好的效果。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是AI的真正前沿是否在于多模态和经验学习，还是仅仅通过优化现有算法和数据集即可实现突破。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对科学进步与技术进步之间关系的理解，以及如何定义和识别真正的创新。
• 不同评论者对AI创新路径的看法存在分歧，有的强调新硬件和数据表示的重要性，有的则认为新想法往往是旧想法的重新应用。

LLMs were invented in four major developments... all of which were datasets

Most people know that AI has made unbelievable progress over the last fifteen years– especially in the last five. It might feel like that progress is
*inevitable*
– although large paradigm-shift-level breakthroughs are uncommon, we march on anyway through a stream of slow & steady progress. In fact, some researchers have recently declared a
“Moore’s Law for AI”
where the computer’s ability to do certain things (in this case, certain types of coding tasks) increases exponentially with time:
the proposed “Moore’s Law for AI”. (by the way, anyone who thinks they can run an autonomous agent for an hour with no intervention as of April 2025 is fooling themselves)
Although I don’t really agree with this specific framing for a number of reasons, I can’t deny the trend of progress. Every year, our AIs get a little bit smarter, a little bit faster, and a little bit cheaper, with no end in sight.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
Most people think that this continuous improvement comes from a steady supply of ideas from the research community across academia – mostly MIT, Stanford, CMU – and industry – mostly Meta, Google, and a handful of Chinese labs, with lots of research done at other places that we’ll never get to learn about.
And we certainly have made a lot of progress due to research, especially on the systems side of things. This is how we’ve made models cheaper in particular. Let me cherry-pick a few notable examples from the last couple years:
- in 2022 Stanford researchers gave us
FlashAttention
, a better way to utilize memory in language models that’s used literally everywhere;
- in 2023 Google researchers developed
speculative decoding
, which all model providers use to speed up inference (also developed at
DeepMind
, I believe concurrently?)
- in 2024 a ragtag group of internet fanatics developed
Muon
, which seems to be a better optimizer than SGD or Adam and may end up as the way we train language models in the future
- in 2025 DeepSeek released
DeepSeek-R1
, an open-source model that has equivalent reasoning power to similar closed-source models from AI labs (specifically Google and OpenAI)
So we’re definitely figuring stuff out. And the reality is actually cooler than that: we’re engaged in a decentralized globalized exercise of Science, where findings are shared openly on
ArXiv
and at conferences and on social media and every month we’re getting incrementally smarter.
If we’re doing so much important research, why do some argue that progress is slowing down?
People are still complaining
. The two most recent huge models,
Grok 3
and
GPT-4.5
, only obtained a marginal improvement on capabilities of their predecessors. In one particularly salient example, when
language models were evaluated on the latest math olympiad exam
, they scored only 5%, indicating that
recent announcements may have been overblown
when reporting system ability.
And if we try to chronicle the
*big*
breakthroughs, the real paradigm shifts, they seem to be happening at a different rate. Let me go through a few that come to mind:
LLMs in four breakthroughs
1. Deep neural networks: Deep neural networks first took off after the
AlexNet model
won an image recognition competition in 2012
2. Transformers + LLMs: in 2017 Google proposed transformers in
Attention Is All You Need
, which led to
BERT
(Google, 2018) and the original
GPT
(OpenAI, 2018)
3. RLHF: first proposed (to my knowledge) in the
InstructGPT paper
from OpenAI in 2022
4. Reasoning: in 2024 OpenAI released O1, which led to DeepSeek R1
If you squint just a little, these four things (DNNs → Transformer LMs → RLHF → Reasoning) summarize everything that’s happened in AI. We had DNNs (mostly image recognition systems), then we had text classifiers, then we had chatbots, now we have reasoning models (whatever those are).
Say we want to make a fifth such breakthrough; it could help to study the four cases we have here. What new research ideas led to these groundbreaking events?
It’s not crazy to argue that
all the underlying mechanisms of these breakthroughs existed in the 1990s,
if not before. We’re applying relatively simple neural network architectures and doing either supervised learning (1 and 2) or reinforcement learning (3 and 4).
Supervised learning via cross-entropy, the main way we pre-train language models, emerged from Claude Shannon’s work in the 1940s.
Reinforcement learning, the main way we post-train language models via RLHF and reasoning training, is slightly newer. It can be traced to the
introduction of policy-gradient me

data.title: Auth for B2B SaaS: it's not like auth for consumer software
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了B2B软件与B2C软件在身份认证（auth）方面的关键区别，指出B2B认证不能简单照搬B2C模式。主要从三个方面进行比较：

1. **逻辑隔离与租户模型**：在B2C中，用户是直接客户，拥有独立账户和数据控制权。而在B2B中，企业客户需要控制其用户访问权限，用户权限不同，租户模型以公司为核心，如Slack的“工作区”。

2. **优先级与权衡**：B2B软件需要考虑企业控制、合规性等，而B2C更注重用户体验和快速增长。

3. **协议与功能**：B2B需要支持复杂的权限管理和跨公司协作功能，而B2C通常只需简单用户管理。

作者建议在设计初期就考虑这些区别，以避免后续复杂重构。B2B认证需要适应企业的多租户和权限管理需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：身份验证与授权系统的复杂性及其解决方案

不同观点：
• weitendorf 认为身份验证（Auth）的复杂性源于过度复杂化的设计，实际上只需要关注身份（Identity）和授权模型（Authorization model）两个核心概念。消费者和B2B的Auth差异主要体现在身份管理和授权模型的不同。消费者通常依赖第三方（如Gmail、Facebook）来管理身份，而企业则通过域名和邮箱控制员工身份。此外，消费者默认只能访问自己的数据，而企业中管理员可以访问企业的全部数据，因此需要通过角色和权限来限制访问。最终问题归结为互联网缺乏良好的身份管理系统，导致依赖基于电子邮件和域名的账户体系，这种集中化信息管理模式存在权限升级的漏洞。

• nijave 同意weitendorf的观点，但补充提到OpenIDC作为SAML的前身，具有无需处理证书到期的优点，并且被广泛支持。

• skeptrune 指出处理类似"让所有人使用Yubikey"这种超级烦人的要求是一个痛点，表示愿意购买解决方案来解决这一问题。

• funerr 提问，想了解该方案与better-auth的比较。

• nylonstrung 提问，想了解该方案与zitadel的比较。

补充讨论：
• koakuma-chan 提供了一个链接，但链接似乎出现了客户端异常，无法访问。

争议焦点：
• 对于身份验证和授权系统的简化方案存在不同实现方式的讨论，例如OpenIDC、better-auth和zitadel等，各有其支持者与应用场景。用户对于如何选择适合的解决方案存在疑问，特别是比较不同工具之间的优劣。

总体来看，讨论的核心在于如何简化身份验证和授权系统，同时有效解决实际应用中的复杂性与安全问题。不同用户对具体工具和实现方式有各自的偏好和疑问。

44424256.article_content:
Auth for B2B SaaS: it's not like auth for consumer software
Ned O'Leary
Cofounder and CEO, Tesseral
Auth
for business software (B2B) shouldn’t look the same as auth for consumer software  (B2C). In many cases, it actually
can’t
work the same way.
I’ll cover three important buckets of differences between B2B auth and B2C auth:
Logical isolation and tenancy models
Priorities and trade-offs
Protocols and features
By the way – let’s use
auth
loosely here and let it subsume related stuff like user management. Similarly, let’s just imagine away the vague grey area between consumers and businesses (e.g., software for sole proprietors) and focus solely on obvious consumer apps and obvious enterprise products. A simplified model of the world helps make things clear.
Logical isolation and tenancy models
In B2C software, your customers are your users. They’re individual people that control their own accounts. Things don’t work that way in B2B software. Businesses want to control their users’ access; and within a given business, not all users should work the same way. This has pretty significant implications for auth.
Let’s first look at tenancy in consumer software and then take a glance at business software.
Users: First-class tenancy in consumer software
In a consumer application, we primarily care about individual users.
To illustrate what this looks like, I went to Club Penguin Legacy and created an account for myself. Signing up for a CPL account is pretty easy. Aside from email verification, all you need is a username and a password.
Club Penguin associates all of my data with my penguin. I get to edit some of my penguin’s data if I want. For example, each penguin gets an igloo. I get to edit my own igloo.
No one else gets to edit my igloo.
If I want to upgrade my igloo, Club Penguin checks to see how many coins I have. This is a property that’s associated with my user account. Regrettably, I do not have enough coins to purchase the undersea igloo theme.
None of what I’ve covered here should seem surprising. This all seems kind of obvious – kind of normal – doesn’t it?
I have an account for myself, and data lives on the account level. I alone exercise control over my account. My content is mine, at least in the sense that it doesn’t belong to another user. It’s just me and the penguin.
Isn’t this how pretty much all software works
, you might wonder. This is how we learn to build software in school, right? It’s the most obvious way to implement logical isolation; it makes intuitive sense.
But this tenancy model doesn’t work for business software. If you use the Club Penguin tenancy model in business software, you’re going to have a very bad time.
Organizations: First-class tenancy in business software
The tenancy model for business software doesn’t put end users first. When you’re selling B2B, your customer isn’t an end user. It’s more complicated than that. Your customer is a company. And the company wants control over its users.
I like to use Slack as an example here.
If you’ve ever used Slack, you have a sense for what it’s like. You can send passive aggressive GIFs to your coworkers. You can upload custom reactions that are just cropped pictures of your boss’s face lifted from college-era Facebook photos. You can scroll all the way up in #general to find gossip that HR hasn’t thought to remove.
All of Slack’s useful features require that you and your colleagues can exchange messages, so you all need to be clustered together in the same software-defined place. Slack calls these places
Workspaces
. Normally, each
Workspace
maps onto a unique business customer. And end users – employees of business customers – all belong to
Workspaces
. We can say that the
Workspace
is the first-class tenant. We can say that a
tenancy firewall
exists between such tenants.
Business software pretty much always implements tenancy like this. You need some concept of company-level tenancy to support the features that business customers expect. (More on this later.)
Now, in the real world, this actually ends up being a bit complicated. Keeping Slack as an example, one of my former employers actually had dozens of Workspaces across the company; IT had some convoluted enterprise-y way of managing these in a hierarchy. Plus, Slack now has its Connect feature that allows you to communicate across tenants. But let’s imagine all of these wrinkles away.
It’s certainly possible to bolt-on a B2B multitenancy model when you already have some users. We see this from time to time. However, it's usually complicated and laborious. A lot of sensitive code needs to get rewritten when you change your tenancy model.
Life is easier when you get this right from the start.
Different priorities
Performance at scale
Consumer software must always anticipate the possibility of many users.
At the extreme end of scale, Meta, reports 3.35
billion
Daily Active People (DAP) across its different applications (Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, etc.). Even a relatively

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同方式绘制数据以揭示隐藏假设和偏见，以及主观预测的价值和局限性。

不同观点：
• MarkusQ认为，通过用多种方式绘制同一数据（如对数刻度、不同指标随时间的变化等），并进行相同的推断，可以揭示隐藏的假设或思维漏洞。他强调，如果结果不一致，往往能发现思维中的缺陷。
• Keeganpoppen赞赏主观预测的价值，并指出将事物简化为数学模型可能带来的偏见。他认为有无数可能的模型，且模型可能会被用来支持任何论点。他还提到，涂鸦方法对假设数量敏感，能揭示不同假设间的相互作用，但也可能将所有假设视为等概率。
• Groby_b批评了AI 2027报告的简化推断方法，认为通过涂鸦模型可以更好地进行预测。他强调这种方法能引导探索替代方案并暴露偏见，且因其简单性而更具实用价值。

补充讨论：
• Keeganpoppen进一步讨论了涂鸦方法的应用，建议在选择假设和模型时应有思考，并提到低分辨率的直线绘制有助于表达思维路径，而不必拘泥于数学模型的形式。
• 争议的焦点在于对数学模型的过度依赖及其潜在的偏见和简化性。Keeganpoppen和Groby_b都指出了模型选择和使用中的主观性和暴露偏见的重要性。
• 各方都认同涂鸦方法在揭示假设和偏见方面的实用性，并计划将其纳入自己的分析工具包中。

Scribble-based forecasting and AI 2027
Scribble-based forecasting and AI 2027
Jun 2025
Two kinds of forecasts
The AI 2027 forecast
Scribble-based forecasting
Comments at
lemmy
,
substack
.
Mistakes?
fix plz
(If you just want to see what happens, go
here
.)
AI 2027
forecasts that AGI could plausibly arrive as early as 2027. I recently spent some time looking at both the
timelines forecast
and some critiques [
1
,
2
,
3
].
Initially, I was interested in technical issues. What’s the best super-exponential curve? How much probability should it have? But I found myself drawn to a more basic question. Namely, how much value is the math really contributing?
This provides an excuse for a general rant. Say you want to forecast something. It could be when your hair will go gray or if Taiwan will be self-governing in 2050. Whatever. Here’s one way to do it:
Think hard.
Make up some numbers.
Don’t laugh—that’s the classic method. Alternatively, you could use math:
Think hard.
Make up a formal model / math / simulation.
Make up some numbers.
Plug those numbers into the formal model.
People are often skeptical of intuition-based forecasts because, “Those are just some numbers you made up.” Math-based forecasts are hard to argue with. But that’s not because they lack made-up numbers. It’s because the meaning of those numbers is mediated by a bunch of math.
So which is better, intuition or math? In what situations?
Here, I’ll look at that question and how it applies to AI 2027. Then I’ll build a new AI forecast using my personal favorite method of “plot the data and scribble a bunch of curves on top of it”. Then I’ll show you a little tool to make your own artisanal scribble-based AI forecast.
Two kinds of forecasts
To get a sense of the big picture, let’s look at two different forecasting problems.
First, here’s a forecast (based on the
IPCC 2023 report
) for Earth’s temperature. There are two curves, corresponding to different assumptions about future greenhouse gas emissions.
Those curves look unassuming. But there are a lot of moving parts behind them. These kinds of forecasts model atmospheric pressure, humidity, clouds, sea currents, sea surface temperature, soil moisture, vegetation, snow and ice cover, surface albedo, population growth, economic growth, energy, and land use. They also model the interactions between all those things.
That’s hard. But we basically understand how all of it works, and we’ve spent a ludicrous amount of effort carefully building the models. If you want to forecast global surface temperature change, this is how I’d suggest you do it. Your brain can’t compete, because it can’t grind through all those interactions like a computer can.
OK, but here’s something else I’d really like to forecast: Where is this blue line going to go?
You
could
forecast this using a “mechanistic model” like with climate above. To do that, you’d want to model the probability Iran develops a nuclear weapon and what Saudi Arabia / Turkey / Egypt might do in response. And you’d want to do the same thing for Poland / South Korea / Japan and their neighbors. You’d also want to model future changes in demographics, technology, politics, technology, economics, military conflicts, etc.
In
principle
, that would be the best method. As with climate, there are too many plausible futures for your tiny brain to work through. But building that model would be very hard, because it basically requires you to model the whole world. And if there’s an error anywhere, it could have serious consequences.
In practice, I’d put more trust in intuition. A talented human (or
AI
?) forecaster would probably take an
outside view
like, “Over the last 80 years, the number of countries has gone up by 9, so in 2105, it might be around 18.” Then, they’d consider adjusting for things like, “Will other countries might learn from the example of North Korea?” or “Will chemical enrichment methods become practical?”
Intuition can’t churn through possible futures the way a simulation can. But if you don’t
have
a reliable simulator, maybe that’s OK.
Broadly speaking, math/simulation-based forecasts shine when the phenomena you’re interested in has two properties.
It evolves according to some well-understood rule-set.
The
behavior
of the ruleset is relatively complex.
The first is important because if you don’t have a good model for the ruleset (or at least your
uncertainty
about the ruleset), how will you build a reliable simulator? The second is important because if the behavior is simple, why do you even need a simulator?
The ideal thing to forecast with math is something like
Conway’s game of life
. Simple known rules, huge emergent complexity. The worst thing to forecast with math is something like the probability that Jesus Christ returns next year. You could make up some math for that, but what would be the point?
The AI 2027 forecast
This post is (ostensibly) about AI

data.title: Cloud-forming isoprene & terpenes from crops may drastically improve climate
data.author: gsf_emergency_2
data.article_summary: 2025年6月26日，《Science》期刊文章指出，科学家开始揭示生命体如何促进云层形成，这可能大幅改善气候科学。研究显示，植物、浮游生物和海浪飞沫释放的微小颗粒能进入大气，帮助云层形成。这些颗粒作为凝结核，促使水蒸气凝结成云滴。通过深入了解这一过程，科学家可以更准确地预测气候变化模型，因为云层对地球的辐射平衡和温度调节起着关键作用。研究借助科研飞机收集高空大气数据，进一步验证了这些发现。这项研究有助于改进气候预测和应对全球变暖的策略。

44423263.article_summary: 2025年6月26日，《Science》期刊文章指出，科学家开始揭示生命体如何促进云层形成，这可能大幅改善气候科学。研究显示，植物、浮游生物和海浪飞沫释放的微小颗粒能进入大气，帮助云层形成。这些颗粒作为凝结核，促使水蒸气凝结成云滴。通过深入了解这一过程，科学家可以更准确地预测气候变化模型，因为云层对地球的辐射平衡和温度调节起着关键作用。研究借助科研飞机收集高空大气数据，进一步验证了这些发现。这项研究有助于改进气候预测和应对全球变暖的策略。

data.title: Data Centers, Temperature, and Power
data.author: quectophoton
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了数据中心的电力消耗和温度管理问题。数据中心的需求随着全球连接的增加和人工智能的发展而急剧上升。电力是运营数据中心最大的成本之一，全球数据中心消耗了约7.4吉瓦的电力，占全球总电力的1-1.3%，而整个IT行业的能源消耗则占全球的10%。数据中心需要不间断运行，因此配备了多重供电系统，包括电网、发电机和高科技电池系统。

电力使用效率通过“电力使用效率（PUE）”来衡量，该指标将总能耗与计算设备能耗进行比较。冷却系统消耗约40%的电力，是能耗的重要组成部分。任何电力使用都会产生热量，服务器在高负荷工作（如处理人工智能任务）时会产生更多热量。温度控制不仅依赖冷却系统，还涉及服务器布局、人员活动和环境温度等多重因素。

44398743.article_content:
It’s easy to open a data center, right? All you have to do is connect a bunch of
hard drives
to power and the internet, find a building, and you’re off to the races.
Well, not exactly. Building and using one
Storage Pod
is quite a bit different than managing exabytes of data. As the world has grown more connected, the
demand for data centers
has grown—and then along comes artificial intelligence (AI), with
processing and storage demands
that amp up
the need
even more.
That, of course, has real-world impacts, and we’re here to chat about why. Today we’re going to talk about power, one of the single biggest costs to running a data center, how it has impacts far beyond a simple utility bill, and what role temperature plays in things.
How Much Power Does a Data Center Use?
There’s no “normal” when it comes to the total amount of power a data center will need, as data centers vary in size. Here are a few figures that can help us get us on the same page about scale:
The
largest data center market
in the world is in Northern Virginia in the United States and it has a 2,552
megawatt
capacity. (By the way: 1MW = 1 million watts. For context, one megawatt is enough energy to power about 200 American homes.)
In 2023, data centers consumed
7.4 gigawatts of power
. (1GW = 1 billion watts.)
That’s approximately
1–1.3% of total power
in the world. Expand that to all IT energy demand, and that number is about
10% of global energy consumption
.
The goal of a data center is to be always online. That means that there are redundant systems of power—so, what comes in from the grid as well as generators and high-tech battery systems like uninterruptible power supplies (UPS)—running 24 hours a day to keep servers storing and processing data and connected to networks. In order to keep all that equipment running well, they need to stay in a
healthy temperature (and humidity) range
, which sounds much, much simpler than it is.
Measuring Power Usage
One of the most popular metrics for tracking power efficiency in data centers is
power usage effectiveness (PUE)
, which is the ratio of the total amount of energy used by a data center to the energy delivered to computing equipment.
Note that this metric divides power usage into two main categories: what you spend keeping devices online (which we’ll call “IT load” for shorthand purposes), and “overhead”, which is largely comprised of the power dedicated to cooling your data center down.
There are valid
criticisms of the metric
, including that improvements to IT load will actually make your metric worse: You’re being more efficient about IT power, but your overhead stays the same—so less efficiency even though you’re using less power overall. Still, it gives companies a repeatable way to measure against themselves and others over time, including directly comparing seasons year to year, so it’s a widely adopted metric.
Calculating your IT load is a relatively predictable number. Manufacturers tell you the wattage of your device (or you can
calculate it
based on your device’s specs), then you take that number and
plan for it being always online
. The sum of all your devices running 24 hours a day is your IT power spend.
Comparatively, doing the same for cooling is a bit more complicated—and it accounts for
approximately 40% of power usage
.
What Increases Temperature in a Data Center?
Any time you’re using power, you’re creating heat. So the first thing you consider is always your IT load. You don’t want your servers overtaxed—most folks agree that you want to run at about 80% of capacity to keep things kosher—but you also don’t want to have a bunch of servers sitting around idle when you return to off-peak usage. Even at rest, they’re still consuming power.
So, the methodology around temperature mitigation always starts at power reduction—which means that growth, IT efficiencies, right-sizing for your capacity, and even device provisioning are an inextricable part of the conversation. And, you create
more
heat when you’re asking an electrical component to work harder—so,
more processing for things like AI tasks means more power
and more heat.
And, there are a number of other things that can compound or create heat: the types of drives or processors in the servers, the layout of the servers within the data center, people, lights, and the ambient temperature just on the other side of the data center walls.
Brief reminder that servers look like this:
Only most of them aren’t as beautifully red as ours.
When you’re building a server, fundamentally what you’re doing is shoving a bunch of electrical components in a box. Yes, there are design choices about those boxes that help mitigate temperature, but just like a smaller room heating up more quickly than a warehouse, you are containing and concentrating a heat source.
We humans generate heat and need lights to see, so the folks who work in data centers have to be taken into account when considering the overall temperature of the data center. C

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ubuntu新团队Debcrafters及其对Debian和Ubuntu的影响

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为Debcrafters的成立不应影响Debian的开发和维护，担心Ubuntu会从Debian的努力中获得不成比例的利益，并可能导致Debian的二次包装问题。同时，neilv表示个人仍偏好使用Debian Stable，因为其在生产使用中表现更好。
• [jnsgruk] 介绍了Debcrafters团队的目标和结构，强调团队将吸引来自不同Linux发行版的贡献者，并鼓励团队成员每周花一天时间为其他发行版做贡献，以促进学习和想法分享。
• [notpushkin] 对debcraft和Debian已有的debcraft项目之间的关系提出疑问，质疑两者是否相同。
• [AdmiralAsshat] 以幽默的方式质疑Starcraft团队是否真的在玩游戏，而不是专注于开发工作。
• [tonymet] 关注品牌问题，认为Debcrafters的名称容易让人联想到Debian，并质疑Ubuntu的质量不如Debian，同时提到Debian品牌作为质量信号的重要性。
• [alexktz] 对Jon加入Ubuntu项目表示欢迎，认为其带来了新的活力。
• [thesuperbigfrog] 提出关于Debian中未维护软件包的弃用过程的问题，询问如何确定一个包是否应由Debcrafters或其他人员维护，以及如何衡量软件包的使用情况和优先级。
• [nullbyte] 提到一个技术问题，指出Ubuntu官方网页上的500服务器错误影响不好。

补充讨论：
• Debcrafters团队的成立及其对Debian和Ubuntu之间关系的影响是主要讨论焦点，特别是在品牌和资源分配上的潜在冲突。
• 讨论中还涉及Debian和Ubuntu在软件包维护和弃用过程中的具体操作问题，反映了社区对透明度和优先级设定的关注。
• 一些评论带有幽默和个人偏好，如AdmiralAsshat和neilv的评论，但也包含了对实际问题的关切。

• ceejayoz不同意关于“最大欺诈”的说法，指出Rick Scott担任公司高管时其公司曾涉及更大规模的Medicare欺诈，并引用了美国司法部的数据，说明Rick Scott的公司被罚款17亿美元，且该案件在当时是美国历史上最大的医疗欺诈和解案。

• zzzeek的观点带有政治色彩，认为在拜登政府期间发现的浪费、欺诈和滥用行为远超过之前的事件，并批评联邦调查局和司法部等机构被右翼媒体控制，暗示这些机构在处理欺诈问题上可能存在偏见。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于谁应该为“最大Medicare欺诈”负责。Refreeze5224和ceejayoz都提到了Rick Scott，但ceejayoz更具体地引用了法律数据来支持他的观点。zzzeek则将讨论引向政治层面，认为当前政府的处理和媒体报道存在问题。

• 论据和例子：ceejayoz提供了具体的法律判决和罚款数据来支持Rick Scott涉及大规模欺诈的说法，而zzzeek则依赖于对当前政府和机构的批评，但没有提供具体的法律或财务数据。

• 讨论之间的关系：Refreeze5224引发了关于Rick Scott的讨论，而ceejayoz通过引用具体数据进一步证实了Rick Scott的案件规模，zzzeek则将讨论引向政治批判。

data.title: Helix: A Modern, High-Performance Language
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: Helix是一门现代高性能编程语言，结合了Python的简洁和C++的强大，旨在提供高性能和内存安全。它采用高级内存跟踪系统（AMT）以确保内存安全，同时比Rust等语言更灵活。Helix具备跨平台标准库，支持与C++无缝互操作，适合系统编程、游戏开发和人工智能等领域。其设计哲学强调现代语法和易用性，适合初学者，同时也为有经验的开发者提供底层控制。Helix的错误报告系统直观且有帮助，提供清晰的错误信息和可操作的建议。目前，Helix正在开发自举编译器，并已开始支持泛型和继承等高级特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕编程语言Helix的特性、设计选择及未来前景的讨论。

不同观点：
• [munificent] 对Helix的"Questionable Types"机制表示困惑，认为其行为与Java中的null处理类似，质疑其新颖性。
• [hannofcart] 赞赏Helix默认非空类型的设计和错误处理机制，认为这是评估新语言的重要标准，并对借用检查器（borrow checker）的实现充满期待，认为如果Helix能兑现其承诺，将会是非常理想的编程语言。
• [snovymgodym] 认为Helix的高级内存追踪是一个亮点，但对其实际应用前景持怀疑态度。指出类似C++的改进语言（如D, Zig等）普遍缺乏广泛采用，原因是切换成本高且收益有限。例外的是Rust，因其保证内存安全的特性获得更多支持。
• [skulk] 关注Helix对语言服务器协议（LSP）的重视，认为这是语言开发工具支持的一大进步。
• [corank] 对高级内存追踪（AMT）在具体数据结构如双向链表中的实现表示关注，担心运行时的性能开销。
• [rich_sasha] 对Helix的性能、借用检查器的友好性及可读性表示赞赏，但对其开发团队和支持力量表示关注，认为成功的编程语言通常需要强大的后盾。

补充讨论：
• [johnisgood] 关注Helix在Linux平台上的兼容性问题，认为需要更多测试和反馈。
• [44za12] 批评Helix在文档未完成的情况下就宣布发布，认为这不够严谨。
• [JadeNB] 指出Helix与已有的Helix编辑器名称冲突，建议在文档中添加免责声明以避免混淆。
• [90s_dev] 对Helix宣称结合Rust和Zig的优点表示怀疑，特别是其C/C++ ABI兼容性和无运行时的特性，认为可能过于理想化。
• [devjab] 对Helix缺乏OOP支持表示不同意见，认为这是Rust和Zig的一大优势。
• [dupdrop] 对Helix的语法设计（如条件表达式语法）表示不满，但表示会进一步了解语言的其他方面。

争议焦点：
• Helix的"Questionable Types"机制是否真正新颖，以及与Java的null处理行为的比较。
• Helix能否在众多类似语言中脱颖而出，获得广泛采用。
• Helix的语法设计选择是否合理。
